source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Services by skilled professionals
CFR(s): 484.75(a)
Standard: Provision of services by skilled professionals.  

Skilled professional services are authorized, delivered, and supervised only by health care professionals who meet the appropriate qualifications specified under §484.115 and who practice according to the HHA's policies and procedures.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:

Based on one (1) of two (2) home visit observations, staff interview, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that its policy for handwashing is implemented. 

Findings include: 

Reference: Facility policy titled, "Hand Hygiene Policy and Compliance Program" states, "Purpose: To prevent transfer of germs and transmission of infections to patients and caregivers... . Procedure: ... II. Hand hygiene technique (non-surgical) ... B. Hand washing with soap and water... (IB) Wash for 20 seconds."

1. On 12/9/2021 at 1:50 PM, a home visit was conducted to observe the care of Patient #3. At 2:20 PM, Staff #5 washed his/her hands for fifteen (15) seconds.

b. Hand hygiene was not performed in accordance with facility policy and procedure. 

2. The above findings were reviewed with Staff #1.

source_record.Facility Name: Visiting Nurse Association of Northern New Jersey, Inc.
source_record.Deficiency Description: Plan Of Care Must Include The Following
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Plan of care must include the following
CFR(s): 484.60(a)(2)(i-xvi)
The individualized plan of care must include the following:

(i) All pertinent diagnoses;

(ii) The patient's mental, psychosocial, and cognitive status;

(iii) The types of services, supplies, and equipment required;

(iv) The frequency and duration of visits to be made;

(v) Prognosis;

(vi) Rehabilitation potential;

(vii) Functional limitations;

(viii) Activities permitted;

(ix) Nutritional requirements;

(x) All medications and treatments;

(xi) Safety measures to protect against injury;

(xii) A description of the patient's risk for emergency department visits and hospital re-admission, and all necessary interventions to address the underlying risk factors.

(xiii) Patient and caregiver education and training to facilitate timely discharge;

(xiv) Patient-specific interventions and education; measurable outcomes and goals identified by the HHA and the patient;

(xv) Information related to any advanced directives; and

(xvi) Any additional items the HHA or physician may choose to include.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on staff interviews, review of facility policies and procedures, and review of one (1) of two (2) medical records, it was determined the facility failed to ensure discharge planning is included in the patient's individualized plan of care.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, Discharge Criteria, states, " ... The patient is informed of discharge plan in a timely manner and acknowledges understanding reason. ... Discharge planning begins at time of admission and will be reflected in the documentation. ... The patient's continuing care needs, if any, are assessed at discharge. ... A complete list of reconciled medications will be provided to each patient on discharge. The list will be explained to the patient/family and interaction documented. ..."

1. Upon review of Medical Record #2, the following was noted:

a. According to the Visit Note Report dated 10/8/20, Patient #1's last agency visit was 10/8/20. The visit was performed by a Registered Nurse (RN). The visit type was an RN Subsequent visit.

b. According to the Visit Note Report dated 10/31/20, the Visit Type was RN Discharge Data Collection Only - No Visit Made.

i. The Narrative states, "Discharge Patient from Agency. Mrs. [name of family member] ... disappointed that services have ended."

c. There was no documented evidence that discharge planning was provided to the patient or family while the patient was receiving agency services.

d. There was no documented evidence that the patient was informed of a discharge plan in a timely manner and acknowledged understanding of the reason. 

e. There was no documented evidence the patient's continuing care needs were assessed at discharge.

f. There was no documented evidence that a complete list of reconciled medications was provided to the patient on discharge or that the list was explained to the patient or family.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2 and Staff #4.

Reference #2: Facility policy, Discharge Summary, states, "A Discharge Summary form will be completed by the Skilled Nurse or Therapist. The Discharge Summary will include, but is not limited to: ... Reason for Discharge ... Patient/Family post-discharge instructions ... The original Discharge Summary form from each service will be filed in the medical record."

1. Review of the Discharge-Transfer Summary Report for Patient #1, revealed the following:

a. The Discharge-Transfer Summary Report was sent to the physician on 10/13/20.

b. The reason for discharge says "Other (Please provide details in Coordination Note)."

i. No Coordination Note was provided.

ii. The reason for discharge was not documented in the discharge summary.

c. The Patient/Family post-discharge instructions were not included in the discharge summary.

d. The original Discharge Summary form from each service was not filed in the medical record.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2 and Staff #4.

B. Based on staff interviews and review of medical records, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure for (1) one of (2) two medical records the care plan is implemented. 

Findings include: 

1. On 2/10/2021, at 11:30 AM, upon review of Medical Record #3, the following was indicated: 

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care was reviewed for the Certification Period 12/4/2020 to 2/1/2021 states, " ... Orders of Discipline and Treatments: ... Skilled Nurse to provide and instruct regarding fall prevention interventions. ... ."

b. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care reviewed for the Certification Period 2/2/2021 to 4/2/2021, states, " ... Orders of Discipline and Treatments: ... Skilled Nurse to perform multifactor fall risk assessment and implement intervention to decrease risk of falls. Skilled Nurse to instruct on home safety, impact of polypharmacy, environmental safety, and fall prevention. ... ." 

2. Staff interviews indicated the following: 

a. On 2/10/2021 at 11:30 AM, Staff #3 was asked where the fall assessments and interventions could be viewed in the medical record. 

b. At 11:45 AM, Staff #3 telephoned Staff #8 to confirm where the Nursing Fall Assessments and Interventions are documented. 

i. Staff #8 stated that the Nursing Fall Assessments and Interventions would be documented in the Narrative Note section of the Assessment. 

3. There were no Fall Assessments nor Interventions documented in the Narrative Note, by the Nurse, on the following dates of the Skilled Nursing Visits:

a. January 14, 2021

b. January 19, 2021

c. February 2, 2021

4. Staff #3 had the opportunity to read the record and was not able to find the fall assessments nor interventions.

5. The above was confirmed by Staff #3 and shared with Staff #1, Staff #2, and Staff #4 during the exit conference.

source_record.Facility Name: Visiting Nurse Association of Northern New Jersey, Inc.
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Integrate all services
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(3)
Integrate services, whether services are provided directly or under arrangement, to assure the identification of patient needs and factors that could affect patient safety and treatment effectiveness and the coordination of care provided by all disciplines.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interviews, medical record reviews, and review of facility documents, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that, for (1) one of (2) two medical records following a patient fall, Skilled Nursing Reassessments are completed.

Findings include: 

Reference #1: The Facility Policy titled, "Fall Reduction Program", states, " ... Purpose: To reduce the risk of patient harm resulting from falls. ... Procedure: ... 2. Reassessment for fall risk will be performed when a patient experiences a fall ... . ... ."

1. On 2/10/2021 at 12:30 PM, upon review of Medical Record #7, the following was indicated:

a. The Occupational Therapist visit note, dated 2/5/2021 states," ... Therapy Assessment/Plan: ... Patient reports slid off stand assist chair prior evening. ... . No injury but needed to call police to raise off floor. ... . Care Coordination: ... What Discipline did you communicate with: Supervisor, PT [Physical Therapy], RN [Registered Nurse]. ... ."

i. There was no evidence in the medical record that a follow-up visit was made for a post fall reassessment by a Nurse. 

b. On 2/10/2021 at 1:00 PM, Staff #3 stated that the Occupational Therapist and/or Supervisor should have entered a request for an order for the Nurse Reassessment visit. 

2. The above was confirmed by Staff #3, and shared with Staff #1, Staff #2, and Staff #4 during the exit conference.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Provide services in the plan of care
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(3)
Providing services that are ordered by the physician as indicated in the plan of care;

Based on staff interviews and review of one (1) of two (2) medical records, it was determined the agency failed to ensure that services are provided as ordered by the physician and indicated in the plan of care.

Findings include:

1. Upon review of Medical Record #1, the following was noted:

a. Patient #1's start of care date was 12/14/20.

b. The Physician orders for skilled nursing are as follows: two times a week for one week, one time a week for 4 weeks, one every two weeks for four weeks, two PRN (as needed) IV (Intravenous), and one PRN status.

c. There was a missed skilled nursing visit the week of 12/27/20 to 1/2/21.

2. The above finding was confirmed with Staff #2 and Staff #4.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Organization and administration of services
CFR(s): 484.105
Condition of participation: Organization and administration of services.

The HHA must organize, manage, and administer its resources to attain and maintain the highest practicable functional capacity, including providing optimal care to achieve the goals and outcomes identified in the patient's plan of care, for each patient's medical, nursing, and rehabilitative needs. The HHA must assure that administrative and supervisory functions are not delegated to another agency or organization, and all services not furnished directly are monitored and controlled. The HHA must set forth, in writing, its organizational structure, including lines of authority, and services furnished.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure a Governing Body was established to oversee the Home Health Agency. 

 

§484.105(a): Governing Body
§484.105(b)(1): Administrator
§484.105(b)(2): Alternate Administrator
§484.105(e)(2): Written Agreement

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Accessibility
CFR(s): 484.50(f)(1,2)
Standard: Accessibility.  Information must be provided to patients in plain language and in a manner that is accessible and timely to— 
(1) Persons with disabilities, including accessible web sites and the provision of auxiliary aids and services at no cost to the individual in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. 
(2) Persons with limited English proficiency through the provision of language services at no cost to the individual, including oral interpretation and written translations.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on facility policy, staff interview, observation, and medical record review, it was determined the facility failed to ensure patients with limited English proficiency are provided a translator in their preferred language (Patient (P6)). 

On 12/10/25 at 12:31 PM, Staff (S)13 was observed providing care to Patient (P)6. P6’s family member was present during the visit and identified him/herself as P6’s primary caregiver. 

At 12:36 PM, while S13 provided care and education to P6, it was observed P6 had a limited understanding of English. S13 spoke to P6 in English and P6 would respond in a mix of Spanish and English. S13 was observed conducting P6’s medication reconciliation and education on medications in English accompanied with limited Spanish. 

At 12:45 PM, conducted a comprehensive assessment of P6. Throughout the assessment surveyors observed P6’s family member providing English to Spanish translation for questions that involved complex vocabulary.

At 1:25 PM, S13 was observed providing diabetes education to P6. While providing the education, P6’s family member stated, “[he/she] won’t understand you, I’ll tell [him/her] what you’re saying.” S13 was agreeable and continued educating P6 in English.

Surveyors did not observe S13 ask P6 during the visit if P6’s family member was an acceptable option for interpretation from English to Spanish. 

A review of P6’s medical record was conducted and revealed the following:

On 11/19/25, P6’s admission visit and initial assessment were conducted by S13. In the “Assessment” section of the Visit Note Report, S13 documented P6’s response to the question, “What is your preferred language?” as “Spanish”. S13 documented P6’s response to the question, “Do you need or want an interpreter to communicate with a doctor or health care staff?” as “Yes”.

On 11/26/25 at 6:28 PM, an In-Home Visit Note Report was documented by a physical therapist that stated, “… Patient is … Spanish speaking …"

On 12/10/25 at 11:46 PM, an In-Home Visit Note Report written by S13 stated, “…Educationm [sic] was done with son present and explaining to patient in Spanish …”
P6’s medical record lacked evidence that P6 requested to use his/her family member as an interpreter. P6’s medical record lacked evidence that an agency-provided language interpreter was offered to P6.

On 12/11/25 at 12:53 PM, an interview was conducted with S1 and S9. When asked how a situation with a patient who has limited English proficiency should be handled, S1 stated, staff should utilize the interpreter application found on the facility provided tablet. S1 stated, staff are able to open the application and choose which language is needed for interpretation services. When asked what occurs if a patient requests to utilize a family member as their interpreter, S9 stated, “we try not to use family and encourage an interpreter.”  

At 2:30 PM, S1 confirmed that a Limited English Proficiency (LEP) patient should be offered the option of having an interpreter during his/her visit. S1 stated, if the patient requests to have his/her family member as an interpreter, the staff member must document the request in the patient's medical record.

Facility policy titled, “Limited English Proficiency Persons (LEP)” (revised 07/01/24) stated, “…Policy … The agency will take reasonable steps to ensure that persons with Limited English Proficiency (LEP) have meaningful access and an equal opportunity to participate in our services, activities, programs, and other benefits … All interpreters, translators, and other aids needed to comply with this policy shall be provided without cost to the person being served, and patients/clients and their families will be informed of the availability of such assistance free of charge … Language assistance will be provided through use of competent bilingual staff, staff interpreters, contact or formal arrangements with organizations providing interpretation or translation services, or technology and telephonic interpretation services … Procedure … 5. Family and friends may not be used to interpret or translate unless client/LEP person is made aware of the availability of interpreters … When a family member or friend is specifically requested by the patient to provide language interpretation, the agency will encourage the addition of an agency-provided language interpreter to be available to the family/patient … Such an offer and the response will be documented in the patient’s medical record.”

On 12/11/25 at 12:53 PM, an interview was conducted with S1 and S9. When asked how a situation with a patient who has limited English proficiency should be handled, S1 stated staff should utilize the interpreter application found on the facility provided tablet. S1 stated staff are able to open the application and choose which language is needed for interpretation services. When asked what occurs if a patient requests to utilize a family member as their interpreter, S9 stated, “we try not to use family and encourage an interpreter.”  

On 12/11/25 at 2:00 PM, P6’s medical record was reviewed and revealed the following:

On 11/19/25, during P6’s initial assessment and admission to the facility, an assessment note by a Registered Nurse (RN) was documented and stated:
“What is your preferred language? Spanish 
Do you need or want an interpreter to communicate with a doctor or health care staff? 1. Yes …”

On 11/26/25 at 6:28 PM, an In-Home Visit Note Report was documented by a physical therapist that stated, “… Patient is … Spanish speaking …"

While S13 provided care and education to P6, it was observed P6 had a limited understanding of English and that P6’s son/daughter was providing translation to Spanish throughout the visit. source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interview, and review of facility policies, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that facility policies to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases, related to cleaning of equipment, hand hygiene, and bag protocol, in four of seven home visits (Patient (P)1, P2, P3, and P7) are adhered to by all staff. 

Facility policy titled “Hand Hygiene”, dated 09/05/25, stated, “… Procedure: 1. Staff performs hand hygiene by hand washing with soap and water or an alcohol-based hand sanitizer …”

Facility policy titled "Bag Protocol Policy," dated 11/25/25, stated, "… Procedure … Infection Control Practices C. Perform hand hygiene before removing or returning supplies to the bag … G. Prior to returning equipment to the home care bag, equipment must be cleaned using gloves with the appropriate disinfectant (refer to Policy 8.006 – Cleaning of Re-Usable Equipment) …" 

On 12/09/25 at 1:05 PM, S3 was observed providing care for P3.

At 1:07 PM, placed his/her tablet on a barrier pad on the living room table with his/her nursing bag.

At 1:14 PM, P3’s family member picked up the tablet while searching for medications on the table.

At 1:19 PM, S3 used scissors to remove dressings for the wound on P3’s left foot.

At 1:21 PM, S3 placed the contaminated scissors next to the tablet on the barrier pad.

At 1:42 PM, S3 began assessing P3’s vital signs.

At 1:45 PM, S3 placed the contaminated vital signs equipment (blood pressure cuff, sphygmomanometer, stethoscope, pulse oximeter, thermometer) on top of the tablet on the barrier pad.

At 1:52 PM, S3 cleaned the vital signs equipment with alcohol wipes and placed the equipment in his/her nursing bag. S3 did not clean the tablet.

At 1:57 PM, S3 discarded the barrier pads and placed the contaminated tablet on P3’s table.

At 2:05 PM, S3 exited P3’s home carrying the contaminated tablet in his/her hands.

At 2:10 PM, an interview was conducted with S3. When questioned about the process for cleaning the tablet, S3 stated, he/she forgot to clean the tablet. S3 stated, the tablet should be cleaned after each patient visit.

 

On 12/11/25 at 10:00 AM, S7 was observed providing care for P7.

At 10:06 AM, S7 donned gloves and began assessing P7’s vital signs.

At 10:10 AM, S7 completed vital signs.

At 10:13 AM, S7 began conducting patient education on discharge with same gloves on from vital signs assessment.

At 10:21 AM, S7 completed patient education and began conducting physical therapy exercises with P7 in his/her kitchen with same gloves on from vital signs assessment.

At 10:29 AM, S7 doffed gloves and entered the central compartment of his/her nursing bag without hand sanitizing. 

At 10:41 AM, an interview was conducted with S7. When questioned about the facility policy for bag technique, S7 stated, staff must doff gloves and hand sanitize before entering the nursing bag. S7 confirmed that he/she did not hand sanitize prior to entering the bag at 10:29 AM.

At 12:40 PM, an interview was conducted with S1 and S9. When questioned about bag technique, S1 stated, staff are taught to hand sanitize prior to accessing the bag and after every glove change.

Findings include:

Facility policy titled "Cleaning of Re-Useable Equipment," dated 06/01/25, stated, "… Definitions: 1. Low-Level Disinfection … Examples include at least 70% isopropyl alcohol/ethyl alcohol … 3. Non-Critical Items – Equipment that is only meant to come in contact with intact patient skin … (e.g., stethoscope, blood pressure cuffs, pulse-oximeters … tablet) … Non-critical items also include … (e.g., staff bags,) … Procedure: 1. Non-critical items which will come in contact with intact patient skin will undergo a low-level disinfection between each patient use … 7. … tablet … should be wiped down with a low-level disinfectant at the … end of each visit …" 

On 12/09/25 at 1:17 PM, Staff (S)4 was observed providing care for P1.

At 1:18 PM, S4 was observed setting up two barrier pads. S4 placed his/her bag on a barrier pad and removed a sphygmomanometer (blood pressure cuff), stethoscope, thermometer, and pulse oximeter from his/her bag placing them on the same barrier pad next to the bag. The second barrier pad remained empty. 

At 1:21 PM, P1 was observed touching both barrier pads with bare hands while searching for his/her admission packet, contaminating both barrier pads. 

At 1:22 PM, S4 took P1’s blood pressure and heart rate and then placed the contaminated equipment (sphygmomanometer, pulse oximeter, and stethoscope) on the empty barrier pad.

At 1:27 PM, S4 took P1’s temporal (forehead) temperature and then placed the contaminated thermometer on the barrier pad with the sphygmomanometer, pulse oximeter, and stethoscope.

At 1:37 PM, S4 cleaned the contaminated vital signs equipment (thermometer, pulse oximeter, sphygmomanometer, and stethoscope) with a disposable alcohol wipe and then placed the equipment back on the previously contaminated barrier pad next to his/her bag, re-contaminating the vital signs equipment.

At 1:44 PM, P1 was observed touching the vital signs equipment and S4’s bag with bare hands while searching for his/her medication list, further contaminating the vital signs equipment and contaminating S4’s bag. 

At 1:45 PM, S4 placed the contaminated vital signs equipment back in his/her bag.

At 2:00 PM, S4 was observed exiting P1’s home without re-cleaning the contaminated vital signs equipment and cleaning the contaminated bag.

At 2:04 PM, an interview was conducted with S4. While reviewing the home visit, S4 confirmed the findings.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Must have a written agreement
CFR(s): 484.105(e)(2)(i-iv)
An HHA must have a written agreement with another agency, with an organization, or with an individual when that entity or individual furnishes services under arrangement to the HHA's patients.  The HHA must maintain overall responsibility for the services provided under arrangement, as well as the manner in which they are furnished. The agency, organization, or individual providing services under arrangement may not have been:

(i) Denied Medicare or Medicaid enrollment;

(ii) Been excluded or terminated from any federal health care program or Medicaid;

(iii) Had its Medicare or Medicaid billing privileges revoked; or

(iv) Been debarred from participating in any government program.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure written agreements for social work services, that were provided to the home health agency's patients, by another home health agency.

Findings include:

On 12/09/25 at 9:51 AM, during entrance conference, Staff (S) 1 reported that the facility currently does not have social workers at this branch to provide services to the patients. 

At 10:15 AM, S1 reported that the parent company has eight branches, and if necessary, staff, social workers, can be borrowed from one of the other branches. When asked if any of these branches share the same license number with this facility, S1 reported that there are no other branches under their license. S1 reported that there are two social workers who cover patients at different branches. 

On 12/11/25 at 1:07 PM, S1 was asked to provide written agreements or contracts with other agencies/branches for use of their HHA or SW staff.

On 12/12/25 at 10:32 AM, Staff (S)1 presented a document to surveyors titled “Shared Employee Form” for S15 and S16, the two social workers the facility uses from a separately licensed facility. The form for S15 stated “Effective Date: 04/20/25”. The form for S16 stated “Effective Date: 08/25/24”. The forms were only signed by the social worker and their supervisor at the other facility. 

At 4:00 PM, S1 presented a document to surveyors titled “Shared Employee Form” for S17, a home health aide the facility uses from a separately licensed facility. The form for S16 stated “Effective Date: 04/20/25”. The form was only signed by the home health aide and their supervisor at the other facility.

S1 confirmed that the Shared Employee Forms were not signed by a representative from their agency, did not specify each party’s responsibilities, functions, and objectives, and did not contain a time during which the services were to be provided or the duration of the agreement.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Plan of care
CFR(s): 484.60(a)(1)
Each patient must receive the home health services that are written in an individualized plan of care that identifies patient-specific measurable outcomes and goals, and which is established, periodically reviewed, and signed by a doctor of medicine, osteopathy, or podiatry acting within the scope of his or her state license, certification, or registration. If a physician or allowed practitioner refers a patient under a plan of care that cannot be completed until after an evaluation visit, the physician or allowed practitioner is consulted to approve additions or modifications to the original plan.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on a review of one (1) of one (1) medical record (#1), staff interview, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure patient-specific plan of care goals and interventions, based on patients' medical diagnosis, physician orders, comprehensive assessment, and patient input. 

Findings include: 

 

Reference: Facility policy titled, "Plan of care (POC)" states, "Policy: Each patient has an individualized Plan of Care (POC) developed in consultation with the patient, physician or authorized practitioner, and staff that integrates comprehensive assessment findings to address patient problems, needs, and goals, as well as to address specific services being provided. PROCEDURE: ... 2. The POC includes: … e. Nutritional requirements … i. Patient specific interventions and education; measurable outcomes and goals identified by the agency and patient … l. Patient/caregiver education and training for timely discharge. … 9. The patient is monitored for response to treatment and progress towards goals. …”

 

1. Review of Medical Record #1 conducted on 3/15/22 at 12:43 PM, for the start of care date 1/19/2022, revealed the patient’s diagnoses included, but are not limited to, acute systolic heart failure, type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes with diabetic peripheral angiopathy without gangrene, peripheral vascular disease, and NSTEMI. 

 

a. Review of the patient’s plan of care for a nursing visit dated 1/20/22, failed to include goals and interventions specific to diabetes related issues such as medication, nutrition, patient/caregiver education. 

 

b. Review of nursing documentation dated 2/9/22 revealed Staff #6 identified bilateral heel pressure wounds. Upon review of the plan of care, Staff #6 failed to include goals and interventions concerning wound care, nutrition, and patient/caregiver education. 

 

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2.

Findings include: 

1. On 3/15/22, upon review of Medical Record #1, the Home Health Certification and Plan of Care indicated the patient’s diagnoses included, but were not limited to, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus w/ Diabetic Chronic Kidney disease, Type 2 Diabetes with Diabetic Peripheral Angiopathy w/o gangrene, etc. Upon review of the nursing assessments, the following was revealed: 

a. On 1/20/22, under ENDOCRINE, for the question "Does the patient have diabetes?", Staff #5 indicated "No." 

b. On 1/26/22, Staff #6’s nursing assessment indicated the patient is diabetic and follow-up assessment questions were addressed to include assessment of lower extremities and diabetic foot care. 

c. On 2/14/22, Staff #5’s nursing assessment, under ENDOCRINE, did not identify the patient as diabetic and indicated the following:

(i) "Does the patient have diabetes?" "No." 

(ii) A review of the wound assessment documentation stated, "#1 Post – Heel RT DIAB ULCER LTD SKIN BKDWN - Change in Status – None, Wound  Assessed – No, caregiver completed care … #2 – POST – HEEL LT. DIAB ULCER UNSP SEVERITY – Change in Status – None, Wound Assessed – No, client completed care, Wound Care Provided – Wound care not provided caregiver completed care."

This includes:... c. Appropriate, timely communication with the patient, caregivers, and staff involved in the patient's care regarding patient needs, goals, and care as well as changes in these.... significant changes in the patient condition... ."

 

1. On 3/15/22, during a review of Medical Record #1, it was revealed that on 2/7/22, Staff #7 (Physical Therapist) documented under INTEGUMENTARY ASSESSMENT, “Patient has bandages on bilateral feet which were just applied and he/she asked they not be removed.” 

a. Under CARE COORDINATION notes, Staff #7 documented that care coordination occurred with “supervisor” and indicated, “RN to eval B/L [bilateral] heel wounds."

b. There was no evidence that Staff #7, or the supervisor, reported this finding to the nurse in charge of the case.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
HHA Comprehensive Assessment in Disaster
CFR(s): 484.102(b)(1)
§484.102(b)(1) Condition for Participation:

[(b) Policies and procedures.  The HHA must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 

At a minimum, the policies and procedures must address the following:]



(1) The plans for the HHA's patients during a natural or man-made disaster. Individual plans for each patient must be included as part of the comprehensive patient assessment, which must be conducted according to the provisions at §484.55.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of three (3) of three (3) medical records (#2, #6,and #10), review of facility documents, and staff interviews, it was determined that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to ensure that all patient's receive an individualized emergency plan as part of their comprehensive assessment.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy titled "Emergency Preparedness/Operations Plan"states, "Policy ... A patient triage list will be maintained and updated ongoing. ... 1. Patients are evaluated according to their care/transport/evacuation needs using the Emergency Preparedness/ On Call Plan. 2. The agency maintains a triage list of patients grouped according to these needs. The list included patients requiring outside assistance and/or transportation to evacuate if needed. 6. Staff a. Staff shall assist in maintaining up to date triage board and/or list. ... Preparation For Emergencies And Disasters: (Preparation) General ...4. The agency shall instruct patients and caregivers on the emergency plan upon admission. ..."

1. Upon review of the "Patient Disaster Plan ID Form" for Patient #2 on 2/18/20, the following was revealed:

a. The facility identified the Evacuation Destination as the patients home. 

b. Upon interview on 2/18/20 at 1:30 PM, Staff #1 confirmed that the patients home should not have been an evacuation location. 

2. Upon review of the "Patient Disaster Plan ID Form" for Patient #6 on 2/18/20, the following was revealed:

a. The facility failed to identify an Evacuation Destination and Evacuation Address, these were left blank.

b. Upon interview on 2/18/20 at 1:30 PM, Staff #1 confirmed the above information. 

3. Upon review of the "Patient Disaster Plan ID Form" for Patient #10 on 2/18/20, the following was revealed:

a. The facility failed to identify an Evacuation Destination and Evacuation Address, these were left blank.

b. Upon interview on 2/18/20 at 1:30 PM, Staff #1 confirmed the above information.

CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on observation, document review, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the hand hygiene policy is implemented.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Hand Hygiene" states, "... Procedure: 1. Staff performs hand hygiene by handwashing with soap and water or using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer: ... f. before and after removal of personal protective equipment (PPE)."

1. During a home visit of Patient #2 on 2/18/20 at 12:35 PM, the following was observed:

a. After performing a physical assessment, Staff #3 removed his/her gloves, and failed to sanitize his/her hands prior to putting on new gloves.2. During a home visit of Patient #5 on 2/19/20 at 10:38 AM, the following was observed:

a. While performing a physical assessment,Staff #9 removed his/her gloves, and failed to sanitize his/her hands prior to putting on new gloves.

3. The above was confirmed by Staff #2 at 11:00 AM.

B. Based on observation, review of facility documents and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that infection prevention policies are adhered to. 

Findings include: 

Reference: Facility policy,"Cleaning of Re-useable Equipment" states, "Definitions: 1. Low-Level Disinfection-...Examples include 70% isopropyl alcohol. 2. Intermediate-Level Disinfection-...Examples include Sani Cloth Plus and bleach wipes. 3. Non-Critical Items...should be cleaned for use by undergoing low-level disinfection (e.g.,... blood pressure cuffs....) ...9. Blood pressure cuffs are cleaned with a low-level disinfectant wipe after each use and before being returned to staff bags." 

1. During a home visit of Patient #1 on 2/18/20 at 11:25 AM, the following was observed:

CFR(s): 484.60(b)
Standard: Conformance with physician or allowed practitioner orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interviews, and review of five of 14 medical records (#3, #4, #5, #6, #13), it was determined that the agency failed to ensure: 1) physician orders indicated on the patient's plan of care, are implemented; 2) services ordered by the physician are provided as indicated in the plan of care.

Findings include:

On 1/26/23 at 11:30 AM, during medical record review, the following was revealed:

Upon review of the "Home Health Certification and Plan of Care" for Patient (P) 5, dated 1/26/2023 to 1/23/2023, the following was noted:"Frequency/Duration of Visits" states "SN (skilled nursing) 2wk8 (two times a week for eight weeks)."The week of 12/25/22, the patient had one skilled nursing visit.

The week of 1/1/23, the patient had one skilled nursing visit.Upon review of the Home Health Certification and Plan of Care for P13, dated 6/4/2022 to 8/2/2022, the following was noted:"Frequency/Duration of Visits" states "SN 1wk1 (one time a week for one week),  2wk3 (two times a week for three weeks), 1wk6 (one time a week for six weeks)."The week of 6/5/22, week two of the certification period, the patient had one skilled nursing visit.

On 1/27/23 at 12:35 PM, the above findings were confirmed with Staff #1.

 

On 1/27/23 at 1:00 PM, during medical record review, the following was revealed:

Upon review of the "Home Health Certification and Plan of Care" for Patient (P) 6, dated 12/7/2022 through 2/4/2023, the following was noted:

The indicated orders for physical therapy visits were: "1WK2 [one visit each week for two week], 2WK5 [two visits each week for five weeks], 1WK1 [one visit each week for one week.] and revised on 1/15/23 to 3WK1 [three visits each week for one week], 1WK1 [one visit each week for one week].”

The week of 1/15/23, P6 had physical therapy visits on 1/17/23 and 1/20/23. P6’s medical record lacked evidence of a third physical therapy visit for the week of 1/15/23.

On 1/27/23 at 1:35 PM, Staff #11 stated “we are unable to reconcile that missed visit.”

Based on observation, staff interview, review of two of three medical records (#3, #4) for the patient's individualized plan of care, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that physician orders indicated on the patient's plan of care, are implemented.

Findings include:

Review of the plan of care for Patient #3 (P3) on 01/26/23, for certification period 01/13/23 to 03/13/23, revealed the following:

The section labeled, "Orders of Discipline and Treatments" states, " ... Therapist to assess lower extremities for presence of lesions on every visit. ... When vital signs are obtained licensed professional to report vital signs falling outside the following established parameters ... Temp100.5 (temperature less than 96.5 degrees Fahrenheit and greater than 100.5 degrees Fahrenheit)." 

During a home visit for P3 on 01/26/23, in the presence of Staff #4 (Patient Care Manager), Staff #8 did not assess the patient's lower extremities for the presence of lesions. Staff #8 did not assess the patient's temperature to determine if it was less than 96.5 degrees Fahrenheit or greater than 100.5 degrees Fahrenheit. 

Review of the plan of care for Patient #4 (P4) on 01/26/23, for certification period 12/23/22 to 02/20/23, revealed the following:

The section labeled, "Orders of Discipline and Treatments" states, " ... When vital signs are obtained licensed professional to report vital signs falling outside the following established parameters ... Temp100.5 (temperature less than 96.5 degrees Fahrenheit and greater than 100.5 degrees Fahrenheit)." 

During a home visit for P4 on 01/26/23, in the presence of Staff #4, Staff #9 did not assess the patient's temperature to determine if it was less than 96.5 degrees Fahrenheit or greater than 100.5 degrees Fahrenheit. 

Upon interview on 01/27/23 at 12:45 PM, Staff #1 confirmed that physical therapists are licensed professionals and therefore, required to report temperatures outside of established parameters, as indicated in the patient's plan of care.

N.J.A.C. 8:42-6.2(a)(6)

source_record.Deficiency Description: Initial Comments - Not A Deficiency Citation
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This was a Federal Recertification and State Re-licensure survey conducted at Valley Home Care on 4/16-4/18/2024, to determine compliance with 42 CFR Part 484 - Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies; and State requirements under Title 8, Chapter 42 - Home Health Agency Licensing Standards. Standard-level deficiencies were cited.

Plan of care
CFR(s): 484.60(a)(1)
Each patient must receive the home health services that are written in an individualized plan of care that identifies patient-specific measurable outcomes and goals, and which is established, periodically reviewed, and signed by a doctor of medicine, osteopathy, or podiatry acting within the scope of his or her state license, certification, or registration. If a physician or allowed practitioner refers a patient under a plan of care that cannot be completed until after an evaluation visit, the physician or allowed practitioner is consulted to approve additions or modifications to the original plan.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, medical record review, staff interview, and review of policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure: 1) patient pain is assessed in accordance with physician orders and facility policy; and 2) patient medications are reviewed in accordance with physician orders and facility policy. 

Findings include:

1.) Facility policy "Pain Assessment, Reassessment, and Symptom Management," approved 4/22, states, "... Procedure: I. Assessment: … B. Each patient receiving skilled services will have a comprehensive pain assessment initially and on an ongoing basis using established criteria, including: 1. Location 2. Intensity 3. Duration 4. Frequency 5. Character (e.g., throbbing, aching, sharp, etc.) 6. Current pain therapy or treatment 7. Effectiveness of current therapy or treatment … D. The patient's assessment of the pain is conducted by using a standardized and validated tool appropriate for age and developmental status. … " 

On 4/16/24 at 12:42 PM, during a home visit of Patient (P) 1, Staff (S)12, a Registered Nurse, was observed performing P1's wound care. S12 stated, "Does it hurt?" and P1 replied, "a little, not bad." At 12:44 PM, while wrapping the patient's leg, P1 indicated the leg was, " very sensitive" and S12 stated, "I think this is the leg you always have a lot of pain with."  As S12 was wrapping the patient's leg, P1 was observed flinching and stated, "Ouch" and S12 stated "sorry."  An assessment of the patient's pain, using a standardized pain tool or criteria established in the facility policy was not observed.

On 4/17/24 at 2:45 PM, S12's Visit Note Report from P1's 4/16/24 visit was reviewed. S12 documented the following Pain Assessment: 

“Was Pain Assessed? Yes; Was Pain Subjectively Assessed? Yes; Does the Client Report Pain? No; Indicate Standardized Pain Tool Used to Determine Patient's Pain Level: Numeric; Numeric: Standardized Pain Tool Used to Determine Patient's Pain Level: 0- Patient has no pain; Were Objective Symptoms observed? No; Are there any additional Details that need to be provided to Describe the Client's Pain? No.”

Review of P1's "Home Health Certification Period and Plan of Care" for Certification Period 4/8/24 - 6/6/24 revealed P1's Orders of Discipline and Treatments, including "...Skilled Nurse for observation and assessment of pain, pain management regimen and skilled teaching related to pain management. Skilled Nurse to intervene with increased pain level to minimize complications. …" 

On 4/18/24 at 1:40 PM, these findings were reviewed with S1 (Manager of Clinical Education). 

2.) Facility policy titled, "Medication Management and Administration," approved 3/23 states, "...II Medication Management A. As part of the initial comprehensive and ongoing clinical assessments conducted by nursing and therapy staff, a review of all medications the patient currently uses will be performed in order to identify any potential adverse effects, drug reactions, and duplicate therapy. …" 

On 4/16/24 at 12:19 PM, S12, a Registered Nurse, was observed during a home visit for P1. During the visit, a review of patient medications was not observed.

On 4/17/24 at 2:45 PM, S12's Visit Note Report from P1's 4/16/24 visit was reviewed. In the Narrative, S12 documented "Medication Reconciliation Conducted: Y [YES]. Medication Reconciliation Issues Identified and Resolved: Y [YES]".

On 4/18/24 at 1:45 PM, during an interview with S1(Manager of Clinical Education), S1 stated that a comprehensive medication reconciliation is completed at every start of care visit, and for subsequent visits, the nurse will ask if there are any changes to the patient's medications, or any new medications. The above finding was confirmed with S1. 

N.J.A.C. 8:42-6.2(a)(4)

Infection control
CFR(s): 484.70(b)(1)(2)
Standard: Control.  

The HHA must maintain a coordinated agency-wide program for the surveillance, identification, prevention, control, and investigation of infectious and communicable diseases that is an integral part of the HHA's quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program. The infection control program must include:



(1) A method for identifying infectious and communicable disease problems; and



(2) A plan for the appropriate actions that are expected to result in improvement and disease prevention.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation during home visits of two of two patients (Patient (P)2, and P7), staff interview, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that re-useable equipment is decontaminated after each use.

Findings include:

On 4/16/24 at 12:07 PM, during a home visit of P2, Staff (S)2, the Registered Nurse (RN) was observed placing his/her bag on a clean barrier. S2 then removed a second bag that contained medical equipment, including a blood pressure cuff and stethoscope. At 12:13 PM, S2 was observed applying the blood pressure cuff directly to P2’s exposed skin. After obtaining P2’s blood pressure, S2 then placed the used blood pressure cuff back into the second bag without disinfecting the blood pressure cuff. S2 then used the stethoscope on P2 and disinfected the diaphragm of the stethoscope. The entirety of the stethoscope was not disinfected. S2 then placed the stethoscope on top of the dirty blood pressure cuff in the second bag. 

On 4/17/24 at 11:25 AM, during a home visit with P7, S9 an RN was observed using a stethoscope on P7. S9 then disinfected the diaphragm of the stethoscope and returned it to the bag. The entirety of the stethoscope was not disinfected.  S9 then applied a blood pressure cuff directly to P7’s exposed skin. After obtaining P7’s blood pressure, S9 then returned the used blood pressure cuff to the bag without disinfecting it.

On 4/18/24 at 2:20 PM, these findings were reviewed with S1, the Manager of Clinical Education. S1 indicated that he/she is in charge of infection prevention for the facility. S1 stated, “the blood pressure cuff and stethoscope should be cleaned after being used. S1 also stated, “any equipment that touches a patients skin needs to be disinfected.” S1 indicated that disposable plastic sleeves are available to use rather than putting the blood pressure directly on the patient’s skin.

Facility policy titled, “Infection Control: Bag Technique,” approved 4/22, states, “Purpose: To maintain the integrity of the clinician bag and prevent transmission of infection. …3. Open reusable equipment section to access equipment needed for patient care. 4. Clean diaphragm of stethoscope, thermometer, pulse ox and stylus with alcohol wipe before and after patient contact. Once cleaned with alcohol return equipment to reuse section of the clinician bag. …”

N.J.A.C. 8:42-12.2(b)(3)

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
All orders recorded in plan of care
CFR(s): 484.60(a)(3)
All patient care orders, including verbal orders, must be recorded in the plan of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interview, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure the ordered frequency of skilled nursing visits corresponds with skilled nursing visits conducted in two (2) out of 17 patients (Patients (P)5 and P10).

Reference the facility policy titled, “Care Planning, Assessment, and Reassessment” approved 4/24, states, “The Plan of Care is consulted with the physician or allowed practitioner and approved by the physician or allowed practitioner. …2. Planning and development of the patient care plan will include: …d. The frequency and duration of visits …”. 

On 4/17/24 at 10:50 AM, medical record review of P10 revealed on 4/3/24 at 6:17 PM, a “Physician Order” that stated, “Order Description: ADD SN [skilled nurse] VISITS FOR WOUND CARE… Service Changes: Calendar Frequency: SN EFFECTIVE 03/31/2024 5WK1 [five visits for one week] …”. P10’s medical record lacked evidence five skilled nurse visits were conducted the week of 3/31/24. 

On 4/18/24 at 10:50 AM, S3 confirmed on the week of 3/31/24 the frequency of nurse visits ordered was five and P10 only had four skilled nursing visits conducted. 

P10’s medical record revealed on 4/6/24 at 1:19 PM, a “Physician Order” that stated, “Order Description: ADDITIONAL SN VISIT FOR WOUND CARE…. Service Changes: Calendar Frequency: SN Effective 04/07/2024 4WK1 [four visits a week for one week] …”. P10’s medical record lacked evidence four skilled nurse visits were conducted on the week of 4/7/24. 

On 4/18/24 at 11:20 AM, S1 stated, “The nurses will call the doctor and verbalize a request for more visits, the doctor will verbalize the approval of additional visits, then the nurse goes into the patient’s calendar and adds in the visits.” S1 indicated the nurse should indicate in the “Description” of the “Physician Order” note how many visits the doctor approved. S1 confirmed there were discrepancies between the calendar frequency and visits completed according to the medical record. 

On 4/18/24, review of Patient (P) 5's medical record revealed a "Physician Order"  on 4/8/24 at 11:34 AM, with the following documented:

"Order Description: Add SN [skilled nurse] visits for WD [wound] care, recert [recertify] home care." There was no documentation of the amount of skilled nurse visits to be added in the description. "Service Changes: Calendar Frequency: SN [skilled nurse] effective 4/07/2024 4WK1 [4 visits a week for 1 week] …" P5's medical record lacked documentation that four nursing visits were conducted the week of 4/7/24.

At 11:30 AM, S1 (Manager of Clinical Education) confirmed there was no additional documentation of the number of skilled nursing visits ordered by the physician, and that the week of 4/7/24, three nursing visits had occurred instead of four. 

N.J.A.C. 8:42-6.2(a)(6)

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Survey dates: July 6, 7, 8, 2021

This was a Federal Recertification Survey, a Federal COVID-19 Focused Infection Control Survey, and State Re-licensure Survey. Valley Home Care is not in compliance with Federal requirements under 42 CFR Part 484 regulations for Home Health Agencies and State requirements under Title 8, Chapter 42, Licensing Standards for Home Health Agencies.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation of one (1) of three (3) skilled nursing visits, staff interviews, review of facility policies and procedures, and review of Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidelines, it was determined the facility failed to ensure separation of clean and soiled equipment is maintained and standard precautions and bag technique are performed in accordance with facility policy.

 

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, "Infection Control - Standard Precautions" states, "... II. Hand Hygiene A. ... Perform hand rubbing with an alcohol based preparation before and after patient contact, immediately after gloves are removed... when moving from a dirty body site to a clean site on the same patient... . III. Gloves A. Wear gloves (clean, nonsterile gloves are adequate) when touching... and contaminated items. B. Put on clean gloves just before touching... non-intact skin. C. Change gloves and wash hands between tasks and procedures on the same patient after contact with material that may contain a high concentration of microorganisms. D. Remove gloves promptly after use, before touching non-contaminated items and environmental surfaces... . E. Perform hand hygiene immediately to avoid transfer of microorganisms to other patients or environments. ... ." 

Reference #2: CDC 2007, "Guideline for Isolation Precautions: Preventing Transmission of Infectious Agents in Healthcare Settings," (http://www.cdc.gov/hicpac/pdf/isolation/Isolation2007.pdf), page 50 states, "During patient care, transmission of infectious organisms can be reduced by adhering to the principles of working from 'clean' to 'dirty', and confining or limiting contamination to surfaces that are directly needed for patient care."

Reference #3: Facility policy, "Infection Control: Bag Technique" states, "Procedure... 2. Perform hand hygiene before entry into bag. ... ." 

1. During a home visit for Patient #2, on 7/6/21, the following was observed:

a. Staff #6 removed the patient's neck-wound dressing with ungloved hands. 

i. Staff #6 sanitized his/her hands, touched the back and seat cushion of a chair, recontaminating his/her hands. Staff #6 then donned gloves to perform care to the neck wound. 

ii. During wound care, while wearing contaminated gloves, Staff #6 retrieved clean supplies from the supply bag without first performing hand hygiene and changing his/her gloves.

iii. At 1:45 PM, Staff #6 removed his/her gloves and picked up a barrier drape, and retrieved additional supplies from the supply bag. Staff #6 did not perform hand hygiene after removing his/her gloves.

b. At 2:10 PM, using only one (1) glove on his/her right hand, Staff #6 performed a saline cleanse to the skin around the tracheotomy site.

i. Staff #6 removed and placed his/her glove, used alcohol wipes, gauze and wrappers, onto the patient's kitchen table next to a pile of clean dressing supplies, co-mingling the clean supplies and used items. 

ii. With ungloved hands, Staff #6 picked up and discarded used wound dressings, into a plastic bag on the floor, then entered his/her bag without performing hand hygiene. 

iii. Staff #6 retrieved a computer tablet from his/her bag without performing hand hygiene. He/she then placed the tablet on the contaminated area of the kitchen table, picking up the computer tablet without performing hand hygiene.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1 and Staff #3 on 7/6/21 at 2:25 PM. 

N.J.A.C. 8.42-12.2(b)

N.J.A.C. 8.42-12.2(b)3

N.J.A.C. 8.42-12.2(b)(6)i

HH aide supervision elements
CFR(s): 484.80(h)(4)(i-vi)
Home health aide supervision must ensure that aides furnish care in a safe and effective manner, including, but not limited to, the following elements:

(i) Following the patient's plan of care for completion of tasks assigned to a home health aide by the registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional;

(ii) Maintaining an open communication process with the patient, representative (if any), caregivers, and family;

(iii) Demonstrating competency with assigned tasks;

(iv) Complying with infection prevention and control policies and procedures;

(v) Reporting changes in the patient's condition; and

(vi) Honoring patient rights.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of two (2) of three (3) medical records (#3 and #6), staff interviews, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure the registered nurse includes appropriate elements to the Home Health Aides assignment for rendering safe and effective care. 

Findings include: 

Facility policy, "Home Health Aides - Assignment & Supervision Policies" states, "... Procedures: I. Assignment of Home Health Aides... Home Health Aide care plan is developed by a Registered Nurse... The Home Health Aide plan of care will include... The type of service/procedure to be provided. ... Specific procedure to be performed including... frequency... ."

1. Review of Medical Record #3, on 7/8/21, revealed the following:

a. The patient's Start of Care (SOC) date was 6/23/2021. On the "Aide Care Plan Report," the RN chose for "Frequency" - "Per Patient Request" for the following: 

i. Fall Risk

ii. Observe Physical/Mental Changes

iii. Report Falls

iv. Report S/S [signs and symptoms] of Infection To RN

v. Report Change in Pain Level To RN

vi. Impaired Hearing 

2. Review of Medical Record #6 on 7/8/21, revealed the following:

a. The patient's Start of Care (SOC) date was 6/4/2021. On the "Aide Care Plan Report," the RN chose for "Frequency" - "Per Patient Request" for the following: 

i. Fall Risk

ii. Observe Physical/Mental Changes

 

iii. Report S/S [signs and symptoms] of Infection To RN

iv. Report Change in Pain Level To RN

 

v. Do Not Resuscitate

3. Upon interview on 7/8/21 at 2:40 PM, Staff #3 confirmed that "Frequency" for the above care/services should not be "Per Patient Request" and should have been "Every Visit."

N.J.A.C. 8:42-6.2(a)

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This is a Federal Recertification survey conducted on 2/5/18, 2/6/18, and 2/8/18, which resulted in standard level deficiencies.

COMPLIANCE W/ ACCEPTED PROFESSIONAL STD
CFR(s): 484.12(c)
The HHA and its staff must comply with accepted professional standards and principles that apply to professionals furnishing services in an HHA.     




This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interview and review of facility documents, it was determined that the facility failed to develop a written policy and procedure for handling, storage, cleaning and disinfecting of electronic devices.

Findings include:

Reference #1: CDC [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention] Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities, 2008 states, "Ensure that, at a minimum, noncritical patient-care devices are disinfected when visibly soiled and on a regular basis (such as after use on each patient ...)". 

1. On 2/5/18 and 2/6/18, during 4 home visits, the following was observed:

a. Facility issued tablets (electronic devices), requiring the patients to sign by using their finger on the surface of the tablets, were not being disinfected between patient use.

b. Facility issued tablets (electronic devices) had a suede-like device cover that was a non-cleanable surface.

2. On interview, it was revealed that there is no policy and procedure regarding cleaning and disinfecting of electronic devices. 

3. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2. 

B. Based on observation, review of facility documents, and staff interviews, it was determined the facility failed to maintain acceptable standards to assure prevention of infection. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: The facility policy and procedure "Infection Control-Standard Precautions/Transmission-Based Precautions" stated, "...PROCEDURE: 1. Hand Hygiene ...B. Indications for hand hygiene include: 1. Before having contact with patient and after all contact is completed; 2. Between procedures; 3. Immediately after having contact with body fluids or excretions, mucous membranes, non-intact skin or wound dressings; 4. After removing gloves; ...C. Techniques for hand hygiene: ...2. When decontaminating hands with alcohol-based rub: a. apply product to palm of one hand b. rub hands together, covering all surfaces of hands and fingers until hands are dry. ...IV. Transmission Based Precautions A. Contact Precautions ...4. Gloves and Hand Hygiene: ...c. Gloves should be changed after having contact with infective material (e.g. fecal material and wound drainage). ..."

Reference #2: The facility policy and procedure "Bag Technique" stated, "...PROCEDURE: ...2. Perform hand hygiene before entry into bag. 3. Remove equipment/supplies needed for patient care. 4. Close bag and leave it in safe place. ...6. Perform hand hygiene before repacking or re-entering the bag. ..."

1. During a home visit with Patient #2 on 2/5/18, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #10 applied hand sanitizer to his/her hands, rubbed his/her hands together, but did not allow his/her hands to dry. Staff #10 dried his/her hands with a paper towel.

b. Prior to showering Patient #2, Staff #10 removed wound dressings from Patient #2's left lower extremity. Staff #10 did not doff his/her gloves to decontaminate his/her hands.

c. Staff #10 provided personal care to Patient #2 in the shower. Once the shower was complete, Staff #10 did not doff his/her gloves, decontaminate his/her hands or donn new gloves prior to assisting Patient #2 with skin care.

d. Prior to performing wound care on Patient #2, Staff #10 applied hand sanitizer to his/her hands, and rubbed his/her hands together, but did not allow his/her hands to dry, instead, dried them with a paper towel.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1 and Staff #2.

3. During a home visit with Patient #3 on 2/6/18, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #12 opened the clean area of the bag without sanitizing his/her hands.

i. He/she removed hand sanitizer from the clean portion of the bag and applied it to his/her hands. 

ii. He/she failed to close the clean portion of the bag after obtaining needed supplies, as per Reference #2 above.

b. Staff #12 sanitized his/her hands, then proceeded to pull his/her tablet from the clean portion of the bag and keyboard.

i. Staff #13 confirmed that the tablet and keyboard should be placed in the outside zippered portion of the bag. 

c. Staff #12 removed alcohol wipes from the clean portion of the bag without sanitizing his/her hands. 

d. Staff #12 obtained the pulse oximeter from the clean portion of the bag without sanitizing his/her hands. 

e. Patient #3 signed the tablet and Staff #12 placed the tablet and keyboard back into the clean portion of the bag without the tablet being sanitized.

i. Staff #12 confirmed that he/she cleans the tablet and keyboard as needed.

ii. Staff #13 confirmed that it is recommended to clean the tablet when a patient signs the surface with their finger. 

4. The above finding were confirmed with Staff #1 and Staff #2.

ASSIGNMENT & DUTIES OF HOME HEALTH AIDE

Written patient care instructions for the home health aide must be prepared by the registered nurse or other appropriate professional who is responsible for the supervision of the home health aide under paragraph (d) of this section.

Quality assessment/performance improvement
CFR(s): 484.65
Condition of participation: Quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI).



The HHA must develop, implement, evaluate, and maintain an effective, ongoing, HHA-wide, data-driven QAPI program. The HHA's governing body must ensure that the program reflects the complexity of its organization and services; involves all HHA services (including those services provided under contract or arrangement); focuses on indicators related to improved outcomes, including the use of emergent care services, hospital admissions and re-admissions; and takes actions that address the HHA's performance across the spectrum of care, including the prevention and reduction of medical errors. The HHA must maintain documentary evidence of its QAPI program and be able to demonstrate its operation to CMS.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interviews, review of facility documents, and review of facility policies and procedures, it was determined the facility failed to ensure an effective, ongoing, data-driven quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program, is maintained.

2. The facility failed to ensure performance improvement activities focused on high risk, high volume, or problem prone areas. (Cross refer to Tag G-646).

3. The facility failed to collect, measure, and analyze data to monitor the effectiveness of safety and quality of care (Cross refer to Tag G-654).

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on observation during one (1) of four (4) home visits, staff interviews, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure their infection prevention policies regarding manufacturer's instructions for use, are followed.

Findings include:

 

Reference: SaniZide Plus Germicidal Solution manufacturer's instruction for use states, "... Contact time [Between One (1) to Ten (10) minute contact time depending on the organism]." 

1. During a home visit on 7/12/21, Staff #3 was observed spraying SaniZide Plus Germicidal Solution to disinfect patient equipment and then placed the equipment in the bag without waiting for the appropriate contact time. 

2. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #1.

B. Based on observation and staff interview in three (3) of four (4) home visits, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that laptops/tablets are cleaned according to facility policy.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, Care Maintenance and Use of Laptop Computer/Tablet/Device, states, "...14. No stickers should be put on the computer. 15. The exterior of the notebook should be kept clean with a soft, damp cloth. No alcohol or detergent should be used. 16. The Screen/LCD/monitor should be wiped with a soft, dry cloth. No glass cleaner, alcohol or detergent should be used. 17. The patient is to sign a visit verification on the tablet at the conclusion of the visit. When the patient is signing, the clinician should hold the tablet for the patient to prevent cross contamination and the patient signs with stylus [sic] after which the clinician wipes the stylus with an alcohol wipe."

1. During a home visit for Patient #1 on 7/12/21, the following was observed:

a. After documentation on the tablet was completed and Patient #1 signed the laptop using his/her finger, Staff #2 placed the laptop back into his/her bag without cleaning it.

i. The screen was visibly dirty.

2. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 7/12/21, the following was observed:

a. Staff #3 placed the tablet directly on the bed, on top of the patient's bedsheets.

b. After documentation on the tablet was completed, Staff #3 sprayed the tablet with SaniZide Plus Germicidal Solution.

c. At the end of the patient visit, Staff #3 handed the tablet and stylus to Patient #3's caretaker and requested a signature. Staff #3 proceeded to place the laptop back into his/her bag without cleaning the tablet or wiping the stylus with an alcohol pad.

3. During a home visit for Patient #4 on 7/12/21, the following was observed:

a. After documentation on the tablet was completed, Staff #2 placed the laptop in front of Patient #4 for a signature. Patient #4 pulled the tablet towards her/him and rested it on her/his chest to sign. The stylus was not wiped down with an alcohol pad.

i. The screen was visibly dirty.

4. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #1.

N.J.A.C. 8.42- 12.2(b)

C. Based on observation and staff interview in one (1) of four (4) home visits, it was determined the facility failed to ensure separation between clean and soiled equipment was maintained.

Findings include:

1. On 7/12/21, during a home visit for Patient #4, the following was noted:

a. Staff #2 placed a barrier on a clean surface and placed a blood pressure cuff, stethoscope, pulse oximeter and oral thermometer on the barrier.

b. After taking the patient's temperature with an oral thermometer, Staff #2 placed the oral thermometer on the left side of the barrier.

c. After checking the patient's oxygen level, Staff #2 placed the pulse oximeter on the left side of the barrier next to the oral thermometer.

d. After checking the patient's blood pressure and listening to the patient's heart rate, Staff #2 sprayed the blood pressure cuff and stethoscope with SaniZide Plus Germicidal Solution and then placed the blood pressure cuff and stethoscope directly next to the pulse oximeter and oral thermometer, which had not been disinfected.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1.

D. Based on observation during three (3) of four (4) home visits, staff interviews, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure hand hygiene is performed in accordance with facility policy.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, Hand Washing, states, " ...Procedure: A. Wet hands under warm water and apply soap. B. Rub hands together vigorously for at least 15 seconds C. Rinsed thoroughly ... Indications for Handwashing and Hand Antisepsis: C. If gloves are changed during a procedure and hands are not visibly soiled... "waterless antiseptic hand cleaner may be used to decontaminate between glove changes... ." 

1. On 7/12/21, during a home visit for Patient #1, the following was noted:

a. Staff #2 was washing his/her hands at the kitchen sink. Staff #2 rubbed his/her hands vigorously for ten (10) seconds.

2. On 7/12/21, during a home visit for Patient #2, the following was noted:

a. Staff #4 was discarding trash with gloved hands. Staff # 4's gloved hand touched the lid of the garbage can. Staff #4 did not immediately remove his/her gloves and wash his/her hands.

 

3. On 7/12/21, during a home visit for Patient #4, the following was noted:

a. Staff #2 was performing wound care while his/her cell phone began ringing. Staff #2, while wearing gloves, silenced the cell phone.

b. Staff #2 continued with wound care without removing his/her gloves and performing hand hygiene.

i. Staff #2 failed to disinfect her/his cell phone device.

4. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1 and #13.

N.J.A.C. 8.42-12.2(b)

N.J.A.C. 8.42-12.2(b)3

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Quality assessment/performance improvement
CFR(s): 484.65
Condition of participation: Quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI).



The HHA must develop, implement, evaluate, and maintain an effective, ongoing, HHA-wide, data-driven QAPI program. The HHA's governing body must ensure that the program reflects the complexity of its organization and services; involves all HHA services (including those services provided under contract or arrangement); focuses on indicators related to improved outcomes, including the use of emergent care services, hospital admissions and re-admissions; and takes actions that address the HHA's performance across the spectrum of care, including the prevention and reduction of medical errors. The HHA must maintain documentary evidence of its QAPI program and be able to demonstrate its operation to CMS.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of facility documents, review of facility policy and procedure, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that it maintained an effective, ongoing, data-driven quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program.

Findings include:

1. The facility failed to ensure that the QAPI program tracks, measures, and analyzes quality indicators of performance (Cross refer to Tag G-642).

2. The facility failed to collect, measure, and analyze data to monitor the effectiveness of safety and quality of care (Cross refer to Tag G-654).

3. The facility failed to conduct annual performance improvement projects (Cross refer to Tag G-658).

source_record.Facility Name: PROMISE CARE OF ESSEX COUNTY LLC
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection prevention and control
CFR(s): 484.70
Condition of Participation: Infection prevention and control.

The HHA must maintain and document an infection control program which has as its goal the prevention and control of infections and communicable diseases.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility policies and procedures, review of nationally recognized guidelines, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that its infection control program adheres to acceptable standards of practice.

Findings include:

1. The facility failed to ensure that its infection control program adhered to acceptable standards of practice (Cross refer to Tag G-682).

2. The facility failed to ensure that its infection control program includes methods for surveillance, identification, prevention, and investigation of communicable diseases (Cross refer to Tag G-684).

3. The facility failed to ensure that all employees received annual training in infection control (Cross refer to Tag G-686).

source_record.Facility Name: PROMISE CARE OF ESSEX COUNTY LLC
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Organization and administration of services
CFR(s): 484.105
Condition of participation: Organization and administration of services.

The HHA must organize, manage, and administer its resources to attain and maintain the highest practicable functional capacity, including providing optimal care to achieve the goals and outcomes identified in the patient's plan of care, for each patient's medical, nursing, and rehabilitative needs. The HHA must assure that administrative and supervisory functions are not delegated to another agency or organization, and all services not furnished directly are monitored and controlled. The HHA must set forth, in writing, its organizational structure, including lines of authority, and services furnished.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of personnel files, review of facility documents, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that its governing body assumes responsibility for the agency's overall management, operation, and provision of services.

Findings include:

1. The facility failed to ensure that the governing body maintained responsibility for the agency's overall management, operation, and provision of services (Cross refer to Tag G-942).

2. The facility failed to ensure that qualified personnel were employed (Cross refer to Tag G-952).

3. The facility failed to ensure that a qualified, pre-designated person assumes responsibilities for the administrator when he/she is unavailable (Cross refer to Tag G-954).

If the OPO experiences an actual natural or man-made emergency that requires activation of the emergency plan, the OPO is exempt from engaging in its next required testing exercise following the onset of the emergency event.

(ii) Analyze the OPO's response to and maintain documentation of all tabletop exercises, and emergency events, and revise the [RNHCI's and OPO's] emergency plan, as needed.



*[ RNCHIs at §403.748]:

(d)(2) Testing. The RNHCI must conduct exercises to test the emergency plan. The RNHCI must do the following:

(i) Conduct a paper-based, tabletop exercise at least annually. A tabletop exercise is a group discussion led by a facilitator, using a narrated, clinically-relevant emergency scenario, and a set of problem statements, directed messages, or prepared questions designed to challenge an emergency plan.

(ii) Analyze the RNHCI's response to and maintain documentation of all tabletop exercises, and emergency events, and revise the RNHCI's emergency plan, as needed.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of facility documents, review of policy and procedure, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to complete and/or conduct the required two exercises to test the emergency plan at least annually. 

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, Emergency Preparedness Plan states, " ...Testing Program B. [Name of facility] will conduct exercises to test the emergency plan at least annually. 1. Participate in full-scale exercise that is community based or on a community based exercise is not accessible, and individual, facility based. ...3. The group that participates in the table top exercise will analyze the agency's response to and maintain documentation of the drill, table top exercise and emergency events, and revise the agency's emergency plan, as needed. ... ." 

1. Review of the facility's document, "Table Top Exercise Weather Emergency: Blizzard" completed on November 10, 2017 revealed the following:

a. There was no evidence of an analysis and/or revision of the emergency plan for the exercise.

b. Staff #1 confirmed there was no analysis performed post exercise to determine if the facility's emergency plan required revision. 

2. Upon request, Staff #1 was unable to provide evidence of a community or facility-based exercise for 2017 or 2018.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection control
CFR(s): 484.70(b)(1)(2)
Standard: Control.  

The HHA must maintain a coordinated agency-wide program for the surveillance, identification, prevention, control, and investigation of infectious and communicable diseases that is an integral part of the HHA's quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program. The infection control program must include:



(1) A method for identifying infectious and communicable disease problems; and



(2) A plan for the appropriate actions that are expected to result in improvement and disease prevention.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of personnel files, review of facility policy and procedure, review of nationally recognized guidelines, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that its infection control program includes methods for surveillance, identification, prevention, and investigation of communicable diseases.

Reference #1: Facility policy, Infection Control Program states, "... 1) The Infection Control Program is the responsibility of all [name of facility] staff in collaboration with the program's leadership staff and includes the following objectives... d) To comply with current applicable local, State, and regulatory body regulations, including... Center for Disease Control (CDC) guidelines. ... ."

Reference #2: https://www.cdc.gov/tb/topic/testing/healthcareworkers.htm, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), 2016, Testing Health Care Workers, states, " ... There are two types of testing for TB in health care workers. Initial baseline testing upon hire: Two-step testing with a TB skin test or a TB blood test. ...Two-step testing with the Mantoux tuberculin skin test (TST) should be used for baseline or initial testing ... ."

Reference #3: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/rr6007a1.htm, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Morbidity and Mortality Weekly, 2011, states, " ...
