All persons who work in health-care facilities should have presumptive evidence of immunity to measles. ...All persons who work in health-care facilities should have presumptive evidence of immunity to mumps. ... All persons who work in healthcare facilities should have presumptive evidence of immunity to rubella. ...This information should be documented and readily available at the work location. ... ."

1. Review of Staff #3's personnel file on 8/2/18 revealed the following:

a. There was no evidence of rubella or rubeola immunity.

3. Review of Staff #16's personnel file on 8/2/18 revealed the following:

a. There was no evidence of 2-step Mantoux testing, rubella immunity, or rubeola immunity.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:

A. Based on observation, staff interview, and document review, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that infection prevention practices are implemented in accordance with the Centers for Disease Control's (CDC) recommendations, and facility policy. 

Findings includes:

Reference: Facility policy, "Hand Hygiene" states, "... Our Procedure: 

1.0 Indications For Hand Decontamination. Bayada Home Health Care requires that employees decontaminate their hands with an antiseptic agent in an effort to decrease health care-acquired infections ...

a. Before and after having any direct client contact associated with care-giving activities ...

b. Before applying and after removing gloves or other personal protective equipment ...\

c. After contact with inanimate objects ...

2. Procedures For Hand Decontamination ...

2.2 Washing with antimicrobial soap and water 

2.2.7 Turn off water by using a paper to cover the faucet handle."

1. In the morning of 3/12/18, in the presence of Staff #1, a home visit was conducted and the following was observed:

a. Staff #10 turned off the water faucet handle at the sink without a paper barrier.

b. After removing his/her gloves, Staff #10 proceeded to give the electronic tablet to the patient for signature without first sanitizing his/her hands. 

2. On 3/13/18, in the presence of Staff #1, a home visit was conducted and the following was observed:

a. Staff #7 sanitized his/her hands, removed wound dressing supplies from the supply box, and then applied gloves.

(i) Staff #7 did not sanitize his/her hands before applying gloves.

b. Staff #7 picked up a wrapper from the floor, then he/she picked up a scissor that had been cleaned and placed the scissor in the supply box.

(i) Staff #7 did not sanitize his/her hands after touching the floor.

c. Medical Record #11 indicated a visit date of 1/16/18. The "Visit Note Report" reflected documentation time was completed on 1/20/2018.

2. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #1.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Investigate complaints made by patient
CFR(s): 484.50(e)(1)(i)
(i) Investigate complaints made by a patient, the patient's representative (if any), and the patient's caregivers and family, including, but not limited to, the following topics:

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on a review of 4 complaints and staff interview on 3/15/18, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that 3 complaints were not processed in accordance with facility policy.

Reference: Facility policy "Client Complaints" states, "... 3.0 Complaint Process ... 3.3 The Client Service Manager, Clinical Manager and/or Director investigate and respond to complaints from clients or their representatives promptly and in accordance with applicable state requirements. The client is informed of the findings of the investigation and the decisions rendered to resolve the complaint. 

4.0 Documentation. 4.1 All complaints, verbal and written, are documented in the applicable electronic system. 3. A Complaint Report form indicated that a complaint was voiced on 1/24/18. There was no documentation of any investigation by the Client Service Manager, Clinical Manager and/or Director. 

4. The above was confirmed by Staff #4.

source_record.Facility Name: Cape Regional Home Health Care, LLC
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
RN performs assessment
CFR(s): 484.55(a)(1)
A registered nurse must conduct an initial assessment visit to determine the immediate care and support needs of the patient; and, for Medicare patients, to determine eligibility for the Medicare home health benefit, including homebound status. The initial assessment visit must be held either within 48 hours of referral, or within 48 hours of the patient's return home, or on the physician- ordered start of care date.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of 10 medical records, staff interview and review of facility documents, it was determined that the facility failed to perform initial assessments within the required time frame for 6 patients.

Findings include: 

Reference: Facility policy "Client Assessment and Reassessment" states, "... 1.1 The initial assessment must be done prior or simultaneous to the start of care, and within the following time frames: a. 48 hours of referral b. 48 hours of client's return home c. on the physician-ordered start of care date."

1. The medical record of Patient #15 revealed a Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC (start of care) of 10/30/17. The patient was referred for home health services on 10/27/17 and was initially seen on 10/30/17, one day late, and not within 48 hours of the patient being available. There was no evidence that the patient postponed services. 

2. The medical record of Patient #2 revealed a Home Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC of 2/18/18. The patient was referred to home health services on 2/14/18 and initially seen on 2/18/18, two days late, and not within 48 hours of the patient being available. There was no evidence that the patient postponed services.

3. The medical record of Patient #14 revealed a Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC of 10/6/17. The patient was referred to home health services on 9/28/17. The first scheduled visit was made for 10/2/17. Subsequently, the visits were rescheduled for 10/4/17 and for 10/6/17, as per the patient request. The physician was notified of the changes.

a. There was no evidence that the patient initially postponed the services. The first scheduled visit was 2 days late, and not within 48 hours of referral. 

4. The medical record of Patient #3 revealed a Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC of 1/25/18. The patient was referred for home health services on 1/18/18 and was initially seen on 1/25/18. The patient was discharged from the hospital on 1/18/18. 

a. Patient #3 was seen five (5) days late, and not within 48 hours of the patient being available. There was no evidence that the patient postponed services. 

5. The medical record of Patient #11 revealed a Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC of 1/11/18. The patient was referred for home health services on 11/8/17. The patient's discharge date was 1/8/18 and was initially seen on 1/11/18. 

a. Patient #11 was seen one (1) day late, and not seen within 48 hours of the patient being available. There was no evidence that the patient postponed services. 

6. The medical record of Patient #10 revealed a Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC of 2/13/18. The patient was referred for home health services on 2/8/18. The patient's discharge date was 2/7/18 and was initially seen on 2/13/18. 

a. Patient #10 was seen three (3) days late, and not within 48 hours of the patient being available. There was no evidence that the patient postponed services. 

7. During interview, Staff #1 confirmed that there were no documentation under the Coordination Notes addressing the late assessments. 

8. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #2.

source_record.Deficiency Description: 5 Calendar Days After Start Of Care
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
5 calendar days after start of care
CFR(s): 484.55(b)(1)
The comprehensive assessment must be completed in a timely manner, consistent with the patient's immediate needs, but no later than 5 calendar days after the start of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of 4 medical records, and staff interview on 3/14/18, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the comprehensive assessment for 2 patients was conducted in accordance with facility policy.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy "Referral Process & Admission Criteria And Procedure" states, " ... 3.0 Admission/Readmission Procedure ... 3.1.2. The comprehensive assessment must be completed in a timely manner, consistent with in client's immediate needs, but no later than 5 calendar days after the start of care ... 3.9 When a discipline is added after the initial evaluation has been completed, ... medical social worker will make their initial evaluation within five to seven days of receiving the referral."

1. Review of Medical Record #7 revealed a Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a Start of Care (SOC) of 2/3/18. A medical social worker evaluation order was obtained on 2/8/18. This evaluation was conducted on 2/16/18 and not within 5 to 7 days, as required by the above policy. There was no evidence that the patient postponed the service. 

2. Review of Medical Record #17 revealed a Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC of 8/12/17. The physician order stated "PT [Physical Therapy] Effective 8/13/2017 1WK1 [one visit for the week of 8/13/17]." Although attempts to reach the patient were made, as indicated on a note dated 8/15/17 (none thereafter), the physical therapy evaluation was conducted on 8/23/17, and not within 5 calendar days, as required by the above policy. There was no evidence that the patient postponed the service. 

3. The above was confirmed by Staff #2.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Patient's needs
CFR(s): 484.55(c)(4)
The patient's medical, nursing, rehabilitative, social, and discharge planning needs;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on a review of 2 medical records of patients considered at a high nutritional risk, and staff interview, on 3/16/18, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that patient nutritional needs are met in accordance with the nutritional policy for Patient #17.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Nutritional Care and Assessment" states, "... Our Procedure: ... 2.0 All clients will receive a nutritional risk screening as a part of the initial assessment ... 3. The client's physician will be involved in the plan of care and ordering a nutritionist to complete a consult ... 4. Clients deemed high risk or with certain diagnosis will automatically have a nutritional consult: ... clients with wounds greater than a Stage II or a non-healing wound ... 5.0 All clients receive a nutritional risk assessment as part of the comprehensive assessment ... 5.3 Clients who score 6 or above on the assessment will have a nutritionist ordered and follow through as noted above."

1. The medical record of Patient #17 revealed a Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a Start of Care (SOC) of 8/12/17. The Nutritional section of Visit Note Report, dated 8/12/17, of the Nursing Oasis Admission indicated a total nutritional assessment risk score of 11, placing the patient at a high nutritional risk. The patient was discharged from home health services on 10/4/17. 

2. There was no evidence that a nutritional referral had been made or that the patient refused, as required by the above reference policy.

source_record.Facility Name: Cape Regional Home Health Care, LLC
source_record.Deficiency Description: Provide Services In The Plan Of Care
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Provide services in the plan of care
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(3)
Providing services that are ordered by the physician as indicated in the plan of care;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of 4 medical records and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the patient plan of care is implemented in accordance with physician orders for 2 patients.

Findings include:

1. On 3/13/18, review of Medical Record # 17 revealed the following:

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a Start of Care (SOC) of 8/12/17 indicated the physician "Orders of Discipline and Treatments" for: ... "SN [skilled nurse] ... Skilled observation of client weight. Notify physician of weight gain of 3 pounds in one day or 5 pounds in one week."

b. A skilled nursing visit was performed on 8/12/17. At that time, the patient's weight was 145 pounds (lbs). 

c. Subsequent visits made on 8/14/17, 8/17/17, 8/21/17, and 8/24/17 lacked evidence of the patient's weight or of any inquiry of the patient's weight. 

d. A visit made on 8/31/17 indicated a patient weight of 149 lbs. A subsequent visit on 9/7/17 indicated a weight of 157 lbs. 

e. There was no evidence that the physician was made aware of the increase in the patient's weight.

2. On 3/14/18, review of Medical Record #15 revealed the following:

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC of 10/30/17 indicated the physician "Orders of Discipline and Treatments for:

"Home Health Aide Service For Assistance With Personal Care ... 

Registered Dietician For Evaluation To Assess Nutritional Needs ...

Skilled Nurse to Observe Patient With Generalized Depression And Assess Need For Disease Education ...

Skilled Nurse To Perform Anticoagulant Monitoring Via Fingerstick Or Venipuncture And Report Results To Physician. Skilled Nurse Observe And Assess The Effectiveness Of Anticoagulation Regimen And Provide Skilled Teaching Related To Anticoagulation Therapy."

b. Although there was documentation that an Aide Care Plan was mailed to the client on 11/1/17 (unable to locate one), there was no evidence that aide services were provided to the patient. The patient was discharged from service on 11/28/17.

c. There was no evidence that a dietician evaluated the patient for nutritional needs. The patient was discharged from service on 11/28/17.

d. The nursing Visit Note Reports a total of 7 visits, following the initial Nursing Oasis Admission, lacked evidence of any observations related to Depression or of any education provided toward the disease. 

e. Although, there was evidence of education provided to the patient/caregivers about anticoagulation therapy, there was no evidence that the patient was on any anticoagulation regimen. 

f. The above was confirmed by Staff #2.

source_record.Facility Name: Cape Regional Home Health Care, LLC
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Patient and caregiver education
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(5)
Patient and caregiver education;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of two medical records and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the patient/caregiver is assessed for appropriateness of medication delivery and educated as needed. 

Findings include:

1. On 3/15/18, review of Medical Record #2 revealed the following:

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care, Start of Care (SOC) 2/26/18, indicated that Patient #2 was on anticoagulation injection therapy, daily, administered by the patient's caregiver. Although, education was provided about the medication, bleeding precautions and site rotation, there was no evidence that the patient/caregiver was assessed for appropriateness of delivery/feedback demonstration of subcutaneous injection. 

b. The nursing Visit Note Report dated 3/8/18, indicated that the patient was placed on Microbid prior to the nursing visit due to "Urine odor worsened earlier in the week." Education was provided regarding the medication., however, there was no evidence that the patient/caregiver was provided education related to the prevention of urinary infection.

2. On 3/13/18, review of Medical Record #17 revealed the following:

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care with a SOC of 8/12/17 indicated physician "Orders of Discipline and Treatments ... Skilled Nurse to access PICC line ... Client and CG [caregiver] instructed to perform infusion ..."

(i) The Narrative section of the Oasis Visit Note Report dated 8/12/17, indicated that the "Cg [caregiver] and client need continued instruction regarding IV ABX [intravenous antibiotic ] infusion." The patient was scheduled to receive intravenous antibiotics twice daily, via the family. In the evening of 8/13/17, after a call from the family/patient requesting assistance with the infusion, an as needed visit was done by a nurse. Although, caregiver and patient observed administration and verbal instructions was provided that day and subsequent visits (7), there was no evidence that a feedback demonstration was done. 

3. The above was confirmed by Staff #1 and Staff #2.

Communication with physicians

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This was a Federal Recertification Survey, State Re-Licensure Survey, and Mandatory Vaccination Investigation conducted on February 14, 15, and 16, 2023. Patient Care is not in compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies and State requirements under N.J.A.C. 8:42, Home Health Agency Licensing Standards.

Interdisciplinary assessment of the patient
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(1)
Ongoing interdisciplinary assessment of the patient;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation of two of three patients (#3, #16), staff interviews, review of medical records, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that ongoing interdisciplinary assessment findings are incorporated into the plan of care. 

Findings include:

Facility policy titled, "Patient Assessment, Initial and Reassessment (reviewed 01/06/23) states, " … Procedure: … 1. Upon admission and reassessments, the qualified clinician performs the following assessment activities and collects the following data: … b. Patient's strengths, goals, and care preferences, including information that may be used to demonstrate patient's progress toward achievement of goals identified by patient … . " 

 

During a home visit for Patient #3 (P3) on 02/14/23 at 3:07 PM, a family member asked Staff #5 (Registered Nurse) what the criteria was for the patient to restart physical therapy services, stating that the patient wanted to increase the use of his/her walker. Staff #5 stated that the patient had just been recertified and "when [his/her] certification period is up again, I'll make sure that the doctor orders it." 

Upon interview on 02/16/23 at 9:50 AM, Staff #1 (Executive Director) stated that if a patient or family is expressing a need for additional services in the middle of a certification period, the staff member "would call the physician or clinical manager" for evaluation. A review of P3's medical record was conducted, including Staff #3's Visit Note from 02/14/23. There was no documentation of a request for evaluation of physical therapy services. Staff #1 confirmed that there was no documentation in the medical record regarding a request for evaluation of physical therapy services.

 

During a home visit for Patient #16 (P16) on 02/15/23, the following was indicated:

Upon interview at 10:40 AM in the presence of Staff #11 (Speech Therapist), P16 was asked if there were any services he/she felt were needed that he/she was not receiving. P16 stated, "I'm not sure if I need a Home Health Aide, but my daughter says that I could use one. So maybe a Home Health Aide."

On 02/16/23, review of Staff #11's Visit Note for the home visit conducted for P16 on 02/15/23, revealed that there was no documentation that Staff #11 discussed P16's desire for a Home Health Aide with the RN case manager or the physician.

Upon interview on 02/16/23 at 9:58 AM, Staff #1 stated, "If the patient is requesting another service, the clinician would call the doctor directly and report that the patient wanted another service. If the clinician was busy, they may request the help of the PCM (Patient Care Manager) to call the doctor." Staff #1 confirmed that there was no evidence in P16's medical record that Staff #11 notified the nurse of physician that P16 was requesting another service.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This was a Federal Recertification Survey conducted on March 2, 3, and 4, 2020, that resulted in Standard Level deficiencies. Patient Care is in compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, Conditions Of Participation for Home Health Agencies.

HHA Comprehensive Assessment in Disaster
CFR(s): 484.102(b)(1)
§484.102(b)(1) Condition for Participation:

[(b) Policies and procedures.  The HHA must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 

At a minimum, the policies and procedures must address the following:]



(1) The plans for the HHA's patients during a natural or man-made disaster. Individual plans for each patient must be included as part of the comprehensive patient assessment, which must be conducted according to the provisions at §484.55.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of three (3) of three (3) medical records (#9, #10, and #11), review of facility documents, and staff interviews, it was determined that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to ensure that all patients receive an individualized emergency plan as part of their comprehensive assessment.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, Emergency Preparedness/ Operations Plan, states, "Policy ... A patient triage list will be maintained and updated ongoing. ... 1. Patients are evaluated according to their care/transport/evacuation needs using the Emergency Preparedness/ On Call Plan. 2. The agency maintains a triage list of patients grouped according to these needs. The list included patients requiring outside assistance and/or transportation to evacuate if needed. 6. Staff a. Staff shall assist in maintaining up to date triage board and/or list. ... Preparation for Emergencies And Disasters: (Preparation) General ...4. The agency shall instruct patients and caregivers on the emergency plan upon admission. ..." 

1. Upon review of the "Patient Disaster Plan ID Form" for Patient #9, #10, and #11 on 3/3/20, the following was noted:

a. The Evacuation Destination and Evacuation Address were blank.

b. Staff #2 confirmed the above on 3/3/20 at 1:30 PM.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interviews, and review of facility documents, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that all staff adhere to acceptable standards of practice to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases. 

Findings include: 

Reference #1: Facility policy, Cleaning of Re-useable Equipment, states, "Definitions: 1. Low-Level Disinfection-...Examples include 70% isopropyl alcohol. 2. Intermediate-Level Disinfection-...Examples include Sani Cloth Plus and bleach wipes. 3. Non-Critical Items...should be cleaned for use by undergoing low-level disinfection (e.g.,... blood pressure cuffs....) ...9. Blood pressure cuffs are cleaned with a low-level disinfectant wipe after each use and before being returned to staff bags." 

Reference #2: Facility document, Home Care Bag Protocol Job Aid, states, "... Remove containers that will be used to discard contaminated disposable supplies, such as a plastic bag. ... Never re-enter the bag unless hands are clean. You must perform hand hygiene before re-entering the bag. ..."

Reference #3: Manufacturers Instructions for Use, Sani-Cloth Germicidal Disposable Wipe, states, "... Do not reuse towelette. Dispose of used towelette in trash. ..."

Reference #4: Facility policy, Hand Hygiene, states, "... Staff will perform hand hygiene ... after contact with inanimate objects (including medical equipment) ..."

1. During a home visit for Patient #5 on 3/3/20 at 10:40 AM, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #12 cleaned the blood pressure cuff with an intermediate level disinfectant. 

i. The blood pressure cuff should have been cleaned with a low level disinfectant. 

2. During a home visit for Patient #1 on 3/2/20 at 11:15 AM, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #3 used one towelette to clean the portable pulse oximeter, the blood pressure cuff, and the stethoscope. 

i. The same towelette was used to clean all three pieces of equipment. 

ii. The used towelette was placed on the barrier pad with the home care bag and clean equipment.

b. Staff #3 measured Patient #1's oxygen level with the pulse oximeter several times throughout the visit. 

i. Each time the pulse oximeter was cleaned, the used towelette was placed on the barrier pad with the home care bag and clean equipment. 

c. Staff #3 did not discard the contaminated disposable towelette into a container. 

3. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 3/3/20 at 10:55 AM, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #9 cleaned the blood pressure cuff, stethoscope, and pulse oximeter and then assessed the patient's temperature. 

i. Staff #9 failed to perform hand hygiene after cleaning the equipment. 

ii. Staff #9 failed to perform hand hygiene after assessing the patient's temperature. 

4. During a home visit for Patient #4 on 3/3/20 at 12:05 PM, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #10 cleaned the blood pressure cuff, stethoscope, and pulse oximeter while wearing gloves. 

i. Staff #10 re-entered the home care bag without doffing his/her gloves and performing hand hygiene.

5. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This report is the result of an unannounced standard-level Federal Recertification and State Re-licensure survey completed on January 23, 2026 at Bayada Home Health Care, Inc. It was determined the facility is not in substantial compliance with Federal requirements of 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies and State requirements of N.J.A.C. Title 8 Chapter 42 Home Health Agency Licensing Standards.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interview, and review of facility policies, it was determined the facility failed to ensure acceptable infection prevention standards of practice were implemented by; 1. Not following proper bag technique according to facility policy, in two of five home visits (Patient (P) 2 and P5), and 2. Not adhering to appropriate equipment disinfection protocols, according to facility policy, in two of six home visits (P6 and P7). 

Facility policy titled, "0-1570 Equipment & Supplies Maintenance," dated 01/01/24, stated, "… Our Procedure: 1.0 General Information. ... 1.3 Contact time is the length of time that the disinfectant must remain wet on the object or surface to effectively disinfect it. Clinical research supports contact time for each product; contact times will vary from product to product and will be noted on the product Requirements for Use (RFUs) … 2.0 Cleaning Procedures for Non-critical, Semi-critical, and Critical Items. ... 2.1 Non-critical Items ... 2.1.2 Client care/assessment items: Client care and assessment items … such as bandage scissors, stethoscopes, and blood pressure cuffs should be disinfected after client use before returning to the supply bag … These items can be disinfected with 70% alcohol … or a germicidal wipe. The solution must be allowed to completely dry prior to returning items to the supply bag …"

The "Sani-Cloth Germicidal Disposable Wipe" RFU, was reviewed and stated, "DIRECTIONS FOR USE: … TO DISINFECT AND DEODORIZE HARD, NONPOROUS SURFACES: … Unfold wipe and thoroughly wet surface. Allow surface to remain wet for two (2) minutes. Let air dry. …"

On 01/22/26 at 10:36 AM, Staff (S)12 was observed conducting a home visit for P7.

At 11:35 AM, S12 had his/her stethoscope positioned with the headset and ear tubes around his/her neck and the bell dangling loosely on his/her chest. As S12 repositioned P7 in the bed, the bell of the stethoscope was observed making contact with P7’s Foley catheter bag (indwelling urinary catheter), P7’s linens, and P7’s barrier pad.

At 11:37 AM, S12 used a Sani-Cloth germicidal disposable wipe to clean the stethoscope and placed it on a clean barrier to dry.

At 11:38 AM, S12 placed the stethoscope back in the supply bag (one minute of contact time).

At 12:30 PM, an interview was conducted with S12. S12 stated, he/she does not typically wear the stethoscope around his/her neck after vital signs are completed. S12 stated, he/she was unaware that the stethoscope bell made contact with P7’s bed and Foley catheter bag. S12 stated, he/she was unsure of the contact time for the Sani-Cloth wipes. S12 stated, he/she usually cleans vital signs equipment as soon as he/she is finished using it and gives it time to dry while performing other tasks with the patient. S12 stated he/she was not aware that the stethoscope only had one minute of contact time before being returned to his/her supply bag.

On 01/23/26 at 1:15 PM, an interview was conducted with S4. When asked about contact time for Sani-Cloth wipes, S4 stated equipment should air dry for at least 2.5 minutes after the Sani-Cloth wipe is used. S4 stated, one minute of contact time would not be long enough.

Findings include:

Facility Policy titled, "0-1314 Bag Technique," dated 03/25/25 stated, "… Our Procedure: ... 6.0 Bag Technique Procedure ... 6.3 Keep the bag closed when not in use … 6.5 Open the bag, remove all needed items from the bag … 6.6 Close bag … 6.8 When care is complete, disinfect items with an EPA-registered disinfectant wipe … Place items on a clean barrier until dry …"

1. On 01/21/26 at 3:02 PM, Staff (S) 8 was observed conducting a home visit for Patient (P) 2.

At 3:09 PM, S8 was observed hanging his/her bag on P2’s kitchen chair. After entering his/her clinical bag, S8 left the clinical bag unzipped. The bag was observed to be left unzipped throughout the entire home care visit.

At 3:54 PM, an interview was conducted with S8. When asked whether the bag should be left unzipped after removing any patient equipment needed, S8 stated, "I always leave it open."

2. On 01/22/26 at 9:01 AM, S10 was observed conducting a home visit for P6.  

At 9:04 AM, S10 placed two clean barriers onto P6’s side table. S10 was observed placing a tablet and a mobile cellular phone onto a clean barrier. The surveyor did not observe S10 disinfecting the mobile cellular phone or the tablet prior to placing them onto the clean barrier. The barrier was thus considered potentially contaminated.

At 9:38 AM, S10 was observed removing the tablet and the mobile cellular phone from the potentially contaminated barrier. 

At 9:39 AM, S10 was observed disinfecting the reusable equipment used on P6 (thermometer, Pulse Oximeter, and an automatic Blood Pressure monitor with cuff) and placed each equipment piece onto the potentially contaminated barrier, thus potentially re-contaminating the cleaned equipment. 

At 10:07 AM, an interview was conducted with S10. When discussing the observation made regarding the tablet and mobile cellular phone being removed off a barrier and then clean equipment placed on that same barrier to dry, S10 stated that he/she will be sure to be mindful of clean versus dirty barriers during future home visits.

On 01/23/26 at 1:15 PM, an interview was conducted with S4. When asked about a mobile cellular phone being placed on a clean barrier, S4 stated that the barrier would then be considered dirty and a new barrier would be needed for equipment to dry. 

On 01/22/26 at 10:10 AM, Staff (S) 6 was observed conducting a home visit for P5. After entering his/her clinical bag, S6 left the clinical bag unzipped. The clinical bag remained unzipped throughout the entire home visit. 

At 10:58 AM, S6 was asked if the bag should be zippered when not in use, S6 responded stating, "I was never told it had to be kept zippered." 

On 01/23/26 at 1:15 PM, an interview was conducted with S4. S4 explained that the clinical bag should always be closed throughout the entire visit.

NJAC 8:42-12.2(b)

Written notice for non-covered care
CFR(s): 484.50(c)(8)
Receive proper written notice, in advance of a specific service being furnished, if the HHA believes that the service may be non-covered care; or in advance of the HHA reducing or terminating on-going care. The HHA must also comply with the requirements of 42 CFR 405.1200 through 405.1204.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, facility document review, and review of medical records, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that all patients with Medicare coverage received a “Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage (NOMNC),” in six of six discharged Medicare patients (Patients (P) 13, P14, P15, P16, P17, and P18). 

Findings include:

Facility Policy titled, "0-322 Home Health Change of Care Notice (HHCCN), Advanced Beneficiary Notice of Non-Coverage (ABN), Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage (NOMNC) and Fast Track Appeal Review Procedures," dated 01/01/25, stated, "… Our Procedure: … 3.0: Notice of Medicare Noncoverage (NOMNC). 3.1: A standardized Review Notice, NOTICE OF MEDICARE NON-COVERAGE (NOMNC), #0-3195, is given on paper or electronically, to all beneficiaries when Medicare coverage is about to end based on the physician’s orders and all home healthcare is ending, (except those admitted to a facility or hospital) no later than two (2) days prior to discharge … 3.2: The Initial Notice of Medicare Provider Non-Coverage is delivered as follows: a. Face to face and signed and dated by the client and representative, b. If the Initial Notice of Medicare Provider Non-Coverage cannot or will not be signed, a notation is made on the notice explaining why and dated …"

On 01/23/26, a review of P13, P14, P15, P16, P17, and P18’s medical records was conducted and revealed the following: 

On 07/31/25, P13 was discharged from Home Care services. P13’s medical record lacked evidence of a signed NOMNC. 

On 10/23/25, P14 was discharged from Home Care services. P14’s medical record lacked evidence of a signed NOMNC. 

On 10/15/25, P15 was discharged from Home Care services. P15’s medical record lacked evidence of a signed NOMNC. 

On 11/11/25, P16 was discharged from Home Care services. P16’s medical record lacked evidence of a signed NOMNC. 

On 10/10/25, P17 was discharged from Home Care services. P17’s medical record lacked evidence of a signed NOMNC. 

On 09/09/25, P18 was discharged from Home Care services. P18’s medical record lacked evidence of a signed NOMNC. 

On 01/23/26 at 1:44 PM, Staff (S) 1 confirmed that the medical records for P13, P14, P15, P16, P17, and P18 lacked evidence of a signed NOMNC form. When asked if these patients should have signed a NOMNC form prior to discharge, S1 reported that P13, P14, P15, P16, P17, and P18 should have signed a NOMNC form prior to discharge and a copy should be in their medical record.

Communication with all physicians
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(1)
Standard: Coordination of Care. The HHA must: 
(1) Assure communication with all physicians or allowed practitioners involved in the plan of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interview, and review of facility policy, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that staff communicate with the physician when a missed visit occurs, in three of eight active medical records reviewed (Patient (P) 6, P9, and P12).

Findings include:

Facility policy titled, "0-6277 Missed Visits/Hours," dated 03/24/23, stated, "… Our Procedure: 1.0 Communicating Missed Visits/Hours. 1.1 Physician Ordered Services. The physician must be notified when the plan of care is altered due to fewer visits … being provided as ordered … 1.1.1 Documentation – Home Health and Hospice Offices. … 1.1.1.1 A Missed Visit Notification note to capture the reason that the visit was missed as well as evidence that the physician was informed … must be entered in the electronic record. 1.1.1.2 Missed Visit Process Flow. The field clinician is responsible for documenting the missed visit in the "Missed Visit Coordination Note" … 1.1.1.2.1 The Missed Visit Coordination Note will include the following: … c. Method of notification to physician …"  

A review of P6's medical record was conducted and revealed the following:

P6’s Plan of Care Orders for the certification period beginning 10/02/25 contained a physician order for the Home Health Aide (HHA) as "… Frequency/Duration of Visits: ... HHA Effective 10/05/2025 1WK7 [one visit a week for seven weeks] …"

For the week of 10/12/25 through 10/18/25, P6’s medical record lacked evidence that P6 received a HHA visit as per order and that the physician was notified of the missed visit. 

A review of P9's medical record was conducted and revealed the following:

P9’s Plan of Care Orders for the certification period beginning 11/29/25 contained a physician order for the HHA as "… Frequency/Duration of Visit: ... HHA Effective 11/30/2025 1WK6 [one visit a week for six weeks] …" 

For the week of 12/21/25 through 12/27/25, P9’s medical record lacked evidence that P9 received a HHA visit as per order and that the physician was notified of the missed visit. 

A review of P12's medical record was conducted and revealed the following:

P12’s Plan of Care Orders for the certification period beginning 12/25/25 contained a physician order for the HHA as "… Frequency/Duration of Visits: ... HHA Effective 12/28/2025 1WK5 [one visit a week for five weeks] …"

For the week of 12/28/25 through 01/03/26 and 01/04/26 through 01/10/26, P12’s medical record lacked evidence that P12 received HHA visits as per order and that the physician was notified of the missed visit.     

On 01/23/26 at 1:49 PM, an interview was conducted with Staff (S) 1. S1 stated that the physician should be notified when a missed visit occurs and the notification should be documented in the electronic medical record. S1 confirmed that the medical records for P6, P9, and P12 lacked the appropriate missed visit documentation and notification to the physician.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
This is a Federal Allegation Survey (#NJ00140737) conducted on May 9 and 10, 2021 at Holy Redeemer Home Care NJ North to investigate 42 CFR Condition of Participation for Home Health Agencies 484.58: Discharge Planning and 484.60: Quality Assessment/performance improvement.

Standard level deficiencies were identified. 

In addition, a Federal COVID-19 Focused Infection Control Audit survey was conducted on May 9 and 10, 2021, and Holy Redeemer was found to be in compliance.

Contents of clinical record
CFR(s): 484.110(a)
Standard:  Contents of clinical record.  The record must include:

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, review of facility policy and procedure, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that documentation in the medical record is accurate according to the facility policy. 

Reference: Facility policy titled, "Contents of Clinical Record" states, "... Policy: ... The clinical record will contain ...., accurately document care provided .... Procedure: ... K. Notes for each service provided, indicating date, ...."

1. On 6/9/21, at 11:50 AM, a review of Medical Record #1 was conducted with Staff #4 and the following was revealed:

a. The document titled, "Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage" is an information form provided to all patients forty-eight (48) hours prior to their discharge to inform the patient of their rights if they would like to appeal the discharge. 

(i) The statement: "The Effective Date Coverage of Your Current Home Health Services Will End:" is printed at the top of the document with a designated space for the facility to write in the patient's discharge date. 

(ii) The discharge date written on the document is: 10/12/20.

(iii) Patient #1's discharge date was: 10/15/20. 

2. Staff #4 confirmed Patient #1's discharge date was inaccurately documented on the document at the time of review.

Other pertinent instructions
CFR(s): 484.60(e)(4)
Any other pertinent instruction related to the patient's care and treatments that the HHA will provide, specific to the patient's care needs.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, review of three (3) of five (5) Medical Records (#1, #3, and #5), and review of facility documentation, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that written discharge instructions are provided to the patient and available in the medical record.     

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "Contents of Clinical Record" states, "...Procedure: 1. The following information will be available in the clinical record, as applicable to care and services provided: ...Y. Any instructions given to the patient, if discharged..."

Reference #2: Facility document titled, "[Facility Name] Home Care Discharge Instructions" states, "Part 1 - Clinical Records Part 2 - Patient Copy."

1. On 6/9/21, at 11:50 AM while reviewing Medical Record #1, with Staff #4, the following was revealed: 

a. On 10/15/20, Patient #1 was discharged from the agency. 

(i) Medical Record #1 did not contain a copy of written discharge instructions provided to the patient.

2. On 6/10/21, between 10:12 AM and 10:53 AM, during medical record review, the following was revealed:

a. On 9/2/20, Patient #3 was discharged from the agency. 

(i) Medical Record #3 did not contain a copy of written discharge instructions provided to the patient.

b. On 11/10/20, Patient #5 was discharged from the agency. 

(i) Medical Record #5 did not contain a copy of written discharge instructions provided to the patient.

3. At 10:20 AM, Staff #4 confirmed that the written "[Facility Name] Home Care Discharge Instructions" are provided to patients during their discharge visit and the Clinical Records Copy is returned to the office to be scanned into the patient's medical record.

4. Staff #4 confirmed the above findings during review of medical records.

(2) Testing. The [facility] must conduct exercises to test the emergency plan annually. The [facility] must do all of the following:



(i) Participate in a full-scale exercise that is community-based every 2 years; or

 (A) When a community-based exercise is not accessible, conduct a facility-based functional exercise every 2 years; or

	(B) If the [facility] experiences an actual natural or man-made emergency that requires activation of the emergency plan, the [facility] is exempt from engaging in its next required community-based or individual, facility-based functional exercise following the onset of the actual event.

(ii) Conduct an additional exercise at least every 2 years, opposite the year the full-scale or functional exercise under paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this section is conducted, that may include, but is not limited to the following:

(iii) Analyze the [facility's] response to and maintain documentation of all drills, tabletop exercises, and emergency events, and revise the [facility's] emergency plan, as needed.

Content of the comprehensive assessment
CFR(s): 484.55(c)
Standard: Content of the comprehensive assessment. 

The comprehensive assessment must accurately reflect the patient's status, and must include, at a minimum, the following information:

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, medical record review, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to document a complete set of vitals signs with each patient visit in three (3) out of four (4) medical records (#3, #6, #7) reviewed.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, titled: “Client Assessment and Reassessment” states: “…2.0 Assessment Principles.  A comprehensive assessment gives Registered Nurses and Therapists insight into a client’s status through:  a. Observation  b. measurement of vital signs  c. the client’s self-reported symptoms… 6.3.2.1  Vital signs: Vital signs must be taken and recorded into HCHB (Home Care Home Base) during every skilled nurse and therapy visit. Vital Signs include blood pressure, temperature, pulse, respiratory rate with breath sounds, and pulse oximeter reading…..”

1. An interview with Staff #1 on 9/15/2021 at 1:41 PM confirmed that a complete set of vital signs should be assessed and documented for each clinician visit. A complete set of vital signs would include pulse, blood pressure, temperature, respiratory rate, and pain level.

2. The medical record of Patient #3 was reviewed. The following was identified:

a. On 4/21/2021, the physical therapist did not document the respiratory rate, the pulse oximetry, and the temperature of the patient.

b. On 4/27/2021, the physical therapist did not document the respiratory rate, the pulse oximetry, and the temperature of the patient.

c. On 4/29/2021, the physical therapist did not document pulse, blood pressure, temperature, the pulse oximetry, and the respiratory rate.

3. The medical record of Patient #6 was reviewed. The physical therapist failed to document the patient’s respiratory rate on the following dates: 7/27/2021; 7/29/2021; and 8/18/2021.

4. The medical record of Patient #7 was reviewed. The physical therapist failed to document the patient’s respiratory rate and pulse oximetry on the following dates: 9/1/2021; 9/3/2021; 9/8/2021; and 9/14/2021.

5. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1, Staff #2, Staff #4, and Staff #11 on 9/15/2021 at 2:30 PM.

Conformance with physician orders
CFR(s): 484.60(b)
Standard: Conformance with physician or allowed practitioner orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of one (1) of three (3) medical records (#4, #5), staff interviews, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the agency failed to ensure that services ordered by the physician are provided, as indicated in the patient's plan of care.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, "Client Care Plan" states, "... The individualized plan of care based on the client's medical diagnosis, physician's order, comprehensive assessment and client input must include the following elements... c. The types of services, supplies and equipment needed... d. The frequency and duration of visits to be made... ."

Reference #2: Facility policy, "Missed Visits/Hours" states, "... Physician Ordered Services... The physician must be notified when the plan of care is altered due to fewer visits or hours of service being provided as ordered. Notification of the missed visits/hours is timely, and as directed on a schedule determined in collaboration with the physician. ... Missed Visit Process Flow... Field clinician is responsible for documenting the missed visit in the "Missed Visit Coordination Note" found in the electronic record. The Missed Visit Coordination Note will include the following: a. Date missed visit occurred... b. Reason for missed visit... c. Method of notification to physician (verbal or fax)."

1. Review of Medical Record #4 on 9/15/21, revealed the following:

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care for start of care (SOC) date 8/18/21 states, "Frequency/Duration of Visits... HHA Effective 8/22/21 2WK3" (twice a week for three weeks).

i. For week 8/22/21 to 8/28/21, one (1) HHA visit was made. The missed visit note dated 8/28/21 states, "Reason for Missed Visit: Add visit to following week. Method of Physician Notification: Notified RN and CM." There was no evidence that the physician was notified.

ii. For week 9/5/21 to 9/11/21, one (1) HHA visit was made. There was no evidence of missed visit note indicating the reason for the missed visit. There was no evidence that the physician was notified.

b. Upon interview at 1:43 PM, Staff #1 confirmed the HHA missed visits for Patient #4. 

c. Upon interview at 2:00 PM, Staff #1 confirmed that "Add visit to the following week" was not an acceptable justification for a missed visit.

2. Review of Medical Record #5 on 9/15/21, revealed the following: 

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care for start of care (SOC) date 8/19/21 states, "Frequency/Duration of Visits... OT 1WK5 (Occupational Therapy once per week for five weeks)."

b. Physician's order dated 9/9/2021 at 1:14 PM states, "Client would benefit from additional OT visits for shower transfer training." 

i. The updated Home Health Certification and Plan of Care, frequency of visits for OT states, "Effective 09/12/2021,1Q2WK2 (once every two weeks for two weeks), 1WK1 (once a week for one week)." The frequency of OT visits does not indicate an increase in the amount of OT visits as indicated by the physician's order.

3. Upon interview on 9/15/21 at 2:00pm, Staff #1 confirmed the OT visits were not increased for Patient #5.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation of infection control practices during two (2) of three (3) home visits, staff interviews, and review of facility policies and procedures, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that hand hygiene occurs in accordance with acceptable standards of practice, and failed to ensure that aseptic technique is maintained while performing patient care.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Hand Hygiene" states, "... Indications for Hand Decontamination... b. Before applying and after removing gloves or other personal protective equipment. c. Between contact with the environment and the client (medical equipment, bedside tables, personal cell phone) in the immediate vicinity of the client before moving to another task."

1. During a home visit for Patient #1, on 9/13/21, the following was observed:

a. At 1:16 PM, Staff #3 placed two barriers on a table, then placed his/her bag on one of the barriers. 

b. At 1:52 PM, while Staff #3 was taking Patient #1's blood pressure, a cat climbed onto the table and sat on the empty barrier. After approximately twenty (20) seconds, the cat jumped off the table.

c. At 1:55 PM, Staff #3 used a Sani-wipe to clean his/her stethoscope, thermometer, pulse oximeter, and blood pressure cuff. Staff #3 placed the clean equipment on the barrier contaminated by the cat.

2. During a home visit for Patient #5, on 9/14/21, the following was observed:

a. At 1:20 PM and 1:28 PM, Staff #5 failed to perform hand hygiene prior to donning gloves.

3. Staff #1 and Staff #2 confirmed the above findings on 9/15/21 at 12:30 PM.

If home health aide services are provided to a patient who is receiving skilled nursing, physical or occupational therapy, or speech-language pathology services, a registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional who is familiar with the patient, the patient's plan of care, and the written patient care instructions described in §484.80(g), must make an onsite visit to the patient's home no less frequently than every 14 days. This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Conformance with physician orders
CFR(s): 484.60(b)
Standard: Conformance with physician orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of two (2) of four (4) medical records, review of facility policy and procedures, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that services ordered by the physician are provided as indicated in the plan of care.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, Client Care Plan, states, "[Name of Agency] develops and implements an individualized plan of care for/with each client. ... 1.1. Actions and interventions are consistent with the care plan and are documented. ... ."

Reference #2: Facility policy, Missed Visits/Hours, "... The physician must be notified when the plan of care is altered due to fewer visits or hours of service being provided as ordered. ... field clinician is responsible for documenting the missed visit in the "Missed Visit Coordination Note" found in the electronic record. The Missed Visit Coordination Note will include the following: a. Date missed visit occurred... b. Reason for missed visit... c. Method of notification to physician (verbal or fax). ... ."

1. Upon review of Medical Record #4 on 9/27/18, the following was noted: 

a. The patient was admitted to the agency on 8/30/18. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care for the certification period from 8/30/18 to 10/28/18, states, "Skilled nurse (SN) to assess for pain, report changes to physician as needed and provide instruction regarding pain control, including pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods."

i. A SN visit report dated 9/3/18 indicated that the nurse was performing a PRN (as needed) visit. The patient's caregiver reported that the patient fell during the night and complained of pain to the toes bilaterally.

ii. The SN visit report indicated that the pain was "new." The visit report states, "Client reported having pain to his/her bilateral foot rating pain on the left foot 6 on a scale of 1-10 and 3 on the right. Also verbalized having pain on the right thigh."

iii. There was no evidence that the changes to the patient's pain level was reported to the physician.

iv. There was no evidence of pain management interventions provided for the patient.

v. There was no evidence that the patient was instructed on pain control methods.

b. The visit frequency order for the certification period from 8/30/18 to 10/28/18, states, "SN 1wk1 (once per week for 1 week), 2wk1 (twice per week for 1 week), 1wk2 (once per week for two weeks)."

i. For the week 9/2/18 to 9/8/18, there was one (1) SN visit and one (1) SN PRN visit made. The visit frequency order indicated that two (2) SN visits were ordered. 

c. Upon interview, Staff #1 confirmed that PRN visits are additions to the visit frequency order and do not take the place of regular visits.

2. Upon review of Medical Record #5 on 9/27/18, the following was noted: 

a. The patient was admitted to the agency on 8/21/18. The visit frequency order for the certification period from 8/21/18 to 10/19/18, states, "SN 2wk3 (twice per week for three weeks), HHA (home health aide) 1wk1, 2wk2 (once per week for one week, twice per week for two weeks)."

i. For the week 8/26/18 to 9/1/18, there was only one (1) SN visit made. The visit frequency order indicated that two (2) SN visits were ordered.

b. On 9/4/18, the physician entered an order change for HHA visits that stated, "Add HHA 2wk2 (twice a week for two weeks)." The effective date of the service change was 9/2/18.

i. For the week 9/9/18, there was no evidence of HHA visits.

ii. For the week 9/16/18 to 9/22/18, there was no evidence of HHA visits.

3. Staff #1 and Staff #7 confirmed the above findings.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility policy and procedure, and staff interview, it was determined that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to ensure that their infection prevention and control policies were implemented. 

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, Bag Technique, states, "... Carry the bag into the home and place it on a clean, dry, hard surface ... Keep bag closed when not in use ... When care is complete, disinfect items ... place items on a clean barrier until dry ..."

1. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 9/27/18, the following was observed:

a. Staff #11 entered the patient's home, placed a barrier on a cushioned chair, and then placed the nursing bag on the barrier.

b. Staff #11 proceeded to place a barrier on the dining room table and placed a personal hand bag on the barrier. Staff #11then placed equipment next to the personal hand bag.

i. Staff #11 removed the hand bag from the barrier. Staff #11 cleaned equipment, then placed the equipment on the barrier, where the hand bag had been, contaminating the equipment.

c. After pulling out equipment, Staff #11 did not close the nursing bag.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #5.

 

3. During a home visit of Patient #1 on 9/26/18, the following was observed:

a. Staff #6 used a stethoscope, pulse oximeter, and blood pressure cuff during an assessment of the patient's vital signs.

b. At the end of the visit, Staff #6 placed the stethoscope, pulse oximeter, and blood pressure cuff into his/her bag without first cleaning the items.

4. Staff #1 and Staff #7 confirmed the above finding.

Integrate all services
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(3)
Integrate services, whether services are provided directly or under arrangement, to assure the identification of patient needs and factors that could affect patient safety and treatment effectiveness and the coordination of care provided by all disciplines.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, medical record review, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that services are integrated to identify patient needs and factors that could affect patient safety and treatment effectiveness.

Findings include:

1. During a home visit of Patient #1 on 9/26/18, the following was observed:

a. The patient was admitted to the agency on 9/24/18. Staff #6 was evaluating the patient for therapy services. Upon interview, the patient disclosed to Staff #6 that he/she has problems getting to his/her doctor's appointments.

i. The patient stated that he/she has a sibling that can sometimes take him/her to appointments, but otherwise does not have reliable transportation. He/she stated that transport vans are not an option because they do not assist patients, and he/she needs assistance ambulating and getting on and off the van. 

b. Staff #6 indicated to the patient that he/she would follow up with the clinical manager to discuss how the patient could be helped.

c. Review of Medical Record #1 on 9/27/18 lacked evidence of a clinical note by Staff #6 documenting the patient's difficulty with transportation to doctor's appointments.

i. The medical record lacked documentation that Staff #6 notified the clinical manager, social worker, or physician about patient's needs.

2. Staff #1 and Staff #7 confirmed the above findings.

Ongoing interdisciplinary assessment of the patient;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, review of facility policy and procedure, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure sharing of information between nursing, therapy services, and the physician.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, Pain Assessment and Management, states, "When pain is assessed as a problem or not being managed effectively, goals and interventions will be established in collaboration with the client and physician as follows: a. Skilled services: Nurse or therapist will communicate the client's status to the physician ..."

 

1. Upon review of Medical Record #7, the following was noted:

a. On 8/27/18, the Physical Therapist performed a pain assessment. 

i. The patient's pain level was assessed as six (6).

ii. The patient's pain was not being managed to the patient's satisfaction.

iii. The therapist contacted the nurse regarding the pain medication. 

b. On 9/05/18, the Physical Therapist performed a pain assessment. 

i. The patient's pain level was assessed as four (4).

ii. The patient's pain was not being managed to the patient's satisfaction.

iii. The therapist discussed the pain complaint with the nurse. 

2. The patient's pain status was never communicated to the physician.

3. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1.

Standard: Conformance with physician orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:

Reference: Facility policy, Missed Visits/Hours states, "... The physician must be notified when the plan of care is altered due to fewer visits or hours of service being provided as ordered. ... Field clinician is responsible for documenting the missed visit in the "Missed Visit Coordination Note" found in the electronic record . ... Justification for missed visit/hours is documented on a Coordination of Services (COS) note... ."

1. Review of Medical Record #7 on 2/28/18 revealed the following:

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care for certification period 1/14/18 to 3/14/18 states, "Frequency/Duration of Visits: SN (skilled nurse): 3wk1 (3 times per week for 1 week), 2wk1 (two times per week for 1 week), 1wk1 (once a week for 1 week)... OT (occupational therapy): 1wk1 (once a week for 1 week)."

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on observation, review of facility policies and procedures, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that infection prevention practices were in accordance with the Centers for Disease Control's (CDC) recommendations and the facility's policy.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, Bag Technique states, " ... 6.4 Decontaminate hands with alcohol based waterless hand gel or antimicrobial soap and water prior entering the bag. ... ."

Reference #2: Guideline for Hand Hygiene in Health Care Settings: Recommendation of the Healthcare Infection Control Practices Advisory Committee and the ICA/SHEA/APIC/IDSA Hand Hygiene Task Force, published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report at MMWR 2002; 51 (No. RR-16) states, "... Recommendations: 1. Indications for Handwashing and Hand antisepsis... C. Decontaminate hands before having direct contact with patients... F. Decontaminate hands after contact with a patient's intact skin... G. Decontaminate hands after contact with... a patient's nonintact skin... I. Decontaminate hands after contact with inanimate objects... in the immediate vicinity of the patient... J. Decontaminate hands after removing gloves. ... ."

1. During a home visit for Patient #4 on 2/27/18, the following was observed:

a. While performing a dressing change to the patient's left leg, Staff #5 donned and doffed gloves multiple times without hand sanitizing between glove changes.

b. Staff #5 donned gloves and began to clean the patient's leg wound. While wearing the same gloves, Staff #5 reached into a box to retrieve additional supplies for the patient, then returned to the patient.

i. Staff #5 did not discard his/her gloves or hand sanitize prior to retrieving clean supplies or prior to returning to the patient.

2. Staff #3 and Staff #4 confirmed the above findings.

 

3. During a home visit on 2/27/18, after patient contact, Staff #7 reached into his/her supply bag to retrieve gloves. 

a. Staff #7 failed to decontaminate his/her hands prior to re-entering the supply bag. 

4. At 12:35 PM, Staff #7 donned gloves and proceeded to examine and touch the patient's left foot wound. 

a. Staff #7 failed to perform hand hygiene prior to donning gloves. 

5. Staff #2 confirmed the above findings.

B. Based on observation, review of facility policy and procedure, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to implement its policy and procedure for the handling, storage, cleaning and disinfecting of point of care devices.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, Infection Control Procedures for Point of Care Devices states, "... Our Procedure... 5.1 Disinfect the point of care device and stylus with manufacturers approved hospital grade disinfectant wipe or alcohol wipe after each client or caregiver interaction with device (i.e. signature using finger or stylus); before returning to supply bag; and more frequently as needed. ... ."

1. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 2/28/17, Staff #7 was observed using a facility issued tablet (electronic device). 

a. At 12:24 PM, Staff #7 placed the tablet on the patient's side table. 

b. Staff #7 proceeded to assess the patient by checking his/her pulse rate and auscultating heart and lungs with a stethoscope. 

i. Staff #7 repeatedly picked-up the tablet, touched the surface of the tablet to document, then touched the patient. 

ii. Staff #7 failed to disinfect the tablet after each interaction with the device. 

c. At 1:15 PM, Staff #7 touched the surface of the tablet to schedule the next visit. 

i. Patient #2 signed by gliding a finger on the surface of the device. 

ii. Staff #7 did not disinfect the device before or after patient use. 

d. Upon interview, Staff #7 stated that devices are cleaned with alcohol swabs, however he/she uses an "electronic spray cleaner."

2. Staff #3 confirmed the above findings.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Initial Comments - Not A Deficiency Citation
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
A Federal Recertification survey was conducted on July 10, 11, and 12, 2018 resulting in Standard level deficiencies.

Medical Records Reviewed: 9

Home Visits Made: 5

Staff interviews conducted: 10

Plan of care
CFR(s): 484.60(a)(1)
Each patient must receive the home health services that are written in an individualized plan of care that identifies patient-specific measurable outcomes and goals, and which is established, periodically reviewed, and signed by a doctor of medicine, osteopathy, or podiatry acting within the scope of his or her state license, certification, or registration. If a physician refers a patient under a plan of care that cannot be completed until after an evaluation visit, the physician is consulted to approve additions or modifications to the original plan.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and document review, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure implementation of policies regarding the provision of patient care in accordance with the plan of care and physician orders. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, "Physician Orders," states, "...A. The plan of care is established by the patient's physician in conjunction with the nurse... B. Any changes to the plan of care are sent to the physician... ."

Reference #2: Facility policy, "Coordination of Patient Care," states,"...POLICY: CRITERIA: A. The primary nurse is designated to coordinate services provided to the patient/client by the home care organization..... D. Casual relief and other qualified staff members provide care in the absence on the primary staff member assigned to a patient..... E. Patients and/or families are notified regarding changes in staff assignment and visit schedule is [sic] far in advance of the scheduled visit as possible... ."

1. Patient #2 began Home Health Services on 6/21/18. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care stated, "SN [skilled nursing]: ... 6/21/2018 to 8/19/2018: 1 to 2 visits as needed wound care C/P complications 6/24/2018 - 6/30/2018: 1 visit every week for 1 week." 

a. On 7/13/18, a review of the medical record of Patient #2 revealed that during the week of 6/24/18 to 6/30/18, three (3) skilled nursing visits were made. However, the visit of 6/26/18 and 6/29/18 were documented as "PRN" [as needed] visits. These visits were scheduled visits for wound care and not additional PRN visits. 

b. There was no evidence that the nursing staff obtained a new set of orders for the visits made.

(i) There was no evidence that the physician was notified. 

c. The above was confirmed with Staff #4. 

2. Patient #4 began Home Health Services on 6/7/18. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care stated, "HHA [home health aide]: 6/7/2018 to 8/4/2018: 1 to 3 visits every week for 9 weeks."

a. On 7/11/18, a review of the medical record of Patient #4 revealed that home health aide services began on 6/13/18 (2nd week) and not during the first week. 

(i) There was no evidence that the physician or the patient were notified.

b. The above was confirmed with Staff #4.

3. Patient #9 began Home Health Services on 6/16/18. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care stated, "SN: 6/16/2018 to 8/11/2018: 1 to 3 visits every week for 9 weeks" and "PT [physical therapy]: 6/18/2018 to 7/14/2018: 1 to 3 visits every week for 4 weeks."

a. On 7/12/18, a review of the medical record of Patient #9 revealed that the last skilled nursing visit was performed on 6/27/18. At that time, the nurse documented that the patient did not need skilled nursing services.

(i) There was no evidence that the physician was notified regarding the discontinuation of skilled nursing visits.

b. On 6/25/18, 6/26/18 and 6/28/18 the patient canceled physical therapy visits. 

(i) There was no evidence that the physician was notified regarding the missed visits. 

c. The above was confirmed with Staff #4. 

4. Patient #5 began Home Health Services on 6/6/18. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care stated, "MCH [maternal child health]: SN: 6/6/2018 to 6/16/2018: 1 to 2 visits every week for 2 weeks."

a. On 7/11/18, a review of the medical record of Patient #5 revealed that a nursing visit was performed on 6/6/18. At the end of the visit, the nurse documented, "Will follow up on infant feeding and wt [weight] status next visit."

b. There was no evidence of any additional skilled nursing visits.

c. There was no evidence that the physician was made aware of the missed skilled visits.

d. The above was confirmed with Staff #4.

5. Patient #7 had a start of care [SoC] to the Home Health Agency on 6/17/18 for a need for skilled nursing services for wound care.

a. On 7/12/18, a review of the medical record of Patient #7 revealed that there was an order for skilled nursing visits to occur from the SoC on 6/17/18, for the frequency of 1 - 3 visits per week for the duration of 9 weeks.

b. The medical record of Patient #7 lacked evidence of the missed skilled nursing visit for the week of 6/24/18 - 6/30/18.

c. The medical record of Patient #7 lacked evidence that the physician was notified of the missed skilled nursing visit. 

d. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #4.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation and document review, it was determined that the facility failed to follow the accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, when practicing hand hygiene.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Hand Hygiene With and Without Water," states, "...Purpose: Hand hygiene is a critical component of patient and employee safety..... Policy: ...hand disinfection is proven to be the singlemost effective procedure in preventing the spread of infections. For hand disinfection to be effective in ridding hands of transient pathogenic microorganisms the following measures must be taken... 7. Hand hygiene must be performed; but not limited to: -Before and after each patient contact -Before entering and re-entering nursing bag -Before using the computer... -Before donning gloves -After removing gloves and or after each glove change... ."

1. On 7/11/18, a home visit of Patient #3 by Staff #8 was observed in the presence of Staff #6. The following was noted:

a. At 9:48 AM, Staff #8 entered the nursing bag to gather supplies, then re-entered the bag two additional times for supplies without performing hand hygiene before each entrance into the bag.

b. At 9:53 AM, Staff #8 went into the computer bag and removed the computer to place on a clean barrier without performing hand hygiene prior to entering into the computer bag.

c. At 10:01 AM, Staff #8 was noted assisting Patient #3 with adjusting the patient's bilateral lower extremity compression stockings without the use of gloves. Patient #3 was noted to have a visibly soiled dressing to the left knee that Staff #8 touched while adjusting the compression stocking. No hand hygiene was performed after the direct patient contact.

d. At 10:13 AM, Staff #8 assisted Patient #3 with coming to a standing position by placing his/her hands on Patient #3's back. Staff #8 then assisted Patient #3 walking by placing his/her hands on Patient #3's hips. Staff #8 then returned to the computer to write notes without performing hand hygiene.

e. At 10:32 AM, Staff #8 donned gloves and then used a Sani-Wipe to clean the stethoscope and the blood pressure cuff. A second Sani-Wipe was used to clean the computer, then the gloves were removed.

(i) There was no hand hygiene performed prior to the donning of the gloves.

Integrate all services
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(3)
Integrate services, whether services are provided directly or under arrangement, to assure the identification of patient needs and factors that could affect patient safety and treatment effectiveness and the coordination of care provided by all disciplines.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and document review, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure the implementation of the coordination of the patient care policy.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Coordination of Patient Care," states, "...PURPOSE: A. The agency coordinates services by referring patients to appropriate community and professional resources. III. POLICY: CRITERIA: A. ...In the event that nursing is not ordered, the therapist is designated as the coordinator..... C. When more that one service is provided to the patient/client... the actions and goals of the individual services are complimentary and reflect cooperative care plan. 1) Ongoing communication is maintained with patients/caregivers... All communication is documented in the medical record....."

1. A home visit was made on 7/11/18 for Patient #3. Patient #3 was receiving therapy services for increasing strength.

a. Patient #3 was noted stating he/she was anxious with trying to walk after he/she had fallen that past weekend.

b. Staff #8 was noted to be emotionally and physically supportive with Patient #3 in assisting him/her to walk. 

2. An interview with Staff #8, in the presence of Staff #6, at the conclusion of the home visit revealed that a referral had been made for Patient #3 to see psychiatry regarding his/her anxiety.

a. Staff #8 was not certain about the date and time in which the referral was made.

b. Staff #8 was not certain if the referral had been completed, and, if it had, what the outcome was.

3. A review of the medical record of Patient #3 revealed that Staff #11 noted on 6/21/18, in the Intervention Documentation for Depression, that "Pt (patient) has referral to psychiatry and psychology for depression and anxiety."

a. The medical record lacked evidence regarding who the referral was with, and if the referral had been completed.

4. Staff #4 and Staff #6 agreed with the above findings.

Patients receive education and training
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(5)
Ensure that each patient, and his or her caregiver(s) where applicable, receive ongoing education and training provided by the HHA, as appropriate, regarding the care and services identified in the plan of care.  The HHA must provide training, as necessary, to ensure a timely discharge.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and document review, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure the implementation of ongoing education for emergency preparedness as reflected in the care plan. 

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Emergency Management Plan," states, "...POLICY: A. ...Potential emergency or risk factors will be identified for each patient and appropriate emergency plans discussed with the patient and/or caregiver at the time of admission during a comprehensive assessment, and thereafter on revisits....."

1. On 7/12/18, seven (7) medical records were reviewed for emergency preparedness assessment and planning.

a. 4 out of 7 medical records reviewed noted the care plan for emergency preparedness was addressed and resolved at the Start of Care [SoC] for Patient #1, Patient #3, Patient #7, and Patient #8. 

b. 1 out of 7 medical records reviewed noted that the care plan for emergency preparedness was addressed and resolved less than one week later for Patient #9.

c. There was no emergency preparedness care plan noted for Patient #2.

d. An interview with Staff #3 and Staff #9 revealed that emergency preparedness education and evaluation was ongoing, and that the care plans for patients regarding emergency preparedness should remain open till the patient is discharged from the Home Health Agency. 

2. Staff #3 and Staff #9 confirmed the above findings.
