Based on staff interview, review of two (2) out of five (5) medical records on 9/9/21 and 9/10/21 and review of facility documents, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that their policy and procedure for missed visits is implemented.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Missed Visits" states, "... Procedure ... 2. If a visit is missed and not rescheduled the clinician will: A. Notify the physician ... B. Document in the patient's clinical record the following information: ... 4. Description of any unmet needs and how the patient's needs were met 5. Physician notification including date, time, physician name, method of notification and the staff reporting the information ..."

1. A review of Medical Record #6, with Staff #2, revealed the following:

a. For certification period 6/14/21 - 8/12/21, the Home Health Certification and Plan of Care states, ".... SN (Skilled Nursing), 6/6/21 1-2 x 1 week (one to two times for one week) ..."

b. Review of SN visits for the week of 6/6/21 revealed that no SN visits were conducted, in accordance with the plan of care.

(i) The Skilled Nursing Note by the Registered Nurse (RN) in the "Charts/Clinical Notes" section of the medical record dated 6/7/21 stated, "... Patient stated [he/she] will call the agency once [he/she] is settled ... and ready to resume services. ... Team communication sent to the clinical team with patient update."

(ii) The documentation by the RN did not specify if physician notification was made and did not include the date, time, physician name, the method of notification and the staff reporting the information. This is not in accordance with the facility policy and procedure.

2. A review of Medical Record #8, with Staff #2, revealed the following:

a. For certification period 5/25/21 - 7/23/21, the Home Health Certification and Plan of Care states, ".... AID (Home Health Aid), 6/20/21 2-3 x week x 2 weeks (two to three times a week for two weeks) ..."

b. Review of AID visits for the week of 6/27/21 revealed that only one (1) AID visit was conducted, in accordance with the plan of care.

(i) The Home Health Aid Note by the AID in the "Charts/Clinical Notes" section of the medical record, dated 6/30/21 stated, "Per ... RN this morning - this patient no longer needs the aide so ... visits have been canceled effective today 6/30/21."

(ii) The medical record did not contain documentation by the RN of physician notification of the missed visit which includes the date, time, physician name, and method of notification. A description of how the patient's needs were met was also not documented by the clinician. This is not in accordance with the facility policy and procedure.

3. The above findings were confirmed on 9/10/2021 by Staff #2.

N.J.A.C. 8:42 - 6.2(a)6

source_record.Facility Name: Hunterdon Medical Center Home Health Services
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interview, and a review of facility documents during 3 of 3 home visits, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure A.) nursing staff implement proper bag technique procedures and B.) staff perform hand hygiene according to facility policy and the Visiting Nurse Associations of America (VNAA) Clinical Procedure Manual.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "Home Health Bag Technique" states: "... II. Procedure A. The bag may have the following contents: 1. Hand washing equipment -- alcohol-based hand rub and skin cleanser, soap, and paper towels ... D. Bag Technique 1. The bag is placed on a clean barrier in the home. ... and should be placed out of reach of children and pets. ... 2. Prior to administering care, ... waterless skin cleanser and paper towels are removed and hand hygiene is performed. These supplies are left available for hand hygiene at the end of the visit. ... 4. When the visit is completed, re-usable equipment is cleaned using agency approved germicidal wipe, ..."

Reference #2: The Visiting Nurse Associations of America 19th Edition VNAA Clinical Procedure Manual Section 7: Infection Control Procedure 7.4 Bag technique states, "Key Points ... 2. Keep bag clean and dry ... d. Place the bag in a barrier in a "clean" area of the home: 1) Appropriate areas include a clean hard surface ... e. Keep the bag away from ..., pets ..."

1. On 9/8/21, during entrance conference, Staff #1 indicated that the facility follows the following nationally recognized guidelines and clinical procedures for infection control: CDC (Centers for Disease control and Prevention), VNAA (Visiting Nurse Association of America), and WHO (World Health Organization).

2. On 9/8/21, during an observation of Patient #1's home visit conducted by Staff #3 and Staff #4, the following was observed:

a. At 12:29 PM, Staff #3 placed his/her clinician bag on the seat of a chair located in the kitchen. The patient was observed to have a pet dog at the time of arrival that was present multiple times in the kitchen during the visit.

(i) At 12:50 PM, while Staff #3 and Staff #4 were providing care to the patient, the pet was observed standing on its hind legs with two paws placed on the clean barrier and then proceeded to touch/sniff several areas on the outside of the bag with its nose. The bag was closed at the the time of the observation.

b. At 12:38 PM, Staff #4 arrived to the patient's home. Staff #4 was observed to place his/her clinician bag on a barrier on the seat area of a soft surfaced leather like material chair located in the patient's dining room area.

c. At 1:10 PM, Staff #4 was observed sitting on the barrier placed on the kitchen chair where Staff #3's bag was placed. While sitting, Staff #4's back was observed touching the outside surface of Staff #3's clinician bag.

3. On 9/9/21 at 10:38 AM, during an observation of Patient #5's home visit conducted by Staff #6 and Staff #7, the following was observed:

a. Prior to administering care, Staff #6 removed supplies from his/her bag which included waterless skin cleanser, paper towels, and 2 electronic devices and placed them onto the clean barrier. Staff #6 then proceeded to apply the waterless skin cleanser to a paper towel and was then observed wiping down the 2 electronic devices with the paper towel containing the waterless skin cleanser and then placing them back onto the clean barrier.

(i) Staff #7 indicated on interview during the visit that the one phone device on the barrier was a facility issued electronic device that is utilized by the Home Health Aids (HHAs).

(ii) After completion of the visit an interview was conducted with Staff #1 regarding the cleaning and disinfection techniques for facility issued electronic phone devices. Staff #1 explained that Super Sani Cloth wipes or alcohol wipes are utilized for the cleaning and disinfection of facility issued electronic devices, not waterless skin cleanser.

4. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #1 on 9/10/21.

N.J.A.C. 8:42-12.2 (b)

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "Home Health Hand Hygiene" states: "1. Policy Personnel providing care in the home setting will follow the visiting Nurse Association of America Clinical Procedure manual for Hand Hygiene. ..."

Reference #2: The Visiting Nurse Associations of America 19th Edition VNAA Clinical Procedure Manual Section 7: Infection Control Procedure 7.8 Hand Hygiene states, "Key Points ... 7. Hand hygiene must be performed: a. Before entering/re-entering the clinician bag ... Procedure ... 2. Hand washing Soap and Water ... f. use towel to turn off faucet. ..."

1. On 9/8/21 at 12:38 PM, during an observation of Patient #1's home visit, Staff #3 was observed to entered his/hers clinician bag without first performing hand hygiene.

2. On 9/9/21 at 10:38 AM, during an observation of Patient #5's home visit, Staff #6, upon arrival to the home was observed to wash his/hers hands in the kitchen sink using soap and water. Staff #6 did not used his/hers clean hands, not a towel, to turn off the faucet when complete. Staff #6 then proceeded to re-wash his/her hands at the sink with soap and water and again was not observed to use a towel to turn off the faucet.

3. The above findings were confirmed on 9/10/21 with Staff #1.

N.J.A.C. 8:42-12.2 (b)

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy titled, "Home Health Hand Hygiene" states, "... Procedure: 1. .... Adhere to standard precautions. Perform hand hygiene. .... 3. Establish a clean field .... with all the supplies and equipment that will be necessary. 4. Don gloves. 5. ... Remove soiled dressing. 6. Discard dressing and gloves .... 7 . Perform hand hygiene and don clean gloves. 

1. On 9/9/21 during an observation of Patient #4's home visit conducted by Staff #9, the following was observed: 

a. At 10:20 AM, Staff #9 removed Patient #4's  wound dressing with gloved hands, retrieved multiple 4x4 gauze from a clean supply packet without removing his/her dirty gloves and performing hand sanitizing.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Home Health Aide Assignments And Duties
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Home health aide assignments and duties
CFR(s): 484.80(g)(1)
Standard:  Home health aide assignments and duties. 

Home health aides are assigned to a specific patient by a registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional, with written patient care instructions for a home health aide prepared by that registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional (that is, physical therapist, speech-language pathologist, or occupational therapist).

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff and family interviews, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure a copy of the home health aide plan of care is maintained in the patient's home. 

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy titled, "Home Health Certified Home Health Aide Plan of Care and Supervision" states, "... II Procedure: ... G. A current copy of the CHHA [Certified Home Health Aide] plan of care will be maintained in the patient's home. ..."

1. On 9/9/2021 at 8:05 AM, during a visit to Patient #3's home while conducting an observational visit for certified home health aide services, the following was revealed:

a. At 8:15 AM, while observing Staff #8 perform care to the patient, an inquiry to Patient #3's spouse was made regarding how the patient and/or spouse knows what the home health aide's assigned responsibilities are to be performed.  The spouse presented a form titled, "Patient Care Plan," which has individual sections for the different assigned staff disciplines to complete with information related to that discipline's service/treatment for the the patient. 

(i) Documented in the "Home Health Aide" section was: "For Personal Care and assistance with activities of daily living." 

b. At 8:20 AM, upon request, Staff #8, the certified home health aide, confirmed he/she uses his/her phone to view the details of the current home health aide care responsibilities assigned specific for the patient. 

(i) Staff #8 confirmed the care plan the aide reviews for his/her assigned responsibilities is from the agencies program 'NetSmart' that details the patient-specific assigned responsibilities for the aide to provide care.    

 c. At 8:40 AM,  the spouse confirmed, he/she does not exactly know what [name of Staff #8] is suppose to do, but that Staff #8 assists with ADLs [activities of daily living] and stated, "I don't ask [her/him] to do laundry."   

2. On 9/10/2021 at 11:10 AM, during review of Medical Record #3 with Staff #1 and Staff #11, the following was revealed:

a. Upon request, the current assigned home health aide's care plan/responsibilities for patient #3 was provided and included twenty-two (22) detailed responsibilities with correlating visit frequencies.

(i) There was no provided evidence a copy of the aide's assigned responsibilities were provided or maintained in the patient's home. 

3. Staff #1 and Staff #11 confirmed the above findings at the time of review. 

N.J.A.C. 8:42 - 7.5(a)(2)(i)

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Promptly alert relevant physician of changes
CFR(s): 484.60(c)(1)
The HHA must promptly alert the relevant physician(s) or allowed practitioner(s) to any changes in the patient's condition or needs that suggest that outcomes are not being achieved and/or that the plan of care should be altered.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interview and facility document review, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that all revisions to the plan of care be authorized and incorporated in an updated plan of care.  

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "Home Health Monitoring Patient's Response Reporting to Physician" states, "...II Procedure: ... D. All conferences or attempts to communicate with the physician will be documented in the clinical record. ..."

Reference #2: Facility policy titled, "Home Health Care Planning Process" states, "... I. Policy: The patient plan of care will be developed or revised within five (5) working days of initiation of each service or of the reassessment of the patient. ... III Procedure: ... J. Clinicians will inform the patient's physician of any changes that suggest a need to alter the plan of care. Changes must be written, dated, and signed by the professional making the changes."...

1. On 9/9/2021 at 1:15 PM during a review of Medical Record #2 with Staff #1 and Staff #11, the following was revealed:  

a. For Certification Period: 7/27/21 - 9/24/21, the 'Home Health Certification and Plan of Care" included the following physician orders: "SN [Skilled Nursing] 7/27/21 3 PRN [as needed]: pleurx complications, 8/1/21: 2-3 x week x 2 weeks" ... RN [registered nurse] perform Pleural catheter site care/sterile dressing change/connection-detachment of sterile Pleural vacuum system .... frequency and drainage amount .... Instruct Pt/CG [patient/caregiver] in sterile Pleural vacuum system connection/detachment regimen. Teach Pt/CG Pleural catheter insertion site care and dressing change to Pleural catheter insertion site ..."

(i) On 8/6/2021 at 3:18 PM, Staff #10 documented routine visit note in "Chart/Clinical Notes"...Pt's husband (name) comfortable with draining PleurX and changing dressing 2x/wk [week]. They would like RN [registered nurse] to continue to come 1x/wk for drainage/dressing change and to monitor incision site. ..."  

b. There was no documented evidence in the medical record that Staff #11 communicated with the physician the need for skilled nursing visits to be revised from 2-3 x/week to 1x / week for the plan of care. 

(i) There was no documentation to reflect the plan of care was revised for the nursing visit frequencies or a signed and dated authorization was made by the professional authorizing the changes within (5) working days of initiation of the revision. 

2. At 2:00 PM, Staff #1 and Staff #11 confirmed the above findings. 

N.J.A.C. 8:42 - 7.4(a)(1)

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
COMPLIANCE W/ ACCEPTED PROFESSIONAL STD
CFR(s): 484.12(c)
The HHA and its staff must comply with accepted professional standards and principles that apply to professionals furnishing services in an HHA.     




This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility documents and staff interviews, it was determined

that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to maintain acceptable standards of principals to assure prevention of infection. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: The facility protocol for "Skin and Wound Care-Wound Care: Dressing Application" stated, "...Procedure ... 6. Discard dressing and gloves in appropriate containers. ... 12. Discard soiled supplies in appropriate containers. ..."

Reference #2: The facility protocol for "Infection Control-Visit: Generated Waste" stated, "...Key Points ...4. Medical waste: ...b. Examples include old dressings with drainage, paper towels used to wipe blood spills and diapers. ... Procedure... Medical waste disposal ... b. Prepare a plastic bag to dispose of items contaminated with blood, excrement, bodily fluids (e.g., dressings, diapers, etc.) as then are removed. c. After care completed, close bag securely. ... e. Throw in household trash. ..."

Reference #3: The facility policy and procedure "Nursing Bag Techniques" stated, " ...Policy: The principals in bag technique are developed and utilized to maximize the efficient use of the bag and to assure asepsis and the prevention of infection. ...Procedure: Nursing Bag: 1. Contents of the nursing bag may include but not limited to: ... C. Disposable Supplies-paper measuring tapes, sterile and non-sterile gloves, dressings, ..."

1. During a home visit of Patient #5 on January 23, 2018, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #4 provided wound care on the second (2nd) toe of the patient's right foot. 

(i) Staff #4 removed a band-aid dressing with drainage from the second (2nd) toe on the right foot, and placed the soiled dressing inside of his/her dirty gloves. He/she then placed the dirty gloves with the dressing inside, on the patient's recliner chair without the use of a barrier. The dressing was not disposed of as per Reference #1. 

(ii) Staff #4 cleansed the wound on the second (2nd) toe of the right foot and after drying the wound with a 4 x 4 gauze, he/she placed the 4 x 4 gauze on the patient's recliner chair without the use of a barrier. The dressing was not disposed of, as per Reference #1. 

 

(iii) Staff #4 proceeded to dispose of the soiled dressings and gloves, in the patient's trash can, not in a plastic bag, as per Reference #2.

(iv) Staff #4 obtained a paper measuring tape from the counter in the home, and proceeded to measure the second (2nd) toe wound. Once the wound was measured, Staff #4 placed the disposable paper measuring tape back on the counter. The paper measuring tape is considered a disposable supply as per Reference #3, and was not disposed of. 

b. Wound care of the left heel "scab" was observed: 

(i) Staff #4 removed the dressing from the left heel and placed the dirty dressing on the patient's recliner chair without the use of a barrier. The dressing was not disposed of as per Reference #1. 

(ii) Staff #4 proceeded to dispose of the soiled dressings and gloves, in the patient's trash can, not in a plastic bag, as per Reference #2.

2. During a home visit of Patient #4 on January 24, 2018, the following was observed:

a. Staff #5 completed wound care on the right below the knee stump. 

(i) Staff #5 removed the wound dressing from the right below the knee stump, completed wound care and proceeded to dispose of the medical waste in the patient's trash can. Staff #5 did not place the medical waste in a prepared plastic bag, as per Reference #2.

(ii) Staff #5 obtained a paper measuring tape from the counter in the home, and proceeded to measure the right below the knee stump wound. Once the wound was measured, Staff #5 maintained the disposable paper measuring tape to measure another wound. The paper measuring tape is considered a disposable supply as per Reference #3, and was not disposed of. 

(iii) Staff #5 removed the wound dressing from the left foot, completed wound care and proceeded to dispose of the medical waste in the patient's trash can. Staff #5 did not place the medical waste in a plastic bag, as per Reference #2. 

(iv) Staff #5 proceeded to measure wounds on the left foot. Once the wound was measured, Staff #5 placed the disposable paper measuring tape back on the counter. The paper measuring tape is considered a disposable supply as per Reference #3, and was not disposed of. 

3. Staff #7 confirmed that the disposable measurement tape is meant to be disposed of. He/she also confirmed that wound dressings that are draining per facility protocol, are considered medical waste and should be placed in a plastic bag, secured and then placed in patients trash can.

4. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2, Staff #3 and Staff #7.

source_record.Facility Name: Hunterdon Medical Center Home Health Services
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
COORDINATION OF PATIENT SERVICES
CFR(s): 484.14(g)
All personnel furnishing services maintain liaison to ensure that their efforts are coordinated effectively and support the objectives outlined in the plan of care.  




This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on document review and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to maintain a liaison to ensure that efforts are coordinated effectively and support the objectives outlined in the plan of care for all personnel furnishing services to the patients.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled "Internal Referral Process" states, "Policy ... 2. For required Nutrition Consultation services, the Registered Dietician will respond to the referral within (7) days of referral or earlier if warranted by patient condition ....."

Reference #2: Facility job description titled "Clinical Dietitian" states, " ...Position Summary Plans, organizes, directs, coordinate and evaluated the nutrition component of the department's services. Primary Position Responsibilities 1. Provide nutritional screening, assessment, monitoring, follow-up and documentation on all home health patients ..... 4. Provides in-home assessments and education based on department policies and procedures ....." 

1. The start of care for Patient #7 was 11/27/17 for a diagnosis of Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), muscle cramps, contracture of the joint of the left hand, and repeated falls. Patient #7 was identified with the following needs upon the start of care, by Staff #14 on 11/28/17, "SN OASIS C2" document:

a. Homebound status for poor coordination and dependent with activities of daily living (ADLs).

b. Overall status notes that the patient has serious progressive conditions that could lead to death within a year.

c. expresses simple ideas or needs with moderate difficulty

d. Unable to feed self and must be assisted or supervised throughout the meal/snack.

e. Unable to prepare any light meals or reheat any delivered meals.

f. Nutritional assessment noted appetite good, and compliance with prescribed diet was not evaluated.

2. A Skilled nursing visit was made on 12/1/17 and Staff #12 identified the following issues as noted in the "AN NURSING OASIS C2" routine visit note:

a. Dependent with ADLs

b. Registered Dietician (RD) referral made: Meal preparation/Food Record

3. On 12/1/17, a referral was made for a registered dietician consult by Staff #12 in regards to Patient #7.

4. On 12/4/17, a clinical note written by Staff #4 indicated, "(the patient) has not finished food record yet" and would "f/u (follow-up) food record"

a. There was no further note regarding nutrition education on this visit.

5. On 12/7/17, it was noted in the clinical notes from the "GREEN Quad Interdisciplinary Meeting" that an RD evaluation was still pending.

6. On 12/8/17, a clinical note written by Staff #4 indicated "(the patient) has not finished filling out food record"

a. There was no further plan noted on this visit to follow-up with the food record.

b. There was no further note regarding nutrition education on this visit.

7. On 12/21/17, a clinical note was entered in Patient #7's medical record by Staff #13, a dietician. 

a. The clinical note for Patient #7 indicated the following plan:

(i) Recommend completion of food record for intake evaluation

(ii) Maintain weight and safe swallow

b. The clinical note written dated 12/21/17 by Staff #13, did not indicate a coordination with other disciplines regarding Patient #7's nutritional plan.

c. The clinical note did not indicate that an in-home nutritional assessment for Patient #7 was completed by Staff #13.

d. The clinical note did not indicate that in-home nutritional education took place with Patient #7.

(i) Staff #2 confirmed that Staff #13 does not do in-home assessments with patients.

8. Staff #13 saw Patient #7 twenty (20) days after the referral was made. Per facility policy, the registered dietician was to respond to the referral within seven (7) days. 

9. There was no evidence in Medical Record #7 that a follow-up nutritional assessment was made by Staff #13.

10. Staff #2 and Staff #7 agreed with the above findings.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
EXERCISE OF RIGHTS AND RESPECT FOR PROP
CFR(s): 484.10(b)(5)
The HHA must investigate complaints made by a patient or the patient's family or guardian regarding treatment or care that is (or fails to be) furnished, or regarding the lack of respect for the patient's property by  anyone furnishing services on behalf  of the HHA, and must document both the existence of the complaint and the resolution of the complaint. 




This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on a review of facility policy, review of the facility complaint log, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to follow its complaint/ grievance policy. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, Patient/Family/Visitor/Complaint and Grievance Process states, "... II. Definitions: ... C. A 'patient grievance' is a written or verbal complaint ... by a patient, or the patient's representative, regarding the patient's care ... issues related to PCHS's compliance with the CMS Conditions of Participation (CoP), a Medicare beneficiary billing complaint related to rights and limitations provided by 42 CFR 489. All the following are considered grievances: a. A billing issue that is a result of a care or treatment issue will be considered as a grievance under this policy and therefore complaint management staff should be contacted to log complaint and follow up as per procedure... IV: Procedure: ... C. Grievance: 1) Complaint management staff at each business unit will acknowledge in writing all written complaints/grievances within seven calendar days of receipt. Responsible chairmen, directors and/or managers will receive copies of the complaints/grievances as entered into complaint database. a. Any complaint or grievance regarding another business unit, which directed to the Office of Patient Relations will first be directed to the responsible parties for investigation at that unit, will be logged into the Patient Relations database and followed up on as per procedure..." 

1. On 1/25/18 at 10:00 AM, an interview with Staff #1 revealed the following:

a. Patient #1 was admitted to the facility's service on 8/22/17, and was discharged on 11/15/17. 

b. On 11/15/17, the facility erroneously discharged the patient from homecare service as "deceased."

c. On 12/18/17, the facility became aware of this mistake and immediately contacted their contracted billing company, to make necessary billing amendments. 

d. Staff #1 stated this incident was not treated as a complaint/grievance as it was not related to the care or service provided during admission.

2. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #2. 

Reference #2: Facility policy titled, Patient/Family/Visitor/Complaint and Grievance Process states, "IV. Procedure: ... C. Grievance: ... 6) Complaint management staff will respond to the complainant within 30 days of receipt of the grievance. The response will include 1) the steps taken on behalf of the patient/family/visitor/resident to investigate the grievance, 2) the results of the investigation, 3) the corrective action plan, if applicable."

1. A review of facility document conducted on 1/25/18, revealed the following:

a. On 12/18/17, the facility received a telephone call from the patient's family member, complaining that the patient was upset because his/her Medicare and prescription benefits were canceled and was erroneously marked as "deceased" upon discharge.

b. On 12/20/17, the facility's contracted billing company, sent a letter to the patient acknowledging the mistake and informing the patient that corrections were submitted to Medicare to update the patient's status.

 

c. On 1/12/18, an email correspondence from a representative from the contracted billing company, to the patient's family member, indicated that as of 1/11/18, "the date of death was corrected in the Medicare system."

d. On 1/25/18, a review of "The MVP (Medicare Eligibility Verification) Coverage Detail Report," provided by the contracted billing company, indicated that as of 1/25/18, the Date of Death was still listed as 11/15/2017.

2. The facility failed to provide the patient a documented response to include; steps taken to investigate the grievance, results of the investigation and any corrective actions taken, as per policy. 

3. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #1 and Staff #2.

CFR(s): 484.60
Condition of participation: Care planning, coordination of services, and quality of care.

Patients are accepted for treatment on the reasonable expectation that an HHA can meet the patient's medical, nursing, rehabilitative, and social needs in his or her place of residence.  Each patient must receive an individualized written plan of care, including any revisions or additions. The individualized plan of care must specify the care and services necessary to meet the patient-specific needs as identified in the comprehensive assessment, including identification of the responsible discipline(s), and the measurable outcomes that the HHA anticipates will occur as a result of implementing and coordinating the plan of care.  The individualized plan of care must also specify the patient and caregiver education and training. Services must be furnished in accordance with accepted standards of practice.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interviews, medical record review, and review of facility documents, it was determined that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to ensure that patients are accepted for treatment on the reasonable expectation that the HHA can meet the patient's medical, nursing, rehabilitative, and social needs in his or her place of residence. 

Findings include: 

1. The HHA failed to ensure that patients receive home health services that are written in the individualized plan of care. (G572)

2. The HHA failed to ensure that patient services are in conformance with physician's orders. (G578)

source_record.Facility Name: Penn Medicine Home Health Princeton Health
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Skilled professional services
CFR(s): 484.75
Condition of participation: Skilled professional services.

Skilled professional services include skilled nursing services, physical therapy, speech-language pathology services, and occupational therapy, as specified in §409.44 of this chapter, and physician and medical social work services as specified in §409.45 of this chapter. Skilled professionals who provide services to HHA patients directly or under arrangement must participate in the coordination of care.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interviews, medical record review, and review of facility documents, it was determined that the Home Health Agency failed to ensure that patients receive skilled professional services of a physical therapist to meet the patient's rehabilitative needs. 

Findings include: 

1. The HHA failed to ensure that skilled professional services of a physical therapist are available to all patients. (G702)

2. The HHA failed to ensure that skilled professional services of a physical therapist are delivered according to physicians orders. (G710)

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
This is a Federal Recertification Survey and a State Relicensure Survey conducted on May 26, 2021 to May 28, 2021. Penn Medicine Princeton Home Health is not in compliance with N.J.A.C. Title 8 Chapter 42 - Licensing Standards for Home Health Agencies and Penn Medicine Princeton Home Health is not in compliance with 42 CFR Part 484 regulations for Home Health Agencies. Condition level and Standard level deficiencies were identified. The following Conditions were determined to be out of compliance:

484.65: Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement

484.70: Infection Prevention and Control 

A Focused Infection Control Audit was conducted on May 26, 2021 to May 28, 2021, deficiencies were identified.

source_record.Facility Name: Penn Medicine Home Health Princeton Health
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Quality assessment/performance improvement
CFR(s): 484.65
Condition of participation: Quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI).



The HHA must develop, implement, evaluate, and maintain an effective, ongoing, HHA-wide, data-driven QAPI program. The HHA's governing body must ensure that the program reflects the complexity of its organization and services; involves all HHA services (including those services provided under contract or arrangement); focuses on indicators related to improved outcomes, including the use of emergent care services, hospital admissions and re-admissions; and takes actions that address the HHA's performance across the spectrum of care, including the prevention and reduction of medical errors. The HHA must maintain documentary evidence of its QAPI program and be able to demonstrate its operation to CMS.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and document review, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure the evaluation and maintenance of their Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) program.

Findings include:

1. The facility failed to ensure that the home health agency selects the indicators that will be utilized in its Quality Assurance Performance Improvement (QAPI) program. (Refer to Tag G-0642).

2. The facility failed to ensure that the effectiveness of the facility's QAPI program was monitored. (Refer to tag G-0644).

3. The facility failed to ensure that performance improvement preventative measures were implemented as a result of adverse events. (Refer to tag G-0654)

source_record.Facility Name: Penn Medicine Home Health Princeton Health
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection prevention and control
CFR(s): 484.70
Condition of Participation: Infection prevention and control.

The HHA must maintain and document an infection control program which has as its goal the prevention and control of infections and communicable diseases.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, observation, medical record review, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure the maintenance of an infection control program.

Findings include:

1. The facility failed to ensure that contact precautions are maintained in accordance with acceptable standards of practice. (Refer to tag G-0682).

2. The facility failed to ensure a barrier was maintained to limit contamination in a patient care area. (Refer to tag G-0682).

3. The facility failed to ensure that a qualified person is designated for infection prevention and control responsibilities. (Refer to Tag G-0684).

4. The facility failed to ensure an accurate COVID-19 patient screening prior to the scheduled visit. (Refer to Tag G-0684).

5. The facility failed to ensure that visitors entering the agency's office were screened for COVID-19. (Refer to Tag G-0684).

source_record.Facility Name: Penn Medicine Home Health Princeton Health
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Program scope
CFR(s): 484.65(a)(1),(2)
Standard: Program scope. 

(1) The program must at least be capable of showing measurable improvement in indicators for which there is evidence that improvement in those indicators will improve health outcomes, patient safety, and quality of care.



(2) The HHA must measure, analyze, and track quality indicators, including adverse patient events, and other aspects of performance that enable the HHA to assess processes of care, HHA services, and operations.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, the facility failed to ensure that the home health agency selects the indicators that will be utilized in its Quality Assurance Performance Improvement (QAPI) program.

Findings include:

1. An interview on 5/27/2021 at 1:05 PM with Staff #3, a QAPI manager, identified the following:

(a) The home health agency coordinates with a parent company that incorporates home health, hospice, and caregivers within it's "umbrella." Staff #3 identified that the parent company/group determines the indicators that will be measured yearly for the home health agency and the hospice agency.

(b) Staff #3 stated that he/she monitors the adverse events at the facility and provides feedback to staff involved via email or at staff meetings if the adverse event is different than any of the current metrics that are assigned by the parent company to be monitored by the facility. 

2. On 5/28/2021 at 10:06 AM, an interview with Staff #3 confirmed that although the feedback is provided to staff, there is a lack of follow-up to determine if the feedback provided resulted in changes in the provision of care or in an improvement of outcomes. Staff #3 confirmed that these indicators are not measured due to the lack of follow-up.

3. Upon request to Staff #3 on 5/28/2021 at 10:06 AM, the facility was unable to provide evidence of a quality indicator that was chosen by the home health QAPI team based on specific identified issues occurring within the home health agency.

4. Upon request to Staff #3 on 5/28/2021 at 10:06 AM, the facility was unable to provide evidence of how the current metrics were chosen by the parent company to be monitored by the home health agency.

NJAC 8:42-14.2(b)

NJAC 8:42-14.2(c)

source_record.Facility Name: Penn Medicine Home Health Princeton Health
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Program data
CFR(s): 484.65(b)(1),(2),(3)
Standard: Program data.  

(1) The program must utilize quality indicator data, including measures derived from OASIS, where applicable, and other relevant data, in the design of its program.



(2) The HHA must use the data collected to-

(i) Monitor the effectiveness and safety of services and quality of care; and 

(ii) Identify opportunities for improvement.



(3) The frequency and detail of the data collection must be approved by the HHA's governing body.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and the review of pertinent facility documentation, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the effectiveness of the facility's quality assurance performance improvement (QAPI) program is monitored.

Findings include:

1. On 5/27/2021 at 1:05 PM, upon request to Staff #3, a QAPI manager, the facility's QAPI program was provided. It was identified that the facility's number of reported falls had a significant increase between the years 2019 and 2020. An interview with Staff #3 identified that the number of falls that were reported increased due to a newly implemented reporting system that was easier for clinicians to use. Staff #3 stated that education of this system was provided to clinicians and encouraged clinicians to report all levels of incidents from minor/no injury to major with injury.

2. The monitoring of the incident reporting system to determine if the clinicians were using the system correctly was requested of Staff #3 on 5/28/2021 at 9:54 AM. The facility was unable to provide the auditing and monitoring as requested. When asked how the facility was determining the education to clinicians was effective, Staff #3 stated: "I don't know."

3. On 5/27/2021 at 1:05 PM, an interview with Staff #3 was conducted and he/she stated that he/she monitors adverse events at the facility and provides feedback to staff involved via email or at staff meetings if the adverse event is different than any of the current metrics that are being monitored by the facility. On 5/28/2021 at 10:06 AM, an interview with Staff #3 confirmed the previous statement and also noted that although the feedback is provided to staff, there is a lack of follow-up and monitoring to determine if the feedback provided to staff resulted changes in the provision of care or in an improvement of patient outcomes. 

NJAC 8:42-14.2(c)

NJAC 8:42-14.2(d)(5)

Track adverse patient events
CFR(s): 484.65(c)(2)
Performance improvement activities must track adverse patient events, analyze their causes, and implement preventive actions.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:

source_record.Facility Name: Penn Medicine Home Health Princeton Health
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on review of CDC (Centers for Disease Control) Guidelines, observation of one (1) of five (5) home visits, medical record review, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that contact precautions are maintained in accordance with acceptable standards of practice. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: Centers for Disease Control (CDC) 2007 Guideline for Isolation Precautions: Preventing Transmission of Infectious Agents in Healthcare Setting (http://www.cdc.gov/hicpac/pdf/isolation/Isolation2007.pdf) states, "[page 72] Contact Precautions also apply where the presence of excessive wound drainage, fecal incontinence, or other discharges from the body suggest an increased potential for extensive environmental contamination and risk of transmission. ...Healthcare personnel caring for patients on Contact Precautions wear a gown and gloves for all interactions that may involve contact with the patient or potentially contaminated areas in the patient's environment. ...[page 88] Limit the amount of non-disposable patient-care equipment brought into the home of patients on Contact Precautions. Whenever possible, leave patient-care equipment in the home until discharge from home care services. ..." 

Reference #2: Facility policy titled, "Contact Precautions" states, " ...Diseases Requiring Contact Precautions ...MRSA (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus Aureus) infection ... Procedure for Patients Residing in the Community A. Precautions for Health Care Personnel 1. ...a. Gowns and gloves should be worn for procedures and patient care activities likely to generate splashes or sprays of body fluids. ... 4. If possible, a disposable stethoscope and blood pressure cuff should be dedicated to use on a single patient. ..."

1. On 5/26/2021, during a home visit for Patient #3, the following was observed:

a. At 1:27 PM, Staff #9, a Registered Nurse (RN), removed a blood pressure cuff and stethoscope from his/her bag and checked the patient's blood pressure. Staff #9 used alcohol wipes to clean the blood pressure cuff and stethoscope, then placed them back into his/her bag. A disposable stethoscope and blood pressure cuff was not used.

b. At 1:40 PM, Staff #9 performed a dressing change for a right buttock wound treated with Negative Pressure Wound Therapy. Staff #9 did not don a gown while providing any patient care, including the dressing change on the right buttock wound.

2. On 5/27/2021 at 1:15 PM, a review of Medical Record #3 contained the following documentation in the patient's Plan of Care: "Infection Control Precautions...Contact Precautions...[Each visit, Start 5/22/21] [Contact Precautions for MRSA (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) infection]." 

a. Upon interview, Staff #12, a manager, revealed that when patients are on isolation precautions, the staff providing home care services have available for use "specific kits with PPE (personal protective equipment)" which include a "gown, disposable stethoscope, disposable blood pressure cuff ..." 

b. On 5/28/2021 at 10:00 AM, Staff #2, an administrator, confirmed the RN should be following the "Plan of Care" for the patient, including Contact Precaution orders. 

3. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1, Staff #2, and Staff #12 at 12:35 PM. 

B. Based on observation of one (1) of five (5) home visits, staff interview, and review of Centers for Disease Control (CDC) guidelines, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure a barrier is maintained to limit contamination in a patient care area.

Findings include:

Reference: CDC 2007 Guideline for Isolation Precautions: Preventing Transmission of Infectious Agents in Healthcare Settings (http://www.cdc.gov/hicpac/pdf/isolation/Isolation2007.pdf), page 50 states, "During patient care, transmission of infectious organisms can be reduced by adhering to the principles of working from 'clean' to 'dirty', and confining or limiting contamination to surfaces that are directly needed for patient care."

1. On 5/26/2021 at 1:35 PM, during a home visit for Patient #3, Staff #9, a registered nurse (RN), was observed performing a dressing change on the patient's right buttock. Staff #9 set up two blue pads side by side on the patient's couch, next to the patient, and placed clean supplies on the pads.

a. Staff #9 removed a bottle of Curad cleanser from a bag of supplies located on the patient's couch, opened the bottle, and applied the contents to a gauze pad. The bottle of Curad was placed on the blue pad farthest from the patient. Staff #9 used the gauze pad to clean the patient's wound. 

b. At 1:50 PM, after Staff #9 replaced the dressing on the patient's right buttock, he/she wrapped up the dirty supplies in the blue pad closest to the patient, and disposed of the bundle in the garbage can. The bottle of Curad cleanser fell off the remaining pad and onto the patient's couch, with the cap off, and the nozzle where the contents are released laying against the seat of the couch. 

c. At 1:55 PM, Staff #9 replaced the cap on the bottle of Curad cleanser and placed it in the patient's bag of supplies. 

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1, Staff #2, and Staff #12 at 12:35 PM. 

C. Based on observation of two (2) of five (5) home visits, review of facility policy and procedure, and review of CDC (Centers for Disease Control) guidelines, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that alcohol-based hand rub is allowed to dry when decontaminating hands. 

Findings Include:

Reference: Guidelines for Hand Hygiene in Health Care Settings: Recommendation of the Healthcare Infection Control Practices Advisory Committee [HICPAC] and the HICPAC/SHEA/APIC/IDSA Hand Hygiene Task Force, published in the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report at MMWR 2002; 51 (No. RR-16) page 32 states, "... Recommendations ... 2. Hand-hygiene technique

A. When decontaminating hands with an alcohol-based hand rub, apply product to palm of one hand and rub hands together, covering all surfaces of hands and fingers, until hands are dry ... ."

1. On 5/26/2021, during a home visit for Patient #3, the following was observed:

a. At 1:33 PM, Staff #9, an RN, applied hand sanitizer and immediately reached inside his/her bag to retrieve a pack of alcohol wipes with hands visibly wet.

b. At 1:40 PM, Staff #9 removed his/her gloves, applied hand sanitizer, and immediately donned gloves with hands visibly wet.

c. At 1:46 PM, Staff #9 removed his/her gloves, applied hand sanitizer, and immediately donned gloves with hands visibly wet. Staff #9 stated, "It makes it difficult after hand sanitizer to put on gloves."

2. On 5/27/2021, during a home visit for Patient #4, the following was observed:

a. At 9:35 AM, Staff #13, an RN, applied hand sanitizer and immediately donned gloves with hands visibly wet. 

b. At 9:52 AM, Staff #13 applied hand sanitizer and immediately opened a Sterile Dressing Kit with hands visibly wet. Staff #13 then reapplied hand sanitizer and immediately donned sterile gloves with hands visibly wet. 

3. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1 and Staff #2, both administrators, on 5/28/2021 upon exit conference.

NJAC 8:42-12.2(b)(3)

NJAC 8:42-12.2(b)(6)(i)

NJAC 8:42-12.2(b)(6)(ii)

source_record.Facility Name: Penn Medicine Home Health Princeton Health
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection control
CFR(s): 484.70(b)(1)(2)
Standard: Control.  

The HHA must maintain a coordinated agency-wide program for the surveillance, identification, prevention, control, and investigation of infectious and communicable diseases that is an integral part of the HHA's quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program. The infection control program must include:



(1) A method for identifying infectious and communicable disease problems; and



(2) A plan for the appropriate actions that are expected to result in improvement and disease prevention.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on staff interview and review of facility personnel files, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that a qualified person is designated for infection prevention and control responsibilities.

Findings include:

1. On 5/26/2021, upon entrance, Staff #1, Director of Home Health, identified Staff #6 as the facility's designated Infection Control person.

2. Upon interview with Staff #6 on 5/27/2021 at 2:20 PM, Staff #6 stated that he/she was not aware that he/she was the day to day infection control professional at the home health agency and when he/she was told that Staff #1 had identified him/her in that role, Staff #6 asked: "What does that mean?"

3. On 5/28/2021 at 11:51 AM, upon review of the personnel file for Staff #6, the signed Job Description did not include a designation of the infection control role. Staff #6's personnel file did not contain any additional education or training for the infection control role.

4. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1 on 5/28/2021 at 11:55 AM. 

B. Based on staff interview, medical record review, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure an accurate COVID-19 patient screening prior to the scheduled visit in one (1) out of thirteen (13) medical records reviewed.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "FY [Fiscal Year] 2021 Infection Control Plan" states: "...OBJECTIVES 1. To establish the mechanism by which staff will address surveillance, prevention, identification, and control of infections..... Risk Priorities Minimize risk of COVID-19 infection to staff, patients, and families... Strategies to Achieve Goal ... -Standardize screening for COVID-19 on all patients who come onto the [facility] services ....."

Reference #2: Facility screening protocol titled, "Coronavirus Screening (updated version)" states: "Please ask the following when scheduling all patients: 1- Within the last 14 days, have you or anyone in your home had contact with a confirmed or suspected Coronavirus infection, including anyone who has had a coronavirus swab screening? If yes, escalate to a manager prior to scheduling 2-In the past 72hrs (hours) have you or anyone in your home had cough, shortness of breath, fever, chills, muscle pain, new loss of taste or smell, headache, congestion, runny nose, vomiting and/or diarrhea? if yes, escalate to a manager prior to scheduling ... ."

1. On 5/27/2021, the medical record of Patient #6 was reviewed and the following was identified:

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This was a Federal Recertification and State Re-licensure survey conducted at Amedisys Home Health on 9/26-28/2023, to determine compliance with 42 CFR Part 484 - Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies; and State requirements under Title 8, Chapter 42 - Home Health Agency Licensing Standards. Standard-level deficiencies were cited.

Conformance with physician orders
CFR(s): 484.60(b)
Standard: Conformance with physician or allowed practitioner orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on the review of three out of 17 medical records (Patient (P) 5, 8, and 9), and staff interview it was determined the facility failed to ensure that all services ordered by the physician are provided in accordance with the plan of care.

 

A review pf P8’s Plan of Care, for the Certification Period 9/6/23 through 11/4/23, indicated the following orders for social worker visits: “MSW [Medical Social Worker] Effective 09/10/2023 1WK1 [one visit each week for one week]”

P8’s medical record lacked evidence that a social worker visit was conducted. P8’s medical record lacked evidence of communication to the physician, or of an explanation of the missed visit.  This missed visit was confirmed by Staff (S)1 on 9/28/23 at 1:58 PM.

Findings include:

Facility document titled, "Section 7 - Scheduling", revised date 9/13/23, states, "...Missed Visits  All missed visits must be communicated to the physician...Visits - Touchpoints. Standard of Practice for Missed Visits. Touchpoints Missed - Any touchpoint missed must be explained in the patient record. [Facility name] standard of practice is that missed touchpoints should be rare, for patient related reasons only, and must be explained in the patient record. …" 

On 9/28/23, a review of Patient (P)5’s Plan of Care, for the Certification Period 8/25/2023 through 10/23/2023, indicated the following orders for home health aide visits: “HHA [Home Health Aide] Effective 8/27/23 1WK3 [one visit each week for three weeks]."

For the week of 9/10/23, P5’s medical record lacked evidence that a home health aide visit was conducted. P5’s medical record lacked evidence of communication to the physician, or of an explanation of the missed visit.

A review of P9’s Plan of Care, for the Certification Period 8/15/2023 through 10/13/2023, indicated the following orders for skilled nursing visits: “SN [Skilled Nurse] 2WK1 [two visits each week for one week], 1WK2 [one visit each week for two weeks] 8/28/23 - SN [Skilled Nurse] 2WK1 [two visits each week for one week], 1WK4 [one visit each week for four weeks.]"

For the week of 9/17/23, P9’s medical record lacked evidence that a skilled nursing visit was conducted. P9’s medical record lacked evidence of communication to the physician, or of an explanation of the missed visit.

The above findings were confirmed by S1 at 12:20 PM. 

N.J.A.C. 8:42-6.2(a)(6)

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation during home visits of four of four patients (Patient (P)2, P4, P6, and P7), staff interview, and facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that 1.) re-useable equipment is decontaminated after each use; 2.) re-usable equipment is cleaned in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Findings include:

Facility policy "Decontamination of Re-usable Equipment", last review date 6/20/23, states, "...Procedure: …3.  Non-critical items (i.e., blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, stethoscopes, flashlights and scales etc.) should be cleaned with 70% isopropyl alcohol or an agency approved, single use disinfectant wipe after each use and before placing the equipment back in the supply bag. …"

On 9/26/23 at 2:33 AM, during a home visit of Patient (P)2, Staff (S)9 was observed entering the patient's home while carrying a tablet in his/her hands. At 3:10 PM, at the conclusion of the visit, S9 provided the tablet to P2, and the patient used his/her finger to sign the tablet. S9 tucked the tablet under his/her arm, provided hand sanitizer to P2, and then sanitized his/her own hands. S9 then placed the tablet inside his/her supply bag. The tablet was not cleaned following contact with the patient and before placing it back into the bag. 

N.J.A.C. 8:42-12.2(b)(6)

Facility policy and procedure titled, “Hand Hygiene” (reviewed 6/20/23), stated “…GUIDELINES: …4. Perform hand hygiene as follows: a. Before having direct contact with patients. b. Before donning gloves. …d. After contact with a patient’s intact skin. …g. After contact with inanimate objects (e.g., medical equipment) in the immediate vicinity of the patient. …”

On 9/26/23 at 2:11 PM, during a home visit of P4, S5 (Physical Therapist) was observed taking the tablet out of his/her bag and using it to document the patients’ vital signs throughout the visit.  At 2:54 PM, at the conclusion of the visit, S5 provided P4 with hand sanitizer and then provided the tablet to P4, and the patient used his/her finger to sign the tablet. S5 then placed the tablet in his/her supply bag. The tablet was not cleaned following contact with the patient and before placing it back into the bag.

 

On 9/27/23 at 12:20 PM, during a home visit of P6, S6 (Registered Nurse) was observed taking the tablet out of his/her bag and using it to document during the patient’s treatment session. At 12:50 PM, at the conclusion of the visit, S6 provided the tablet to P6, and the patient used his/her finger to sign the tablet. S6 then carrier the tablet out of the patients home. The tablet was not cleaned following contact with the patient.

 

On 9/28/23 at 10:20 AM, during a home visit of P7, S10 (Registered Nurse) was observed taking the tablet out of his/her bag and using it to document during the patient’s treatment session. At 10:37 AM, at the conclusion of the visit, S10 provided the tablet to P7, and the patient used his/her finger to sign the tablet. S10 then placed the tablet into a bag and proceeded to clean the outside of the bag. The tablet was not cleaned following contact with the patient. At 10:42 AM, S10 was asked how often the tablet should be cleaned and S10 stated “the tablet should be cleaned after every visit”.

2. On 9/26/23 at 2:11 PM, during a home visit of P4, S5 (Physical Therapist) was observed using a blood pressure cuff, thermometer, and pulse ox on P4 during the visit. When S5 was finished with the items, he/she cleaned them using a Sani cloth wipe and immediately placed the items back into his/her supply bag. S5 did not allow the items to dry prior to placing them back into his/her bag. At 3:00 PM during interview with S5, he/she indicated he/she was unsure of the appropriate dry time.

On 9/27/23 at 12:20 PM, during a home visit of P6, S6 (Registered Nurse) was observed using a blood pressure cuff, thermometer, and pulse ox on P6 during the visit. When S6 was finished with the items, he/she cleaned them using a Sani cloth wipe and immediately placed the items back into his/her supply bag. S6 did not allow the items to dry prior to placing them back into his/her bag.

3. On 9/26/23 at 2:11 PM, during a home visit of P4, S5 (Physical Therapist) was observed donning gloves. S5 then proceeded to take P4’s vital signs and then clean the equipment that was used. S5 did not change his/her gloves after cleaning the equipment and then conducted P4’s physical therapy visit, at times touching P4 to assist with exercises. S5 then reviewed P4’s medications and went over discharge paperwork with P4, while still wearing the same gloves. At 2:54 PM, at the conclusion of the visit, S5 took out the tablet and P4 signed with his/her finger. S5 then removed his/her gloves and used hand sanitizer. S5 wore the same gloves throughout P4’s entire home visit.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Home Health Services of Hackensack is not in compliance with the requirements for 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B requirements, for Home Health Agencies for this complaint visit only.

Complaint #: NJ00111894

Coordination of Care
CFR(s): 484.60(d)
Standard: Coordination of care. 

The HHA must:

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of 3 medical records and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that patient's needs are met and communicated to the physician.

Findings include:

1. Medical Record #1-The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care indicated a Start of Care on 5/9/18 for the Certification Period of 5/9/2018 to 7/7/2018. The Frequency/Duration of Visits are: " ... HHA [home health aide] effective 5/13/2018 2WK4 [two visits per week for 4 weeks], 1WK2 [one visit per week for two weeks]."

a. Review of the home health aide visits revealed that aide visits were performed in accordance with physician orders. The last aide visit was made on 6/20/18. 

(i) Subsequently, 2 skilled nursing visits were made on 6/22/18 and 6/27/18. The notes indicated that the caregiver was having difficulty with caring for the patient. 

(ii) There was no evidence that additional aide services orders were obtained from the physician to meet the patient/family needs after 6/20/18.

b. On 7/3/18, a skilled nursing visit was performed to assess the need for re-certification. The patient was re-certified from 7/8/18 to 9/5/18 with home health aide services to begin on 7/22/18 for 2 times per week for 6 weeks. 

(i) A clinical note addendum, dated 7/3/18, indicated that the aide was not available due to injury and that the patient's spouse was in agreement to wait for the aide to return.

(ii) There was no evidence that another aide was offered to the patient. There was no evidence that the patient was offered to transfer to another agency, if aide services could not be provided. There was no evidence that the physician was notified.

c. The above was confirmed with Staff #3.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Home Health Aide Assignments And Duties
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Home health aide assignments and duties
CFR(s): 484.80(g)(1)
Standard:  Home health aide assignments and duties. 

Home health aides are assigned to a specific patient by a registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional, with written patient care instructions for a home health aide prepared by that registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional (that is, physical therapist, speech-language pathologist, or occupational therapist).

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of 3 medical records, document review, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the Patient Aide Care Plan for Patient #1 is implemented.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Services Provided/Supervision of Disciplines -HHA [home health aide]" states, " ... Procedure: 1. ... The HHA may provide services in the plan of care from the registered nurse, supervisor or the licensed therapist ..."

1. Patient #1 began receiving Home Health Services on 5/9/18 and aide services on 5/14/18. The Aide Care Plan Report, dated 5/9/18, indicated that vital signs such as temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure and oxygen saturation levels were to be performed every patient visit.

2. Home health aide visits were performed on 5/14/18, 5/16, 5/21, 5/23, 5/30, 6/4, 6/6, 6/13 and 6/20/18.

3. There was no evidence that vital signs were performed during the above visits. There was no evidence that the nurse was notified.

4. The above was confirmed with Staff #3.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Development And Evaluation Of Plan Of Care
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Development and evaluation of plan of care
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(2)
Development and evaluation of the plan of care in partnership with the patient, representative (if any), and caregiver(s);

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on document review and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the social worker after development of the plan of care, follows up with the patient's caregiver. 

Findings include:

1. Medical Record #1-The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care indicated a Start of Care on 5/9/18 for the Certification Period of 5/9/2018 to 7/7/2018. Review of the medical social worker note revealed that the patient was seen on 5/25/18. The plan was for the social worker to provide community resource planning for case management and long term planning through senior services and respite care. The narrative note of 5/25/18 states, "... SW [social worker] ... and follow up with agencies for case management referral."

a. A social worker visit was done on 5/31/18.

b. On 6/6/18, a social worker note indicated a telephone call received from the community case management office regarding the patient/caregiver.

c. On 6/22/18, a nursing visit documents that the patient's caregiver was seen on that day by the senior care center and that forms were given to be completed. The nurse "educated husband to fill out forms, and mail in asap [as soon as possible]."

d. On 6/27/18, a nursing visit documents that a call was placed to the patient's primary physician regarding the patient's status and "spouser [sic] needs forms filled out for respite care."

e. The record lacked evidence that the social worker followed up the family after the 5/31/18 visit.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Provide Services In The Plan Of Care
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Provide services in the plan of care
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(3)
Providing services that are ordered by the physician as indicated in the plan of care;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of 3 medical records and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the patient plan of care is implemented for Patient #1 and Patient #3. 

Findings include:

1. Medical Record #1-The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care indicated a Start of Care on 5/9/18 for the Certification Period of 5/9/2018 to 7/7/2018. The Frequency/Duration of Visits are: " ... PT [physical therapy] 1WK1 [one visit during the first week]" 

a. Review of physical therapist notes revealed that on 5/11/18, the patient refused services. On 5/23/18, an initial physical therapy visit was made.

(i) There was no evidence of any attempts made by the physical therapist to visit the patient during the week of 5/13/18. There was no evidence that the physician was notified. 

b. The above was confirmed with Staff #1, Staff #2, and Staff #3. 

2. Medical Record #3-The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care indicated a Start of Care on 5/22/18 for the Certification Period of 5/22/18 to 7/20/18. The Frequency/Duration of Visits are: " ... HHA [home health aide] Effective 5/27/18 1WK1 [one visit during that week], 2WK5 [two visits per week for the next 5 weeks], 1WK1 [one visit per week]."

a. During Week 4, home health aide visits were not provided. Review of 'Missed Visit Note' revealed that on 6/26/18, a home health aide visit was not conducted due to "scheduling issue" and "additional missed visit for 6/28/18 due to refusal."

b. Interview with Staff #2 revealed that on 6/26/18, aide services were not provided to Patient #3 because the patient was not assigned to another aide. 

c. In the afternoon of 6/28/18, the caregiver for Patient #3 called the agency inquiring about a home health visit for that day. The response was that, no aide was available for that day.

d. There was no evidence that services were provided for the 5th week, 7/1/18. There was no documentation to support the missed visit. There was no evidence that the physician was notified. 

e. Services were not provided in accordance with the plan of care.

Communication with physicians
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(7)
Communication with all physicians involved in the plan of care and other health care practitioners (as appropriate) related to the current plan of care;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on document review, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the nursing staff implement the Incident/Occurrence Reporting System policy.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Incident/Occurrence Reporting System" states, " ... Procedure: 1. An Amedisys Occurrence Report is completed by the staff member who is involved in the incident/occurrence, or who initially receives information from the patient or family regarding an occurrence. All occurrences are reported to the DOO/or designee as soon as possible, including after-hour ... 3. The Clinical Manager/designee will notify the patient's physician of an occurrence as appropriate ... Communications to the physician will be documented in the clinical record."

1. Patient #3 began receiving home health services on 5/22/18 and aide services on 5/27/18. A physical therapist discharge visit note, dated 6/21/18, referenced that Patient #3 sustained a fall, earlier in the day, while in the shower with the aide present. An occurrence report was generated by the aide staff which indicated that EMS (emergency medical services) called the physician; no injury to the patient, but injury to the aide's wrist. 

2. There was no documented evidence that the Clinical Manager/designee notified the patient's physician of the occurrence or of any follow up actions, as per the above referenced policy.

Onsite supervisory visit every 14 days
CFR(s): 484.80(h)(1)(i)
If home health aide services are provided to a patient who is receiving skilled nursing, physical or occupational therapy, or speech-language pathology services, a registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional who is familiar with the patient, the patient's plan of care, and the written patient care instructions described in §484.80(g), must make an onsite visit to the patient's home no less frequently than every 14 days. The home health aide does not have to be present during this visit.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of 3 medical records, document review and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the home health aide performs assigned tasks. 

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Services Provided/Supervision of Disciplines -HHA [home health aide]" states, " ... Procedure: 1. ... The HHA may provide services in the plan of care from the registered nurse, supervisor or the licensed therapist ...

Home Health Aide Supervision for a Medicare Certified Agency: 

[bullet] A supervisory visit will be made to the patient's residence at least every 14 days or less, by the RN [registered nurse] ...

[bullet] Home health aide supervision must ensure that aides furnish care in a safe and effective manager, including, but not limited to, the following elements:

[circle] Following the patient's plan of care for completion of tasks assigned to a home health aide by the registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional."

1. Patient #1 began receiving Home Health Services on 5/9/18 and aide services on 5/14/18. The 'Aide Care Plan Report' dated 5/9/18, indicated that vital signs such as temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure and oxygen saturation levels were to be performed every patient visit.

2. Home health aide visits were performed on 5/14/18, 5/16, 5/21, 5/23, 5/30, 6/4, 6/6, 6/13 and 6/20/18. There was no evidence that vital signs were performed during the above visits. 

3. On 5/17/18, 5/24/18, 6/6/18, 6/13/18 and 6/27/18, a nurse performed home health aide supervisions. There was no evidence that the lack of completion of tasks assigned to the aide were addressed by the nurse. 

4. The above was confirmed with Staff #3.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This was a Federal Recertification survey conducted on October 14, October 15, and October 16, 2020. Amedisys Home Health is in compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies. Standard level deficiencies were cited.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on observation of one (1) of five (5) home visits (#1), staff interviews, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that infection control practices, used to mitigate the spread of COVID-19, are implemented.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Exposure to Coronavirus (COVID-19): Disease Response and Management" states, " ... b. Caring for ALL patients, including asymptomatic patients (excluding COVID-19 Positive and PUI): i. Patients must be asked to wear a face cover or a cloth mask... and if possible, separate them at least 6 feet from other persons who are symptomatic. ... iii. If the patient or caregiver present refuses to wear a mask or if the patient is unable to wear a mask, staff SHOULD ALWAYS wear a face shield."

1. During a home visit of Patient #1 on 10/14/20 at 12:10 PM, the following was observed:

a. Upon interview at 12:12 PM, Staff #4 stated this was his/her first encounter with Patient #1. Staff #4 stated that the night before, he/she called the patient and performed a COVID-19 screening, where he/she asked the patient about the presence of COVID-19 symptoms.

b. While entering the patient's home, Patient #1 was sitting at the kitchen table awaiting Staff #4's entry. Patient #1 was not wearing a mask.

Based on observation of two (2) of five (5) home visits (#2 and #3), staff interviews, and review of facility policies and procedures, it was determined that the facility failed to adhere to acceptable standards of infection control, to minimize infections and the transmission of communicable diseases.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, "The Provision of Wound and Skin Care" states, " ... Clean Technique: Wound care will be provided using clean technique and standard precautions unless specified otherwise by the ordering physician. Aseptic Technique: The purposeful prevention of the transfer of organisms by minimizing the introduction of microbes using basic principles of medical asepsis including but not limited to... Adherence to the basic principles of contamination."

1. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 10/14/20 at 1:05 PM, the following was observed:

a. Staff #5 arrived to the home to perform a wound care dressing change to the patient's right great toe.

Reference #2: Facility policy, "Bag Technique" states, "... Bags should not be placed on the floor in the patient's home. ... ."

1. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 10/15/20 at 10:10 AM, the following was observed:

a. Staff #6 entered the bedroom of the patient to begin patient care. Staff #6 used the straps of the bag to hang his/her bag on a chair in the bedroom.

b. The bottom of the bag touched the floor, contaminating the bag, for the duration of time the bag hung on the chair.

2. Staff #1 and Staff #2 confirmed the above findings on 10/16/20 at 1:33 PM.

Findings include:

Reference: Guidelines for Hand Hygiene in Health Care Settings: Recommendation of the Healthcare Infection Control Practices Advisory Committee [HICPAC] and the HICPAC/SHEA/APIC/IDSA Hand Hygiene Task Force, published in the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report at MMWR 2002; 51 (No. RR-16) page 32 states, "... Recommendations 1. Indications for hand washing and hand antisepsis... I. Decontaminate hands after contact with inanimate objects (including medical equipment) in the immediate vicinity of the patient... J. Decontaminate hands after removing gloves. ... ." 

1. During a home visit for Patient #4 on 10/15/2020, the following was observed:

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
A review of all current medications
CFR(s): 484.55(c)(5)
A review of all medications the patient is currently using in order to identify any potential adverse effects and drug reactions, including ineffective drug therapy, significant side effects, significant drug interactions, duplicate drug therapy, and noncompliance with drug therapy.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interview, and a review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure staff complete medication reconciliation during reassessments in accordance with facility policy, in one of five home visits conducted (Patient (P)2).

Findings include:

Facility policy titled “Medication Management & Administration,” dated 08/03/2026, stated “…For Home Health…, medication reconciliation should be completed on assessment and reassessment; …”

On 08/11/26 at 12:30 PM, Staff (S)6 was observed providing care to P2 during a home care visit. During the visit, S6 was not observed reviewing P2's current medications with the patient.  

At 01:49 PM, an interview was conducted with S6. S6 confirmed he/she did not ask for P2's list of medications during the visit. When asked about the process of medication reconciliation, S6 stated he/she checks medications at the start of care and they usually stay pretty much the same. S6 stated, it was rare to have new medications added. When asked how he/she knew if a medication change occurred, S6 stated he/she asks a family member if there was a change in medications. When asked how frequently he/she checks with a family member regarding medication changes, S6 stated “ideally, it should be every visit.”

On 08/12/26 at 11:56 AM, during an interview with S1, he/she confirmed that medication reconciliation is expected to be completed at every visit. S1 stated that the clinician should review all of the patient’s medications and document any identified changes.

Communication with all physicians
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(1)
Standard: Coordination of Care. The HHA must: 
(1) Assure communication with all physicians or allowed practitioners involved in the plan of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interview, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that 1.) physicians are notified when a plan of care is altered due to fewer visits or hours of service being provided in one of three active medical records reviewed (Patient (P) 5); and 2.) physicians are notified when services requested in referral are not provided in one of three active medical records reviewed (P5), and 3.) physicians are notified when there is a delay in the start of care in one of three active medical records reviewed (P1). 

1. Facility policy titled, “06277 Missed Visits/Hours” dated 03/24/23, stated, “… Our Procedure: 1.0: Communicating Missed Visits/Hours. 1.1: Physician Ordered Services. The physician must be notified when the plan of care is altered due to fewer visits or hours of service being provided as ordered. Notification of the missed visits/hours is timely, and as directed on a schedule determined in collaboration with the physician. 1.1.1. Documentation – Home Health and Hospice Offices. … 1.1.1.2 Missed Visit Process Flow. The field clinician is responsible for documenting the missed visit in the “Missed Visit Coordination Note” found in the electronic record. 1.1.1.2.1 The Missed Visit Coordination Note will include the following: a.
