On 08/13/26 at 2:34 PM, Staff (S) 2 confirmed that P5’s medical record lacked evidence of communication with the physician regarding the missed visit.

2. Facility policy titled, “0-4172 Referral Process & Admission Criteria & Procedure – Home Health – NJ” dated 11/12/20, stated, “…Our Procedure: 2.0. Admission Criteria…2.2 Clients shall be accepted for treatment on the basis of a reasonable expectation that the clients needs can be met by [Home Health Agency] in the client’s place of residence or the community. Such reasonable expectation shall be based on an assessment of at least the following factors: a. Adequacy and suitability of [Home Health Agency] personnel and resources to safety [sic] and adequately provide services to the client…3.0. Admission/Readmission Procedure…3.9. When multiple disciplines are ordered and/or evaluation for services are ordered at the time of referral or added on the course of treatment, initiate of each initial discipline specific assessment/evaluation will be completed as soon as is necessary to meet the client’s care needs in coordination with the physician and client. Any delay or altered time frame for the initiation of services beyond those stated, including those due to client preference, contraindicated, etc., are communicated to the physician and to the client, and documented in the client chart…”

On 08/13/26 at 11:01 AM, S2 confirmed that P5’s medical record lacked evidence of a note from the clinician explaining that the patient did not require OT or HHA services or that P5 declined OT or HHA services. S2 confirmed that P5’s medical record also lacked evidence of communication with the physician notifying him/her that P5 was not receiving HHA and OT services. S2 explained that the physician should have been notified that these services were not being provided.

Findings include:

Facility policy titled, “0-672-Admission Criteria & Procedure-Medicare Certified Offices” dated 02/02/26, stated, “…Our Procedure:…9.0: A registered nurse [RN] or therapist (PT [Physical Therapist], SLP [Speech Language Pathologist]) must conduct an initial assessment visit to determine the immediate care and support needs of the client, and for Medicare clients, to determine eligibility for the Medicare home health benefit. Must have a written agreement
CFR(s): 484.105(e)(2)(i-iv)
An HHA must have a written agreement with another agency, with an organization, or with an individual when that entity or individual furnishes services under arrangement to the HHA's patients.  The HHA must maintain overall responsibility for the services provided under arrangement, as well as the manner in which they are furnished. The agency, organization, or individual providing services under arrangement may not have been:

(i) Denied Medicare or Medicaid enrollment;

(ii) Been excluded or terminated from any federal health care program or Medicaid;

(iii) Had its Medicare or Medicaid billing privileges revoked; or

(iv) Been debarred from participating in any government program.

S1 confirmed that was no written agreement or contractual arrangement governing the use of RN and PT between the two separately licensed agencies.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation of one of one home visit, staff interviews, review of facility policies and procedures, and review of nationally recognized guidelines, it was determined that the facility failed to adhere to acceptable standards of infection control to minimize infections and the transmission of communicable diseases.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Guidelines for Hand Hygiene in Health Care Settings: Recommendation of the Healthcare Infection Control Practices Advisory Committee [HICPAC] and the HICPAC/SHEA/APIC/IDSA Hand Hygiene Task Force, published in the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report at MMWR 2002; 51 (No. RR-16) page 32 states, "... Recommendations 1. Indications for hand washing and hand antisepsis ... I. Decontaminate hands after contact with inanimate objects (including medical equipment) in the immediate vicinity of the patient ..." 

Reference #2: Facility policy, Infection Prevention Procedures For Point Of Care Devices, states: "... Our Procedure: Point of care devices require specific Infection Prevention procedures as categorized by device type and location of device below to ensure the safety of the client and employee. ...3.0 [Facility name] Issued Tablet Or Phone Transported From Home To Home. ... 3.2 ... if using the small device, leave in employee's pocket until use. ...3.4 Disinfect ... phone using an approved EPA registered disinfectant wipe, ... at the following times: 3.4.1 ... and more frequently as needed if contaminated. ..."

Reference #3: Facility policy, Hand Hygiene, states: "... Our Procedure: 1.0 Indications For Hand Decontamination. ... hands are decontaminated preferably using alcohol-based waterless hand gel ...as follows: ... b. Before applying ...gloves ..."

1. On 10/27/2020 at 12:01 PM, during Patient #3's home visit, the following was observed:

a. Staff #7, with ungloved hands and in the immediate vicinity of the patient, disposed of soiled medical supplies used for Patient #3's procedure. 

i. Staff #7 did not perform hand hygiene and then proceeded to remove a facility issued phone from his/her jacket pocket. 

ii. Staff #7, while holding the phone in his/her hand, picked an object up from the floor with his/her other hand, placed the object on a bed located in the patient's room, and then proceeded to return the facility issued phone back into his/her jacket pocket without first disinfecting it. 

iii. Staff #7 did not perform hand hygiene and then proceeded to apply gloves. 

2. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #1.

HHA Comprehensive Assessment in Disaster
CFR(s): 484.102(b)(1)
§484.102(b)(1) Condition for Participation:

[(b) Policies and procedures.  The HHA must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 

At a minimum, the policies and procedures must address the following:]



(1) The plans for the HHA's patients during a natural or man-made disaster. Individual plans for each patient must be included as part of the comprehensive patient assessment, which must be conducted according to the provisions at §484.55.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observations, patient and staff interviews, and review of facility documents, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure an individualized emergency preparedness plan is completed on admission in four of seven patient homes visited (Patient (P) 1, P3, P6, and P7).

Findings include:

On 8/7/24 at 12:18 PM, S20, a Home Health Aide (HHA), was observed providing care for P3. 

At 12:40 PM, P3’s admission packet was reviewed with P3’s wife. Surveyors were unable to locate a completed, individualized emergency preparedness plan within the admission packet.

On 8/8/24 At 12:30 PM, a review of P3’s medical record revealed the following:  the RN who completed the Start of Care documented that the EPP was completed on P3’s admission on 7/24/24 at 4:52 PM and a copy of the EPP was left in P6’s home.

On 8/8/24 at 9:31 AM, S7, a Registered Nurse (RN), was observed providing care for P6. 

At 10:24 AM, when questioned about the admission packet S7 stated that he/she would be filling out the individualized emergency preparedness plan with P6 during the visit on 8/8/24 (26 days after P6 was admitted).

At 1:30 PM, a review of P6’s medical record revealed the following:  the RN who completed the Start of Care record documented that the EPP was completed on P6’s admission on 7/13/24 at 7:49 PM and a copy of the EPP was left in P6’s home.

 

On 8/8/24 at 10:44 AM, S8, an Occupational Therapist (OT), was observed providing care for P7.

At 11:15 AM, P7’s admission packet was reviewed with P7’s wife. Surveyors were unable to locate a completed, individualized emergency preparedness plan within the admission packet.

On 8/8/24 At 1:30 PM, a review of P7’s medical record revealed the following:  the RN who completed the Start of Care documented that the EPP was completed on P6’s admission on 7/10/24 at 3:50 PM and a copy of the EPP was left in P7’s home.

 

Facility policy titled “Emergency Preparedness Plan” last revised 6/24 states “Purpose: The Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPP) describes the Agency’s approach to managing emergencies… Policy: Agency employees are oriented to the Emergency Preparedness Plan, including their responsibilities in carrying out the Plan, upon hire, annually, and when changes in staff responsibilities or roles occur… Patients receiving services from the Agency will, upon admission, be informed of the Agency’s emergency process and their personal responsibilities in the event of an emergency, as outlined in the Agency’s Patient Information Booklet. The clinical staff caring for the patient collaborate with the patient and caregiver to develop and individual EPP.”

 

 

 

1.       On 8/7/2024 at 12:18 PM, during a home care visit with P3, a Home Health Aide (HHA) (S20), was observed providing care. At 12:40 PM, P3’s Patient Information Booklet was reviewed with P3’s family and revealed that P3’s Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPP) was left blank.

 

2.       On 8/8/24 at 9:31AM, during a home care visit with P6, a Registered Nurse (RN) (S7), was observed providing care. At 10:24 AM, when questioned about the Agency’s Patient Information Booklet for P6, S7 stated that he/she would be filling out the individualized EPP with P6 during the visit (on 8/8/2024). At 10:24 AM, prior to the conclusion of the visit, S7 was observed reviewing and completing the EPP with P6 and his/her family, (26 days after P6’s admission), and a copy was left in P6’s home.

At 1:30 PM, P6’s medical record was reviewed. The nurse who completed the Start of Care record documented that the EPP was completed on P6’s admission on 7/13/24 at 7:49 PM and a copy of the EPP was left in P6’s home.  

 

3.       On 8/8/24 at 10:44 AM, during a home care visit with P7, an Occupational Therapist (OT) (S8), was observed providing care. At 11:15 AM, P7’s Patient Information Booklet was reviewed with P7’s family and revealed that P7’s Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPP) was left blank. 

Facility Policy titled, “Emergency Preparedness Plan [EPP]” revised on 6/24, states “…Policy:…Patients receiving services from the Agency will, upon admission, be informed of the Agency’s emergency process and their personal responsibilities in the event of an emergency, as outlined in the Agency’s Patient Information Booklet. The clinical staff caring for the patient collaborate with the patient and caregiver to develop and individual EPP…”

An in-home nursing care visit for Patient (P) 1 was observed on 8/7/24 at 1:16 PM. P1 was admitted to homecare services on 7/10/24 at 9:33 AM for wound care after surgery.

On 8/7/24 at 2:15 PM, P1’s admission packet was reviewed. The admission packet revealed that P1’s Emergency Preparedness Plan was left blank. Staff (S) 5 confirmed that the EPP was incomplete and should have been completed during admission.

Prior to conclusion of the nursing visit on 8/7/24, S5 reviewed and completed the EPP with P1 and his/her family. The EPP was left in P1’s home.

On 8/8/24 at 12:30 PM, S1 confirmed that all patients should have the EPP documented in the medical record and a copy left in the home.

On 8/9/24 at 12:00 PM, P1’s medical record was reviewed.  The nurse who completed the Start of Care record documented that the EPP was completed on P1’s admission on 7/10/24 at 7:31 PM and a copy of the EPP was left in P1’s home.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observations, staff interviews, and a review of facility policies, it was determined that the facility failed to follow accepted standards of practice to prevent transmission of infections and communicable diseases in five out of seven patients (Patient (P) 1, P2, P4, P5 and P7).

Findings include:

Facility Policy titled, “Hand Hygiene” last revised 6/22, states “Procedure: … Handwashing with water: … 5. Rub hands together for at least 20 seconds, covering all surfaces of the hands…”

Super Sani-wipe General Guidelines For Use states, “…DIRECTIONS FOR USE …TO DISINFECT AND DEODORIZE: To disinfect nonfood contact surfaces only: …Unfold a clean wipe and thoroughly wet surface. All treated surface to remain wet for a full two (2) minutes. Let air dry. …”

On 8/7/24 at 1:02 PM, S10, a Physical Therapist (PT), was observed providing care for P2.

At 1:03 PM, after entering P2’s home, S10 entered the patient’s bathroom to perform hand hygiene. S10 washed hands with soap and water for only ten seconds before donning gloves and starting patient care.

 At 1:07 PM, S10 was observed to use a stethoscope to assess P2. 

At 1:37 PM, S10 was observed to use a blood pressure cuff on P2. S10 was then observed to clean the stethoscope and blood pressure cuff with a Super Sani-Cloth wipe and placed items immediately into nursing bag without allowing time to dry. 

On 8/8/24 at 9:31 AM, S7, a Registered Nurse (RN), was observed providing care for P6.

At 9:33 AM, S7 placed three barrier pads on P6’s dining room table. S7 placed nursing bag on the first pad, the laptop on the second pad, and began removing vital signs equipment from the nursing bag and placing them on the third pad. The three barrier pads were placed in close proximity to one another, and each pad was overlapping another pad. 

At 9:46 AM, S7 placed a fourth barrier pad on the table for placing vital signs equipment after cleaning. 

At 9:47 AM, S7 cleaned the blood pressure cuff and sphygmomanometer with Sani Cloth wipes and placed them on the fourth barrier pad. The cuff and sphygmomanometer were observed over the edge of the barrier pad and touching the table surface and the outer surface of the nursing bag after being placed on the barrier pad. S7 did not clean or disinfect the table surface prior to placing the barrier pad.

At 9:48 AM, surveyors observed all four barrier pads on the table were overlapping and cleaned vital signs equipment were observed touching dirty vital signs equipment and dirty supplies.

On 8/7/24 at 1:35 PM, during a home visit of P1, Staff (S) 5, Registered Nurse (RN), was observed using blood pressure cuff.  After removal of the blood pressure cuff, S5 cleaned the blood pressure cuff with the facility approved cleansing wipe and placed the cuff on a clean barrier pad. S5 then placed used cleansing wipe onto the same clean barrier pad.

On 8/8/24 at 11:15 AM, during a home visit of P5, S9, RN, was observed using stethoscope and blood pressure cuff. The “dirty” blood pressure cuff was placed on a disposable barrier. S9 cleaned the stethoscope with facility approved cleansing wipes and placed the “clean” stethoscope next to the “dirty” blood pressure cuff on the disposable barrier pad. After completing his/her assessment of P5’s incision, S9 was observed removing used gloves and placing them on the same barrier as the “dirty” blood pressure cuff and the “clean” stethoscope. S9 was then observed leaning on this barrier to clean the blood pressure cuff.

On 8/12/24 at 10:45 AM, S1, Quality and Education Manager, confirmed that there is not a separate policy for the separation of “clean” and “dirty” items. He/she explained that this information is found in the facility’s “Clinical Bag Technique” policy. A discussion with S1 revealed that this policy lacks guidance for placement of reusable equipment after it is cleaned while it is drying. S1 reported that after equipment is cleaned, staff are taught to place equipment on a clean barrier to dry before returning items to the clinical bag.  

On 8/8/24 at 9:33 AM, during a home visit of P4, S6, Physical Therapist, was observed placing his/her clinical bag on a disposable barrier on P’s couch. A second disposable barrier was placed on the opposite end of the couch. While S6 was documenting, he/she sat on the couch in between the clinical bag and computer. At 9:47AM, the clinical bag was observed pressing against the fabric of the couch on two sides after being displaced by S6 when he/she sat on the couch.

On 8/11/24 at 11:07 AM, S1 confirmed that clinical bags should be placed on a clean, hard, non-porous surface.

Facility Policy titled, “Clinical Bag Technique” revised on 6/24, states “…Procedure: 1. Upon entrance to a patient’s home, the clinical bag is placed on a solid surface. For questionable surfaces a barrier, (e.g. newspaper or paper towel) is recommended. …3. Hand Hygiene is performed prior to administering care. Hand hygiene must be performed before removing any supplies or equipment from the clinical bag. 4. After hand hygiene, the clinician enters the bag and takes out all equipment that will be needed for the visit. Equipment is placed on a paper towel or designated barrier….7. Reusable equipment is cleaned/disinfected, hand hygiene is performed with an alcohol-based antiseptic agent and equipment and supplies are returned to the bag…”

On 8/7/2024 at 1:49 PM, during a home care visit with Patient (P) 1, a Registered Nurse (Staff (S) 5) was observed rendering wound care to P1 per physician’s orders. On arrival, P1 was noted to have a V.A.C. (Vacuum Assisted Closure) dressing in place. After removing the old dressing, P1 was noted to have two wounds (Wound #1 and Wound #2). S5 then removed a gauze pad and cleansing solution from his/her clean area and began irrigating Wound #2. S5 was then observed wiping the skin between both wounds, with the same gauze pad, and proceeded to then cleanse Wound #1. S5 was observed using the same soaked saline gauze to clean both Wound #2 and Wound #1, as well as the skin between both wounds.

S5 then disposed of the gauze pad, removed his/her gloves, performed hand hygiene, and began reapplying a new V.A.C. dressing per physician’s order. At 1:56 PM, S5 stated, “when they [the clinician’s] change this dressing, make sure they treat it as two separate wounds and use different supplies.”

On 8/8/2024 at 10:04 AM, medical record review for P1 revealed “SN [Skilled Nursing] Routine Visit” from visit date 8/7/2024, documentation by S5 states, “…Visit Summation[:] … Visit Summary[:] Wound care rendered per orders using wound vac, both wounds noted no longer tunneling together. …”

These findings were reviewed with S1 (Manager of Clinical Education) and S21 (Wound Team Manager) on 8/8/2024 at 10:24 AM. S1 and S21 confirmed that separate supplies should have been used to cleanse each wound individually.

 

On 8/8/24 at 11:15 AM, during a home visit of P5, S9, a Registered Nurse (RN), was observed using stethoscope and blood pressure cuff. The “dirty” blood pressure cuff was placed on a disposable barrier. S9 cleaned the stethoscope with facility approved cleansing wipes and placed the “clean” stethoscope on the same “dirty” disposable barrier pad. After completing his/her assessment of P5’s incision, S9 was observed removing used gloves and placing them on the same barrier as the “dirty” blood pressure cuff and the “clean” stethoscope. S9 was then observed placing the “dirty” blood pressure cuff on top of the previously cleaned stethoscope and began to clean the blood pressure cuff with facility approved cleansing wipes. The used/dirty gloves were observed to be touching the blood pressure cuff and previously “cleaned” stethoscope during this process. S9 then returned the stethoscope and blood pressure cuff to his/her bag, without disinfecting on a clean surface, after contact with the dirty gloves and disposable barrier.  

On 8/12/24 at 10:45 AM, S1, Quality and Education Manager, confirmed that there is not a separate policy for the separation of “clean” and “dirty” items. He/she explained that this information would be found in the facility’s “Clinical Bag Technique” policy and revealed that this policy lacks guidance for placement of reusable equipment after it is cleaned while it is drying. S1 reported that after equipment is cleaned, staff are taught to place equipment on a clean barrier to dry before returning items to the clinical bag.  

Facility Policy titled, “Clinical Bag Technique” revised on 6/24, states “…Procedure: ...4. After hand hygiene, the clinician enters the bag and takes out all equipment that will be needed for the visit. Equipment is placed on a paper towel or designated barrier….7. Reusable equipment is cleaned/disinfected, hand hygiene is performed with an alcohol-based antiseptic agent and equipment and supplies are returned to the bag…”

 

On 8/7/24 at 1:02 PM, during a home visit with P2, S10, a Physical Therapist (PT), was observed providing care. At 1:03 PM, after entering P2’s home, S10 entered the patient’s bathroom to perform hand hygiene. S10 washed hands with soap and water for ten seconds before donning gloves and starting patient care.

Facility Policy titled, “Hand Hygiene” last revised 6/22, states “Procedure: … Handwashing with water: … 5. Rub hands together for at least 20 seconds, covering all surfaces of the hands…”

 

On 8/7/24 at 1:07 PM, during a home visit with P2, S10, a Physical Therapist (PT), was observed to use a stethoscope to assess P2. At 1:37 PM, S10 was observed to use a blood pressure cuff on P2. S10 was then observed to clean the stethoscope and blood pressure cuff with a Super Sani-Cloth wipe and placed items immediately into nursing bag without allowing time to dry, according to the manufacturers Guidelines for Use.

Super Sani-wipe General Guidelines For Use states, “…DIRECTIONS FOR USE …TO DISINFECT AND DEODORIZE: To disinfect nonfood contact surfaces only: …Unfold a clean wipe and thoroughly wet surface. All treated surface to remain wet for a full two (2) minutes. Let air dry. …

Facility Policy titled, "Cleaning of Non-Critical Equipment" last revised 12/23, states, "...Procedure: ...4

Services by skilled professionals
CFR(s): 484.75(a)
Standard: Provision of services by skilled professionals.  

Skilled professional services are authorized, delivered, and supervised only by health care professionals who meet the appropriate qualifications specified under §484.115 and who practice according to the HHA's policies and procedures.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, medical record review, review of facility documents, and staff interviews, it was determined the facility failed to provide skilled services according to the Home Health Agencies (HHA’s) procedure for Bridging Two Wounds with Vacuum Assisted Closure (V.A.C.) Therapy in one out of seven patients observed (Patient (P) 1).

Findings include:

On 8/7/2024 at 1:56 PM, during a home care visit with Patient (P) 1, a Registered Nurse (Staff (S) 5) was observed rendering wound care to P1 per physician’s orders. S5 packed Wound #1 and Wound #2 separately with white foam and covered with black foam per order. S5 then cut a piece of black foam to create a “bridge” between both wounds. S5 was then observed bridging together both wounds by placing the black foam directly on the patient’s intact skin between the two wounds, without first protecting the intact skin with a piece of the V.A.C. Drape.    

On 8/9/24 at 10:20 AM, an interview was conducted with S1, Manager of Clinical Education. S1 stated that wound V.A.C. training is provided both on orientation and monthly and includes education to staff providing wound care to lay down a barrier or drape between wounds when bridging.  S1 stated that the facility uses KCI’s (the company who provides the wound V.A.C.’s and supplies) guidance and follows their procedure on proper application of wound V.A.C.’s.  

At 11:36 AM, during an interview with S21, Wound Team Manager, when asked S21 if he/she would ever lay black foam directly onto patient’s intact skin in order to create a bridge between wounds S21 stated, “I would if it was narrow.” Inquiry was made for what policy/procedure is expected to be followed by clinicians for bridging together wounds with V.A.C. therapy.  The following was provided by the facility:

Document titled, “V.A.C.® Dressing Application Guide [for] Bridging Two Wounds” by KCI, states, “…10. Protect intact skin between the two wounds with a piece of the V.A.C.® Drape. …”

These findings were confirmed with S1 and S21 on 8/12/24 at 11:25 AM.

This was a Standard Level Federal Recertification Survey, Federal COVID19 Focused Infection Control Survey, and State Re-licensure Survey. Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation of one (1) of five (5) home visits, staff interviews, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the agency failed to ensure that hand hygiene was performed in accordance with acceptable standards of practice, and based on observation of one (1) of five (5) home visits, staff interviews, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the agency failed to ensure that cell phones were cleaned with alcohol wipes after use.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, Hand Hygiene, states, "... All clinical staff will use an alcohol-based waterless antiseptic agent... to decontaminate their hands routinely... after removing gloves... Handwashing with water... rub hands together for at least 20 seconds... ."

1. During a home visit on 9/8/21 for Patient #1, the following was observed:

b. At 12:53 PM, Staff #7 removed his/her gloves and did not decontaminate his/her hands after glove removal.

Reference #2: Facility policy titled, Laptop/Cell Phone Technique, states, "... When the patient... signs the Home Health Aide care plan on the cell phone, the staff will instruct them to use alcohol-based hand sanitizer prior to touching the stylus or cell phone. ii. Staff #6 did not clean the cell phone with an alcohol wipe following usage.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1 and Staff #2 on 9/10/21 at 10:15 AM.

Only as ordered by a physician
CFR(s): 484.60(b)(1)
Drugs, services, and treatments are administered only as ordered by a physician or allowed practitioner.

Based on 1 of 1, medical record review ( MR #1), staff interviews, and review of facility policies and procedures, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that patient care followed a written plan of care established and reviewed by a physician.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, Care Planning Process states, "...The plan of care includes physician orders, ... ."

Reference #2: Facility policy, Physician and Non-Physician Practitioner authentication of orders states, "...Physician/NPP orders will be obtained when indicated by the patient's medical condition or changes in Plan of Care (POC).\ ... ."

1. Review of Medical Record #1 on 7/7/2021 indicated the following:

Patient was hospitalized, required SP cath [sic] change done by MD and is being treated for a UTI (Urinary Tract Infection)."

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Federal Recertification survey conducted on June 4, 5 and 6, 2018 resulting in Standard level deficiencies.

Medical Records Reviewed: 8

Home Visits Made: 5

Staff Interviews: 12

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interview and document review, it was determined that the facility staff failed to clean and disinfect reusable medical equipment.

Findings include: 

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "Nursing Bag Technique" states, "...Clinical personnel will comply with the basic principles of asepsis and bag technique in caring for patients and in the use of equipment..... PROCEDURE: ...7. Reusable equipment is cleaned, hand hygiene is performed with and alcohol-based antiseptic agent and equipment and supplies are returned to the bag ... ."

Reference #2: CDC Guideline for Sterilization and Disinfection in Healthcare Facilities (2008) states, "... 3. Indications for Sterilization, High-Level Disinfection, and Low-Level Disinfection...Recommendation... 3.c. Perform low-level disinfection for noncritical patient-care surfaces... and equipment (e.g. blood pressure cuff) that touch intact skin... 4.c. Ensure that, at a minimum, noncritical patient-care devices are disinfected when visibly soiled and on a regular basis such as after use on each patient ... ."

Reference #3: PDI SANI-CLOTH AF3 Germicidal Disposable Wipe directions for use indicated: "... CLEANING AND DEODORIZING: Wipe surface with towelette until clean. Let air dry. For disinfecting hard nonporous surfaces only. TO DISINFECT: Use a wipe to remover heavy soil. Unfold a clean wipe and thoroughly wet surface. Treated surface must remain visibly wet for a full three (3) minutes. Use additional wipe(s) if needed to assure continuous 3 minute wet contact time ... ."

1. On 6/4/18, a home care visit of Patient #4 was conducted by Staff #10. The following events occurred:

a. Staff #10 removed the blood pressure (BP) cuff from the front section of a backpack, and placed it on a clean barrier. The BP cuff was then applied to the direct skin of Patient #4, and a measurement was taken. 

b. The BP cuff was placed back on the same clean barrier, then was returned to the front section of the backpack prior to the start of therapy.

c. The BP cuff was not cleaned/disinfected before it was returned to the same front section of the backpack in which it was removed from. 

2. On 6/4/18, a home care visit of Patient #3 was conducted by Staff #11. The following events occurred:

a. Staff #11 removed the BP cuff from the nursing bag and placed it on a clean barrier. The BP cuff was then applied to the direct skin of the Patient #3, and a measurement was taken.

b. The BP cuff was placed back on the same clean barrier aside clean equipment, then was returned to the same part of the nursing bag from which it was taken prior to the start of wound care.

c. The BP cuff was not cleaned/disinfected before it was returned to the same section of the nursing bag from which it was taken. 

3. On 6/5/18 a home care visit of Patient #2 was conducted by Staff #12; the following events occurred:

a. Staff #12 removed the BP cuff from the nursing bag and placed it on a clean barrier. The BP cuff was then applied to the direct skin of Patient #2, and a measurement was taken.

b. The BP cuff was placed back on the same clean barrier aside clean equipment.

c. At the conclusion of care for Patient #2, Staff #12 used one Sani-wipe to first wipe down the stethoscope, and then wipe down the BP cuff. The stethoscope was placed around the neck of Staff #12 after being wiped, and the BP cuff was placed back on the original barrier. 

d. The medical equipment was not observed to be thoroughly wet with the Sani-Wipe, and was not observed to remain wet for a full 3 minutes, as required by the manufacturer's instructions.

4. On 6/4/18, a home care visit of Patient #1 was conducted by Staff #3. The following events occurred:

a. Staff #3 removed the BP cuff from the nursing bag and applied it directly onto the skin of Patient #1, and a measurement was taken. Thereafter, the BP cuff was placed back in a separate bag and placed in the outer section of the nursing bag. 

b. The BP cuff was not cleaned/disinfected after use. 

c. This was confirmed with Staff #3.

RN performs assessment
CFR(s): 484.55(a)(1)
A registered nurse must conduct an initial assessment visit to determine the immediate care and support needs of the patient; and, for Medicare patients, to determine eligibility for the Medicare home health benefit, including homebound status. The initial assessment visit must be held either within 48 hours of referral, or within 48 hours of the patient's return home, or on the physician- ordered start of care date.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of 2 of 2 medical records of patients with nutritional needs and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the support needs of the patients are met in accordance with facility policy.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy "Nutrition Assessment" states, "... Procedure: During the initial admission assessment, the admitting clinician will assess the patient's nutritional status using the agency assessment tool and the Braden Scale. If a patient scores as: ...

Moderate nutritional risk (3-5) and /or Braden nutrition rating of 13-14 the clinician should request the patient complete a 3 day diet recall (3DDR), assess the patient's nutritional intake when the 3DDR is complete and provide the appropriate nutritional teaching including addressing identified risks. The clinical should also evaluate the need for nutritional supplements and/or nutritionist referral ...

High nutritional risk (6 or grater) and/or Braden nutrition rating of 12 and below refer the patient to the nutritionist ...

High risk patients may include: ... 2. Non healing wounds 3. Significant weight loss or gain 4. Enteral feedings or TPN [total parenteral nutrition] 5. Nutritional related problems."

1. On 6/7/18, review of the medical records revealed:

a. In Medical Record #8, the patient began receiving home health services beginning 4/18/18 for management of a right lower quadrant ileostomy, left upper quadrant jejunostomy, abdominal enterocutaneous fistula and a right upper extremity PICC (peripherally inserted central catheter) line for TPN (total parenteral nutrition). The patient was assessed to be at moderate nutritional risk according to the initial comprehensive assessment.

(i) There was no evidence that a referral was made to a dietician to evaluate the patient's nutritional needs, as per policy. 

b. In Medical Record #7, the patient began receiving home health services beginning 3/12/18 for wound management of an unstageable pressure ulcer to the sacral region. The patient had a reported unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds or more in the past 3 months. 

(i) Facility policy stated that a significant weight loss would indicate a high risk nutritional patient. The patient was assessed to be at moderate nutritional risk according to the initial comprehensive assessment.

(ii) There was no evidence in the medical record that a 3 day diet recall was initiated to evaluate the patient's nutritional needs, as per policy.

(iii) There was no evidence that a referral was made to a dietician to evaluate the patient's nutritional needs, as per policy.

Integrate all services
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(3)
Integrate services, whether services are provided directly or under arrangement, to assure the identification of patient needs and factors that could affect patient safety and treatment effectiveness and the coordination of care provided by all disciplines.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on medical record review and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that coordination of care is performed for Patient #4 and Patient #6.

Findings include:

1. On 6/6/18, review of Medical Record #6 indicated a home heath start of care beginning 5/11/18. The patient was admitted for the management of wound care to the left hallux amputation. The patient was receiving skilled nursing and physical therapy services. The Start of Care physician order indicated the following wound care order, "... clean with ns [normal saline] or wound cleanser. apply [sic] aquacil ag, dsd [dry sterile dressing] abd [absorbent dressing] and kling ... ."

a. On 5/26/18 during a home visit, the nurse documented "Plans for Next Visit ... VN [visiting nurse] to follow up with __ [name of physician] re [regarding] weight bearing status."

b. The patient was seen on 5/29/18 and discharged from nursing services. There was no evidence that a call was made to the physician regarding the weight bearing status or that this information was shared with physical therapy. 

c. The above physician order does not indicate the frequency of the wound care. There was no evidence that the order was clarified with the physician. 

d. The above was confirmed by Staff #6.

2. Patient #4 had a home health start of care on 5/9/18 for the management of wounds to the left lower leg and therapy to increase mobility due to a displaced bicondylar fracture of the left tibia. Patient #4 was receiving skilled nursing and physical therapy services.

a. Staff #9 discharged the patient from skilled nursing services on 5/14/17 secondary to completion of instructions to the patient and family regarding how to care for the incision and wounds; including instruction on reporting signs and symptoms of infection.

b. On 6/4/18, a home care visit of Patient #4 was conducted by Staff #10. The corresponding visit note by Staff #10 indicates that instruction was provided to the patient regarding signs and symptoms of infection.

(i) Patient #4 reported increased drainage associated with a bad odor coming from the left heel wound to Staff #10. 

(ii) Staff #10 stated he/she would take a look and let the doctor know.

(iii) There was no evidence in the medical record that noted the patient's report of increased drainage and bad odor.

(iv) There was no evidence in the medical record that the change in wound drainage and smell were reported to the physician.

Other pertinent instructions
CFR(s): 484.60(e)(4)
Any other pertinent instruction related to the patient's care and treatments that the HHA will provide, specific to the patient's care needs.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of 2 medical records of patients receiving home health aide services, review of facility policy and procedure and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that a copy of the patient aide care plan is available in the home for Patient #1.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy "Home Health Aide Supervisory Visits" states, "Policy: ... 2. A master HHA [home health aide] Care plan is created for the patient by the referring nurse. A copy of the HHA Care Plan is available in the home."

Patient #1 began home health services on 5/14/18 and was receiving home health aide services. During a home visit on 6/3/18, upon request, Staff #3 was unable to provide the surveyor a copy of the home health aide care plan.

Title 8 Chapter 42 Home Health Agency Licensing Standards.

Accessibility
CFR(s): 484.50(f)(1,2)
Standard: Accessibility.  Information must be provided to patients in plain language and in a manner that is accessible and timely to— 
(1) Persons with disabilities, including accessible web sites and the provision of auxiliary aids and services at no cost to the individual in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. 
(2) Persons with limited English proficiency through the provision of language services at no cost to the individual, including oral interpretation and written translations.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, medical record review, staff interview, and facility document review, it was determined the facility failed to ensure, all patients with limited or no English language proficiency, received a qualified interpreter in four of four patients who requested the use of language interpreter services (Patient (P)7, P18, P19, P20).

A review of P19's medical record was conducted with S2 and S6 and revealed the following:   

A “SN [Skilled Nurse] OASIS Start of Care” note by S8, dated 07/12/26, stated, “… Ethnicity, Race, and Language: … What is your preferred language? Gujarati … Do you need or want an interpreter to communicate with a doctor or healthcare staff? 1. Yes.” The note lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P19 and refused.

A “SLP [Speech Language Pathology] Initial Evaluation” note by S28, dated 07/13/26, stated, “… Encounter Notes: … Note: pt [patient] is able to respond verbally in Gujarat (family translates). pt is able to follow one step level directions with assistance for mobility.” The note lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P19 and refused.

A “OT [Occupational Therapy] Initial Evaluation” note by S29, dated 07/20/26, stated, “… Problem: Patient-Stated Goal: … Intervention: Patient Care Preferences: “… have an interpreter attend each visit and plan visits when caregiver is available. Visit Notes: DIL [Daughter-in-law] present for interpretor [sic] as per preference.” The note lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P19 and refused.

Spanish … Do you need or want an interpreter to communicate with a doctor or healthcare staff? 1. Yes.” The note lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P20 and refused.

A “SN OASIS Resumption of Care” note by S30, dated 08/07/26, lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P20 and refused.

A “PT [Physical Therapy] Initial Evaluation” note by S31, dated 08/19/26, lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P20 and refused.

Findings include:

 

Facility policy titled, "Foreign Language Interpreter," dated 10/2024, stated, "… Procedure. Needs Assessment …  During the admission assessment process the nursing team will verify the patient's communication needs and ensure that the appropriate services are provided … Should the patient refuse the services of a foreign language interpreter, staff will document the refusal in Epic [electronical medical record system] and complete the Foreign Language Interpreter Waiver Form … Interpreter Services … The following resources may be utilized to facilitate adequate communications for patients with Limited English Proficiency: VRI (video remote interpreting), Over the telephone, Face to face qualified interpreters … Team Member Competency. On 08/25/26 at 2:15 PM, a home visit for P7 was observed, completed by Staff (S)14. This would certify that staff could have non-clinical conversations with patients. S1 stated that until certified, staff should use the language line when working with patients.

Encounter Notes...Assessment Revisit Note - Skilled Need: PT for heel cord stretch, ROM [range of motion] and fall prevention...Caregiver Involvement: [Spouse/Name], present and supportive. The medical record lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P7 and lacked evidence that P7 refused interpreter services.

Spanish … Interpreter – Do you need or want an interpreter to communicate with a doctor or health care staff? 1. Yes …”

A "PT Home Visit” note completed by S11, dated 08/25/26, stated, "… Encounter Notes: … Caregiver involvement: Patient has a supportive family present during visit assisting with Spanish translation…” The medical record lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P18 and lacked evidence that P18 refused interpreter services.  

A review of P19's medical record was conducted with S2 and S6 and revealed the following:   

A "SN OASIS Start of Care” note completed by S8, dated 07/12/26, stated, "… Ethnicity, Race, and Language: … What is your preferred language? Gujarati … Do you need or want an interpreter to communicate with a doctor or healthcare staff? 1. Yes.” The medical record lacked evidence that a qualified interpreter was offered to P19 and lacked evidence that P19 refused interpreter services.

A "OT [Occupational Therapy] Initial Evaluation” note completed by S29, dated 07/20/26, stated, "… Problem: Patient-Stated Goal: … Intervention: Patient Care Preferences: … have an interpreter attend each visit and plan visits when caregiver is available. A review of P20's medical record was conducted with S2 and S6 and revealed the following:

Survey date: February 28- March 1, 2024

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
This was a Federal Re-Certification Survey conducted at Visiting Health Services of New Jersey, February 28- March 1, 2024, to determine compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies.

Standard level deficiencies were cited in conjunction with this survey.

Conformance with physician orders
CFR(s): 484.60(b)
Standard: Conformance with physician or allowed practitioner orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, facility policy review, and staff interview, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that services ordered by the physician are provided as indicated in the plan of care.

Facility policy titled, “Verification of Physician Orders”, revised 3/22, states, “…NOTICES TO THE PHYSICIAN … 2. If fewer visits are provided during the week than ordered, the physician will be notified with documentation in the clinical record that the physician is aware of the missed visits unless the physician has authorized missed visits under specified circumstances (for example, the plan of care indicates that the office may skip nursing visits on the day of physician visits or that home health aide visits may  be skipped when the patient’s daughter is in the home to provide personal care). …”

Findings include:

On 2/29/24 during a review of Patient (P) 8’s medical record the “Home Health Plan of Care” for P8 for the certification period of 1/21/24 - 3/20/24, revealed the following: The section labeled Visit Sets stated, “… Speech Language Pathology[SLP]: 1 visit every 6 days for 6 days from 1/29/2024 to 2/3/2024, Comments: ST [Speech Therapy] evaluation for cognition; 1 visit every week for one week from 2/4/24 to 2/9/24; 2 visits per week for three weeks from 2/11/24 to 3/1/24. …”

The week of 2/18/24, P8’s medical record indicated that no SLP visits were made. An “Inconvenience Visit Note was documented on 2/20/24 that stated, “… All Conversations …2/20/24 Inconvenience Visit: approx. [approximately] 2 minutes from pt [patient] house. Spouse cancelled because family dog just passed away. Re-scheduled for Thursday. …”  On 2/29/24 at 3:02 PM, S1 (RN Director) explained that an Inconvenience Visit note is completed when the patient cancels the visit when the clinician is en-route. S1 explained that the clinician should complete a missed visit note in addition to the inconvenience note. The medical record for P8 does not contain evidence that the physician was notified of the missed visit on 2/20/24.

On 3/1/24, during a review of P9’s medical record, the “Home Health Plan of Care” for P9, for the certification period of 1/29/24- 3/28/24, revealed the following: The section labeled Visit Sets stated, “… Speech Language Pathology[SLP]: 1 visit every 6 days for 6 days from 1/29/2024 to 2/3/2024, Comments: Eval [evaluate] and treat; 1 visit every 6 days for 6 days 2/4/2024 to 2/9/2024, Comments: Extension of SLP Eval and treat; 1 visit every week for 1 week 2/11/2024 to 2/16/2024; 1 visit every week for 3 weeks 2/18/2024 …”

The Week of 2/4/24, P9’s medical record indicated that a SLP visit was missed. The “2/6/2024 SLP Missed Visit Note” lacks documentation that a physician was notified of the missed visit scheduled for 2/6/24. The “2/6/2024 SLP Missed Visits Notes” states, “…All Conversations (Oldest Message First) February 29,2024 [name of clinician], SLP to [name] RN  2/6/24 called Dr. [name] office and spoke with [name] to report a MV [missed visit]. 2/29/24 23:08 [11:08 PM]. …” On 3/1/24 at 10:07 AM, during an interview with S1 (RN Director), he/she confirmed that documentation of notification of a missed visit is expected to occur within 24 hours and that this SLP did not meet that expectation.

N.J.A.C. 8:42-6.2(a)(6)

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of facility policy and procedure, observations, and staff interview, it was determined the facility failed to implement its policy and procedures regarding cleaning and disinfecting of equipment, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases. 

 

Facility Policy titled, “Cleaning & Disinfecting Guidelines for Patient Care Equipment” last revised 03/2022, states, “…Procedure … 3. Separation must be maintained between clean and soiled equipment to prevent cross contamination. … 4. …Patient care equipment should be wiped to thoroughly wet the surface (contact time) and remain wet for the time frame specific to the product’s instructions, before drying and returning to the clinician’s bag. …6. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for equipment use, transportation, storage, and cleaning/disinfection. …”

Manufacturer instructions for use (IFU) the Sani-Cloth Germicidal Disposable Wipes, located on the package, states, “… use a wipe to remove visible soil prior to disinfecting. Unfold a clean wipe and thoroughly wet surface. Allow surface to remain wet for two (2) minutes. Let air dry…”

On 2/28/24 at 12:18 PM, during a home visit with P2, Staff (S) 6 (Physical Therapist), was observed opening two clean barriers and placing them near the patient’s side. S6 then placed an unused blood pressure cuff, pulse oximeter, and thermometer on one barrier (clean). After using the equipment on P2, S6 then placed the used equipment onto an unused barrier (dirty). S6 then individually disinfected each used item with Sani-Cloth Germicidal Disposable Wipes and was observed placing disinfected/clean items back onto the same (dirty) barrier to dry. There was no clear and distinct separation between clean and soiled/used equipment observed. Additionally, after disinfecting the blood pressure cuff, S6 immediately rolled up the blood pressure cuff, not allowing the disinfectant to dry on the surface, for the recommended time, as per the manufacturer’s instructions (two minutes).

On 2/29/24 at 10:50 AM, during a home visit with P4, S9 (Registered Nurse), was observed cleaning/disinfecting the used blood pressure cuff with a Sani-Cloth Wipe and then immediately rolled up the cuff, not allowing the disinfectant to dry on the surface for the recommended time.

On 3/1/2024 at 12:24 PM, an interview was conducted with S3 (Director of Quality) and S12 (Registered Nurse - Staff Development) in which the process of cleaning equipment was discussed. S3 explained the staff is educated to clean the blood pressure cuff and allow it to dry (according to manufacturer’s guidelines), prior to rolling them and placing them back in their bags for storage. S3 indicated the staff should not be rolling the blood pressure cuffs up immediately after cleaning them because it does not give the disinfectant time to dry properly. S12 confirmed this by stating “the blood pressure cuff should be left open so you can see the surface and ensure the disinfectant has dried." 

N.J.A.C. 8:42-12.2(b)

Patient's needs
CFR(s): 484.55(c)(4)
The patient's medical, nursing, rehabilitative, social, and discharge planning needs;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
(NJ00141097)

Based on staff interviews, review of one (1) of one (1) medical record, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that patients who require long term planning receive a visit from a medical social worker. 

Findings include:

Discharge plans communication
CFR(s): 484.60(c)(3)(ii)
(ii) Any revisions related to plans for the patient's discharge must be communicated to the patient, representative, caregiver, all physicians or allowed practitioner's issuing orders for the HHA plan of care, and the patient's primary care practitioner or other health care professional who will be responsible for providing care and services to the patient after discharge from the HHA  (if any).

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
(NJ00141097 and NJ00143188)

Based on staff interviews, review of two (2) of three (3) medical records, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that discharge planning was implemented according to facility policy.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, Patient Education Related to Discharge Planning, states, " ... The home health aide staff and interdisciplinary team member assist patient regarding their discharge by ... Consulting with the patient and family regarding the need for discharge instruction. ..."

1. Upon review of Medical Record #1, the following was noted:

2. Upon review of Medical Record #2, the following was noted:

a. Patient #2 was discharged on 10/16/20.

b. Patient #2 was not consulted regarding the need for discharge instructions.

3. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1 and Staff #4.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):

Receive all services outlined in the plan of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of medical records, review of facility policies and procedures, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure patient care services are provided in accordance with the plan of care. 

Findings include: 

Reference #1: Facility policy titled "Physician Participation in Plan of Care," states, "...Policy ...The care will be provided in compliance with his/her therapeutic and diagnostic orders and accepted standards and practice. ...Procedure ...7. Orders will be reviewed and revised by the patients physician (or other authorized licensed independent practitioner) based on:

Whenever the plan of care is changed ...the patient will be notified at the time of the visit. .... 2. Documentation of the notification will include: A. Date and time of notification B. (i) Patient #9 was scheduled to have a SN visit on 9/28/18. The SN visit did not take place.

(ii) There was a lack of documentation of the missed visit notification to the patient.

3. On 11/8/18, the medical record of Patient #11 was reviewed. The following was identified:

5. On 11/9/18, Patient #16 was seen at a home visit by Staff #21, a nurse and Staff #22 a home health aide. Medical record documents were reviewed and the following was identified:

a. On 11/5/18 Patient #16 was scheduled to have a SN visit. On 11/8/18, Staff #21 documented in the nursing notes the following: "... Informed MD that client did her own wound care on Monday 8/5/18 [sic] and no SN visit was made ..."

(i) There was a lack of documentation that the physician was notified regarding the missed visit on that day.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Plan Of Care Must Include The Following

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Integrate all services
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(3)
Integrate services, whether services are provided directly or under arrangement, to assure the identification of patient needs and factors that could affect patient safety and treatment effectiveness and the coordination of care provided by all disciplines.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, medical record review, and review of other facility documentation, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the identification of the patient needs and the coordination of care are provided.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy titled "Internal Referral Process," stated, "...PROCEDURE 1. All internal referrals to other disciplines will be documented within the clinical record... 2. When a clinician identifies that an additional service is needed, the Case Manager will contact the physician... for orders for evaluation. The Case Manager will electronically message the Clinical Supervisor or scheduler, who will assign the appropriate clinician...."

1. On 11/8/18, the medical record of Patient #12 was reviewed. The following was identified:

a. The "Referral Profile" section of the medical record indicated on 7/11/18, that the reason for home care for this patient included strengthening, gait and mobility training. The "Referral Profile" also noted that there should be a skilled nursing (SN) evaluation for physical therapy (PT) needs in the home.

b. The OASIS Start of Care (SOC) completed on 7/12/18 by Staff #20 indicated that Patient #12 was "...homebound due to fall risk due to generalized weakness/intractable pain, poor endurance, ambulates 10 feet with assistive device and supervision and then must rest with a recovery time of 3-5 minutes....." 

(i) Staff #20 noted in the "Therapy Need and Plan of Care" section of the SOC that there were no therapy visits indicated for the patient.

c. Staff #6 completed a note regarding the SN home visit with Patient #12 on 7/17/18 that revealed that a family member of the patient was asking when PT services would begin. 

(i) Staff #6 forwarded the information regarding the request for PT services electronically to Staff #13, the case manager, on 7/20/18. On 7/22/18, Staff #13 responded "noted" to Staff #6's message.

(ii) The medical record lacked documentation regarding the notification to the physician of the request for PT services.

(iii) There was no indication that PT was made aware of the request for services. 

d. Staff #13 completed a home visit on 8/2/18, and indicated in a note that the family member of the patient requested the services of occupational therapy (OT).

(i) Staff #13 received an order for an OT evaluation for 1 visit in 6 days to occur within 6 days (1x6Dx6D) and sent a message to Staff #12, a manager.

(ii) There was a lack of documentation that the request was sent to a scheduler.

(iii) There was lack of documentation that an OT visit was scheduled and/or completed within the timeframe of the physician's order.

2. Staff #4 confirmed the above findings.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Provide Services In The Plan Of Care
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Provide services in the plan of care
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(3)
Providing services that are ordered by the physician as indicated in the plan of care;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of medical records and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to follow the plan of care.

Findings include: 

1. Upon observation of Patient #6 on 11/7/18, the following was determined:

a. The patient had a diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Acute Osteomyelitis of the right foot wound/amputation. 

b. The Plan of Care addressed the following: 

(i) Skilled nursing full systems assessment every visit. 

(ii) Assess/Instruct/Monitor on diabetic foot care including monitoring for lesions.

2. Staff #6 failed to monitor the patient's left foot for lesions.

3. Staff #6 failed to assess the patient's left or right foot for circulation for diabetic foot monitoring. 

4. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #3 and Staff #10.

Communication with physicians
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(7)
Communication with all physicians involved in the plan of care and other health care practitioners (as appropriate) related to the current plan of care;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of medical records, review of facility policy and procedure, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that physicians are notified of changes to the plan of care. 

Findings include: 

Reference #1: Facility policy titled "Physician Participation in Plan of Care," states, "...Policy ...The care will be provided in compliance with his/her therapeutic and diagnostic orders and accepted standards and practice. ...Procedure ...7. Orders will be reviewed and revised by the patients physician (or other authorized licensed independent practitioner) based on: 

A. Changes in the care or service being provided ..."

Reference #2: Facility policy titled "Monitoring Patient's Response/Reporting to Physician," states, "...PROCEDURE ...3. The patient's physician will be contacted on the same day when any of the following occur: ...F. When there is a problem implementing the plan of care G. When a visit is missed for any reason... I. Patient is to be discharged from the organization, or a specific service is to be discontinued 4. All conferences or attempts to communicate with the physician will be documented in the clinical record....."

1. On 11/8/18, the medical record of Patient #1 was reviewed. The following was identified:

a. Patient #1 was scheduled to have a skilled nursing (SN) visit on 11/2/18. The SN visit did not take place.

(i) There was a lack of documentation that the physician was notified regarding the missed visit.

2. On 11/8/18, the medical record of Patient #9 was reviewed. The following was identified:

a. Patient #9 was scheduled to have a SN visit on 10/28/18. The SN visit did not take place.

(i) There was a lack of documentation that the physician was notified regarding the missed visit.

b. There was a note written by Staff #17 on 10/2/18 that indicated that the patient had met all their goals and the patient was discharged from SN service to the Physical Therapy (PT) service.

(i) The medical record lacked documentation that the physician was notified regarding the discharge from the SN service.

3. On 11/8/18, the medical record of Patient #10 was reviewed. The following was identified:

a. On 10/31/18, the physical therapist's (PT) discharge summary documentation noted that 10/31 was the last PT visit because the patient met his/her goals. 

(i) Under the section, "Person Contacted," the following was documented: 

 - Select Physician (physician's name)

 - Contact's name (office staff name)

 - Summary - Type: Discharge 

(ii) There was no documentation as to why PT placed a call out to the physician's office and/or what reason was for the phone communication. 

b. Patient #10 was scheduled to have home health aide visits on 11/1/18 and 11/6/18, both dates had missed visits by the aide.

4. On 11/8/18, the medical record of Patient #11 was reviewed. The following was identified:

 6. On 11/9/18, Patient #16 was seen at a home visit by Staff #21, a nurse and Staff #22 a home health aide. Medical record documents were reviewed and the following was identified:

(ii) An interview conducted with Patient #16, in the presence of Staff #21, confirmed she/he had surgery on 9/15/18 and has been wheelchair bound "for awhile" and has been instructed to be non-weight bearing on the right foot.

(iii) On 11/9/18, during the home visit, Staff #21 wrote next to "walker" "Wheelchair Bound" to update the care plan for the aide to follow. 

(iv) There was no updated instructions provided to the aide by the nurse to ensure the patient remains non-weight bearing and the update was a late revision to the care plan from the SoC on 9/21/18.

c. On 11/5/18 Patient #16 was scheduled to have a SN visit. On 11/8/18, Staff #21 documented in the nursing notes the following: "... Informed MD that client did her own wound care on Monday 8/5/18 [sic] and no SN visit was made ..."

(i) There was a lack of documentation that the physician was notified regarding the missed visit on that day.

7. Upon review of Medical Record #4 on 11/9/18, the following was noted: 

a. The Home Health Aide (HHA) visit frequency order for the certification period beginning 10/11/18 stated, "HHA schedule begins on 10/14/18-2x1Wx2W, 10/28/18 2x1Wx2W (two times one week for two weeks, two times one week for two weeks)."

b. There was evidence of HHA time/availability offered to the patient/family on 10/15/18 and 10/18/18, however the patient/family declined on those days.

eval ..."

(ii) There was no evidence that the physician was informed of an OT visit/evaluation per the Plan of Care.

9. Upon review of Medical Record #7 on 11/9/18, the following was noted: 

a. The Home Health Aide (HHA) visit frequency order for the certification period beginning 10/18/18 stated, "HHA schedule begins on 10/21/18-3x1Wx1W, 10/28/18-2x1Wx1W (three times a week for one week, two times a week for one week)."

(ii) A "Secure Message Report" was posted on 11/7/18 that stated, " ...No need for HHA at this time. Spouse assisting patient with the ADL's, grooming."

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This report is the result of an unannounced standard-level Federal Recertification and State Re-licensure survey completed on April 30, 2026 at Hackensack Meridian JFK at Home. It was determined the facility is not in substantial compliance with Federal requirements of 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies and State requirements of N.J.A.C. Title 8 Chapter 42 Home Health Agency Licensing Standards.

Encoding and transmitting OASIS
CFR(s): 484.45(a)
Standard: An HHA must encode and electronically transmit each completed OASIS assessment to the CMS system, regarding each beneficiary with respect to which information is required to be transmitted (as determined by the Secretary), within 30 days of completing the assessment of the beneficiary.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of facility policy, review of agency pre-survey report, and staff interviews, it was determined the facility failed to ensure timely transmission of Outcome and Assessment Information Set (OASIS) assessments within 30 days of completion of beneficiary assessments.

Findings include:

Facility policy titled, "OASIS Data Transmission," dated 05/2025, stated, "… Procedure 1. The organization will encode and electronically transmit completed OASIS data to the national internet Quality Improvement Evaluation System (iQIES) for each applicable patient within thirty (30) days of the … date assessment completed … 7. A tracking mechanism will be utilized by the organization to ensure accuracy and timeliness of OASIS data and transmission …"  

A review of the iQIES HHA (Home Health Agency) Error Summary by Agency report, with a reporting period of 03/01/25 to 04/23/26, revealed 826 assessments submitted to iQIES greater than 30 days after completion of the beneficiary assessments. The findings were confirmed with Staff (S) 1 on 04/29/26 at 3:18 PM. 

On 04/30/26 at 10:04 AM, an interview was conducted with S1, S2, S3, and S17. S3 stated facility leadership works with the billing team and runs reports to determine timeliness of OASIS assessment transmissions. When asked about their process on how often the facility is monitoring and tracking OASIS assessment transmissions, S1 stated "I don't know if we have a true cadence." S1 was unable to provide a written process or describe the facility's process for monitoring and tracking OASIS assessment transmissions.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
NJ00138671

This facility is not in compliance with the requirements for 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B requirements for Home Health Agencies for this complaint survey only.

The following Condition is out of compliance:

484.60 Condition of Participation: Care Planning, Coordination, Quality of Care. 

On 8/20/20 an IJ (Immediate Jeopardy) was identified:

The facility failed to ensure that competent staff was rendering care and that the plan of care was implemented.

The facility was made aware of the IJ and a copy of the IJ template was provided. A removal plan was accepted on 8/21/20.

On 8/28/20, a visit to the facility was performed to evaluate implementation of the removal plan. The facility did fully implement the removal plan and the IJ was removed.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Care Planning, Coordination, Quality Of Care
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Care planning, coordination, quality of care
CFR(s): 484.60
Condition of participation: Care planning, coordination of services, and quality of care.

Patients are accepted for treatment on the reasonable expectation that an HHA can meet the patient's medical, nursing, rehabilitative, and social needs in his or her place of residence.  Each patient must receive an individualized written plan of care, including any revisions or additions. The individualized plan of care must specify the care and services necessary to meet the patient-specific needs as identified in the comprehensive assessment, including identification of the responsible discipline(s), and the measurable outcomes that the HHA anticipates will occur as a result of implementing and coordinating the plan of care.  The individualized plan of care must also specify the patient and caregiver education and training. Services must be furnished in accordance with accepted standards of practice.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:

Based on review of 1 of 1 medical record, document review and interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that competent staff is rendering care to a patient and that caregiver education and training is provided in accordance with the care plan.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy "Competency Assessment" states, "Procedure Orientation and Probationary Period

As part of the ordination process, a preceptor/Clinical/assigned Supervisor will be assigned to each new person.

Using a Skills/Experience Checklist and assigned MCP [manager of clinical practice] will observe the new personnel performing the required skills and activities. The Skills/Experience Checklist is completed by each clinician upon hire and is used to match team member skill with patient need. Any time a team member indicates that he/she needs further instruction or review the MCP is responsible to ensure that the clinician receives remediation for the skill prior to being planed on a case requiring this skill. The MCP or signee [sic] is responsible for updating the Skills/Experience Checklist and ensuing that scheduling receives these updates."

1. On 8/20/20 review of Medical Record #1 revealed the following:

a. Patient #1's Home Health Certification and Plan of Treatment, Start of Care 8/5/20 to 10/3/20 states, "... #21. Orders for Discipline and Treatments "... Instruct/perform trach [tracheostomy] care. Trach size #6 Care freq [frequency] daily and as needed; ... Perform /instruct use of enteral nutrition and the use/care of equipment.; PEG/PEJ [percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy/percutaneous endoscopic jejunostomy) site care: cleanse site with water and pat dry apply split gauze secure with tape freq daily and as needed. 

#22. Goals/Rehabilitation ... Caregiver will be independent with airway suctioning as evidenced by return demonstration by 3 weeks; Caregiver will be independent with trach care as evidenced by return demonstration in 3 weeks ..."

b. On 8/18/20, Staff #3 (Licensed Practical Nurse) visited the patient at 9:45 AM. The section under "Plan for this Visit Routine" of the Routine Note by nursing states, "Primary Reason for This Visit Teaching and Education." In the Summary Narrative, Staff #3 documented "Pt (patient) in bed, ... with SOB (shortness of breath) on assessment pt tracheostomy has thick mucus hanging outside of inner cannula, pt having SOB using accessory muscles pt husband requested this nurse to suction, this nurse advised pt that education and demonstration on suctioning would benefit the pt as husband is caregiver and should have this skill. Pt husband refused education states "he already does it everyday" this nurse again advised pt that together pt could be suctioned pt husband picked up suctioning catheter and began suctioning this nurse held 02 (oxygen) tubing up while pt suctioned ... This nurse educated pt on sterile tech [technique] and pt husband shouldn't keep reusing hoses, and catheter on pt. Pt husband denied needing supplies, and verbalized understanding. Pt secretions cleared After [sic] suctioning ... Pt has a PEG tube with Kangaroo pump intact and patent running on 55/mL [milliliter] continuously. Pt husband denied needing education. This nurse assessed PEG clean and intact pt husband states he changes daily. ... Pt husband requested this nurse again to change inner cannula again this nurse educated pt to the JFK home care purpose. This nurse tried to educate pt on trach care pt husband refused "I do it everyday" ... This nurse advised pt that case manager will have to assess for further nursing needs as JFK has met the care plan goal, if husband is able to independently maintenance [sic] pt care. Pt husband ... was very irate yelling and pacing the floor pt husband came to provide trach care while starting [sic] asked this nurse "what are you here for then?" This nurse advised pt to educate, assess for further nursing needs and report to RN nurse case manager... Pt husband yelling into phone and at this nurse ordering to get out and not to come back. This nurse left with trach intact and patent with no s/s [sign/symptoms] of pain or distress ..."

c. On 8/18/20 at 12:00 PM, Staff #4 (Registered Nurse) visited the patient and documented in the Summary Narrative, " ... Received patient in bed AAO [awake, alert, oriented] x3 Resp [respiration] easy and regular. Tracheostomy dislodged ... CG [caregiver] instructed to call 911 for transport of pt to ED [emergency department] for eval [evaluation] and reinsertion of trach. Waited in home and monitored pt until EMTs [emergency medical technicians] arrived in home. Left pt stable and in no distress."

d. On 8/20/20 at 12:50 PM, Staff #4 stated that upon arrival, the patient's inner cannula was intact, however, the tracheostomy tube was lying on the patient's chest. The patient was in no distress. He/she stated that the patient's husband told him/her "the nurse left it like that and left the house."

e. Review of Staff #3's "Skills/Experience Checklist" form, a self assessment form of current skills and abilities, completed by Staff #3 and initiated on 12/4/2018, indicated that Staff #3 needed to review, "Tracheostomy care, changes and Suctioning technique." In addition, the Gastrointestinal/Nutrition section of the form, Staff #3 needed to review the following: 

"a. Checking placement of G [gastrostomy] ENG [Masco gastric] and button tube

b. Use of Kangaroo pump, equipment maintenance and teaching

c. Continuous feedings via G, ENG, and button tubes

d. Equipment maintenance and teaching

e. Ostomy management and teaching."

(i) Staff #3 checked off letter "C" in the "Previous Experience" section of the form, which indicates "I need to review this skill." 

(ii) The "Instruction, Review, or Skill Demonstration" section of the Skills/Experience Checklist form states, "Supervisor: indicates whether or not a review of policies/procedures or instruction is required then document completion in the appropriate columns. If C or D is selected, review the instruction and possibly the skill demonstration is required prior to assignment to applicable patient."

(iii) Staff #3's Skills/Experience Checklist form lacked evidence of instruction and/or that the skills demonstration was performed related to tracheostomy care, changes and suctioning technique, or gastrostomy placement, the use of the Kangaroo pump, continuous feeding via G tube, equipment maintenance and teaching, and Ostomy management and teaching prior to a patient assignment, as required by the above reference. 

f. Review of subsequent RN nursing visit notes dated 8/6/20, 8/7/20, and 8/10/20, revealed that trach care was performed, however, there was no evidence that the patient's caregiver was involved in the trach care of the patient or demonstrated any independence with patient care. There was no evidence of education related to trach care on 8/7/20 and 8/10/20. 

g. The above was confirmed by Staff #1. 

In the afternoon of 8/20/20 an Immediate Jeopardy (IJ) was identified. The facility was notified of the IJ and the IJ template was provided. An IJ Removal Plan was accepted on 8/21/20. 

On 8/28/20, a visit to the facility was performed to evaluate implementation of the removal plan. The facility fully implemented the removal plan and the IJ was removed.
