source_record.Facility Name: MERCER CARE PARTNERS MEDICAL HOME HEALTH CARE, LLC
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on staff interview, and review of CDC guidance, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure visitors are screened for COVID-19 with temperature checks and COVID-19 screening questions, prior to entry into the facility.

Findings include:

Reference: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Interim Infection Prevention and Control Recommendations for Healthcare Personnel During the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Pandemic, https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/hcp/infection-control-recommendations. html, updated February 10, 2021 states, "... Establish a process to ensure everyone (patients, healthcare personnel, and visitors) entering the facility is assessed for symptoms of COVID-19 or exposure to others with suspected or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection... ."

1. Upon arrival to the facility on 3/24/21 at 9:45 AM, the survey team was greeted by Staff #9. He/she asked the survey team about the nature of the visit, then alerted Staff #1 about the visit. Staff #1 escorted the survey team into a conference room at 10:00 AM.

a. Staff #1 and Staff #9 did not perform temperature checks on the survey team or ask the survey team COVID-19 screening questions.

b. Temperature checks or COVID-19 screening questions were not conducted for the survey team upon their arrival to the facility on 3/25/21 and 3/26/21.

2. Upon interview on 3/26/21 at 9:40 AM, Staff #2 confirmed the facility does not have a COVID-19 screening policy for visitors. He/she stated, "Because we really don't get visitors, we haven't really thought about it."

3. Staff #1 and Staff #2 confirmed the above findings on 3/26/21 at 1:42 PM.

B. Based on three (3) of five (5) observations, staff interview, and review of facility policies, it was determined the facility failed to ensure staff perform handwashing for a minimum of fifteen (15) seconds, between glove changes, and prior to entering the bag.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, "Hand Hygiene" states, "... 2. If hands are not visibly soiled... use an alcohol-based hand rub for routinely decontaminating hands in all other clinical situations... at the beginning and end of all procedures (i.e. wound care...)... after contact with body fluids or excretions... and wound dressings if hands are not visibly soiled... if moving from a contaminated-body site to a clean-body site during patient care... after removing gloves... IV. Procedure... When washing hands with soap and water... rub hands together vigorously for at least 15 seconds... ."

Reference #2: Facility policy, "Bag Technique and Equipment" states, "... F. Use hand hygiene before removing contents of the bag. If additional equipment/supplies are needed from the bag during the visit, the hand hygiene procedure should be repeated if hands have come in contact with blood or body fluids or contaminated materials. ... ."

1. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 3/25/21 at 9:35 AM, the following was observed:

a. At 9:40 AM, Staff #3 washed his/her hands for nine (9) seconds.

b. At 10:05 AM, Staff #3 washed his/her hands for eight (8) seconds.

2. During a home visit for Patient #4 on 3/25/21 at 12:00 PM, the following was observed:

a. At 12:10 PM, Staff #6 was preparing to perform wound care on the patient's stage 2 sacral ulcer. While wearing gloves, Staff #6 cleaned fecal matter from the patient's rectum and buttocks. He/she then doffed his/her gloves, donned a new pair of gloves, and began measuring the wound. 

(i) Staff #6 did not perform hand hygiene after doffing his/her contaminated gloves and prior to donning a new pair of gloves.

b. At 12:11 PM, Staff #6 doffed his/her gloves, then entered the bag and retrieved a pen and additional gloves. After using the pen to write down the wound measurements, Staff #6 donned the new gloves and began to clean the patient's wound. 

(i) Staff #6 did not perform hand hygiene after doffing his/her gloves, before entering the bag, or prior to donning a new pair of gloves. 

3. During a home visit for Patient #5 on 3/25/21 at 11:40 AM, the following was observed:

a. At 11:58 PM, Staff #7 washed his/her hands for eleven (11) seconds.

b. At 12:02 PM, 12:03 PM, 12:04 PM, 12:05 PM, 12:09 PM, 12:10 PM and 12:11 PM, Staff #7 donned and doffed gloves without performing hand hygiene.

c. At 12:14 PM, Staff #7 washed his/her hands for eight (8) seconds.

4. Staff #1 and Staff #2 confirmed the above findings on 3/26/21 at 1:42 PM.

C. Based on staff interview, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that regular communication and updated CDC Guidelines are shared with staff in order to prevent the transmission of COVD-19.

1. Upon request to Staff #1, the Administrator, on 3/24/2021 for COVID-19 communication documents for 2020, eleven (11) months of Nursing Meeting notes were presented to this surveyor on 3/25/2021. 

 a. The topic of COVID-19 was on the agenda three (3) times; March, April, and November of 2020.

2. Staff #1 and Staff #2 confirmed the above findings on 3/26/21 at 10:50 PM.

source_record.Facility Name: MERCER CARE PARTNERS MEDICAL HOME HEALTH CARE, LLC
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection control
CFR(s): 484.70(b)(1)(2)
Standard: Control.  

The HHA must maintain a coordinated agency-wide program for the surveillance, identification, prevention, control, and investigation of infectious and communicable diseases that is an integral part of the HHA's quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program. The infection control program must include:



(1) A method for identifying infectious and communicable disease problems; and



(2) A plan for the appropriate actions that are expected to result in improvement and disease prevention.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on random observation, staff interview, and review of facility policies and procedures, it was determined that the facility failed to develop policies and procedures addressing prevention and control strategies to mitigate the spread of COVID-19. 

Findings include:

1. During the entrance conference on 3/24/21 at 10:10 AM, Staff #1 confirmed that the facility follows the CDC for its infection control guidelines.

a. Upon arrival to the facility on 3/24/21, 3/25/21, and 3/26/21, temperature checks and COVID-19 screening questions were not performed for the survey team. 

(i) Upon interview on 3/26/21 at 9:40 AM, Staff #2 confirmed the facility does not have a COVID-19 screening policy for visitors.

b. During the entrance conference on 3/24/21 at 10:25 AM, Staff #2 stated that the facility does not admit COVID-19 positive patients. He/she also stated that all new admissions are placed on a fourteen (14) day quarantine and monitored for symptoms of COVID-19 and that staff are required to wear N95 masks for the first fourteen (14) days when visiting new patients.

(i) During a home visit for Patient #1 on 3/24/21 at 2:55 PM, Staff #4 was asked if he/she wears an N95 mask for new patients. Staff #4 stated, "If the patients are a hospital or rehab referral, then we wear an N95 mask. If the patient is a community referral, then we just wear our regular masks."

(ii) During a home visit for Patient #2 on 3/25/21 at 10:23 AM, Staff #3 was asked if he/she wears an N95 mask for new patients. Staff #3 stated, "When the patients come from a rehab or a hospital, we have to wear an N95 for fourteen (14) days. Other than that, we wear our regular masks."

(iii) During a home visit for Patient #4 on 3/25/21 at 12:40 PM, Staff #6 was asked if he/she wears an N95 mask for new patients. Staff #6 stated, "We wear an N95 for fourteen (14) days when the patient comes from a hospital or rehab. I don't think we have to wear it when the patient comes from the doctor's office, but I wear mine anyway."

d. A request was made to Staff #1 on 3/24/21 for the facility's policy on PPE and the use of N95 facemasks. Staff #1 and Staff #2 confirmed that the facility does not have a policy on PPE or on the use of N95 facemasks. 

e. During the entrance conference on 3/24/21 at 10:30 AM, a request was made to Staff #1 and Staff #2 for the following COVID-19 and infection control related policies and procedures: COVID-19 testing for patients and staff, employees returning to work after COVID-19 exposure or positive diagnosis, and the reporting of communicable diseases. No policies and procedures were provided. 

f. On greater than four (4) occasions between 3/24/21 and 3/26/21, Staff #9 was observed sitting at his/her desk without wearing a facemask. Staff #9's desk is located in an open common area near the entrance to the facility. Staff members were observed walking past Staff #8's desk while he/she was not wearing his/her facemask. Staff #8, whose desk is near Staff #9's desk, was present at his/her desk while Staff #9 was not wearing his/her mask.g. source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Conformance with physician orders
CFR(s): 484.60(b)
Standard: Conformance with physician or allowed practitioner orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on staff interview, review of one (1) of one (1) medical record (#6) with a home health aide ordered, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure home health aide services are provided in conformance with physicians orders.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy titled, "Physician's Orders" states, "...Orders for treatment not on the Plan of Care must be secured prior to: 1. Any change/variation from the original Plan of Care... 3. Delay in start of Care..."

1. Upon review of Medical Record #6, the following was noted:

a. The patients start of care was 10/17/21. The Home Health Aide was ordered two times a week for seven weeks.

(i) The patient did not receive home health aide services from 10/17/21 through 10/29/21.

b. On 10/29/21, a physician order states, "Delay in Home Health Aide Services until November 3, 2021."

(i) The patient did not receive home health aide services from 11/3/21 through 11/9/21. The patient was admitted to the hospital on 11/9/21.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #17 on 11/10/21 at 1:00 PM.

N.J.A.C. 8:42-6.2(a)2

B. Based on the review of one (1) out of four (4) medical records (#8), review of facility policy and procedure, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the physician is notified of a change in the patient's plan of care. 

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy titled, "Provision of Care" states, "...It is the policy of the Home Health Agency to secure written orders for all clients... The agency accepts physician certification and recertification of plans of care, as well as signed orders changing the plan of care... PROCESS: Orders for treatment not on the Plan of Care must be secured prior to: 1. Any change/variation from the original Plan of Care... 2. Missed visits with change in frequency..."

1. The medical record of Patient #8 was reviewed, and the following was identified:

a. A Start of Care (SoC) for 9/22/21

b. An order for Skilled Nurse (SN) visits written on 9/22/21 for a frequency of "1WK6" (1 time per week for 6 weeks)

c. During the week of 10/10/21 to 10/16/21, the calendar identified that an SN visit was scheduled for 10/13/21, but the medical record lacked a visit note indicating that a SN visit was made.

2. An interview on 11/9/21 at 1:29 PM with Staff #17, a manager, confirmed the above findings and that the medical record lacked further documentation of communication to the physician regarding the missed visit on 10/13/21.

N.J.A.C. 8.42-6.2(a)(6)

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interviews, and review of nationally recognized infection control guidelines, it was determined the facility failed to adhere to acceptable standards of practice for hand hygiene during wound care. 

Findings include:

Reference: Guideline for Hand Hygiene in Health Care Settings: Recommendation of the Healthcare Infection Control Practices Advisory Committee [HICPAC] and the HICPAC/SHEA/APIC/IDSA Hand Hygiene Task Force, published in the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report at MMWR 2002; 51 (No. RR-16) states, "... Recommendations: 1.  Indications for Handwashing and Hand antisepsis... I. Decontaminate hands after contact with inanimate objects... in the immediate vicinity of the patient."

1. During a home visit for Patient #3, on 11/8/21, the following was observed:

a. At 12:57 PM, Staff #3 was performing wound care on the patient's left heel. Staff #3 placed a plastic bag on the floor near him/her to use for trash. With gloved hands, Staff #3 used saline to clean the wound, then took his/her left hand and moved the plastic bag closer to him/her. Staff #3 then continued with wound care.

b. Staff #3 failed to doff his/her contaminated gloves and perform hand hygiene prior to resuming wound care.

2. Staff #1 and Staff #2 confirmed the above finding on 11/10/21 at 11:00 AM.

N.J.A.C. 8:42-12.3(a)

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection control
CFR(s): 484.70(b)(1)(2)
Standard: Control.  

The HHA must maintain a coordinated agency-wide program for the surveillance, identification, prevention, control, and investigation of infectious and communicable diseases that is an integral part of the HHA's quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program. The infection control program must include:



(1) A method for identifying infectious and communicable disease problems; and



(2) A plan for the appropriate actions that are expected to result in improvement and disease prevention.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and review of Centers of Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidance, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that a process for notifying the local health department about known or suspected cases of COVID-19 within the facility, is developed.

Findings include:

Reference: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Clinical Questions about COVID-19: Questions and Answers, https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/hcp/faq.html, updated November 17, 2021 states, "... Healthcare facilities should have a process for notifying the health department about known or suspected cases of SARS-CoV-2 infection, and should establish a plan, in consultation with local public health authorities, for how exposures in a healthcare facility will be investigated... ." 

1. Upon interview on 11/10/21 at 10:00 AM, Staff #1 confirmed that the facility does not have a process or plan for reporting known or suspected cases of COVID-19 to the local health department. Staff #1 stated, "Because we don't test here and symptomatic patients and staff are tested elsewhere, we did not think we needed to report to the local health department."

N.J.A.C. 8:42-12.2(b)2

source_record.Facility Name: PROMISE CARE OF HUDSON COUNTY LLC
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Coordinate care delivery
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(4)
Coordinate care delivery to meet the patient's needs, and involve the patient, representative (if any), and caregiver(s), as appropriate, in the coordination of care activities.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of two (2) of two (2) medical records (#3, #13) reviewed to assess coordination of care, staff interviews, caregiver interview, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that coordination of care with the medical social worker (MSW) is conducted to meet the needs of the patient.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Care Coordination" states, "... 3. Coordinate care delivery to meet the patient's needs and involve the patient and caregivers as appropriate in coordination of care activities."

1. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 11/8/21 at 12:35 PM, Staff #3 stated that the patient's son called him/her and stated that the patient was having a hard time with his/her illness. Staff #3 stated, "The patient's not doing well. He's been in and out of the hospital for his diabetes. He's having a hard time mentally because he's so young and he's worried what will happen if he can't do his job while he's sick. He's the superintendent of the building he lives in. I'm also trying to help him find an endocrinologist. There's not a lot of them in this area. One didn't take his insurance and another gave him an appointment in March. He's having a tough time."

2. Review of the medical record of Patient #3 lacked evidence that Staff #3, who indicated that he/she was aware that the patient "was not doing well" mentally, notified the physician or coordinated care with the MSW to assist with the mental and emotional needs of the patient. 

3. Upon interview on 11/10/21 at 11:30 AM, Staff #1 indicated that Patient #3 should have been referred to a social worker. 

4. During a home visit for Patient #13 on 11/9/21, in the presence of Staff #15, a caregiver interview was conducted at 12:20 PM. Patient #13's caregiver indicated that she needed a home health aide (HHA) because caring for her spouse was hard and she needed help. The patient's caregiver was asked if she notified the nurse that she needed an HHA. The patient's caregiver stated, "A nurse only came one time. I told her last Thursday about needing help, but I haven't heard anything since. I also told 'that guy.' He doesn't speak Spanish, so I don't know his name." 

5. Review of Medical Record #13 revealed the following:

a. Client Coordination Note dated 11/3/21 states, "MSW had visit with patient and caregiver. Patient would benefit from referral for PCA at this time. MSW reviewed Medicaid eligibility and guidelines, patient eligible at this time. MSW referred patient at visit to Hudson County ABD Medicaid Office for application to be sent to patient home via mail. ... ."

b. There was no evidence in the medical record that the MSW coordinated care with the nurse or physician to notify them that the patient or caregiver was requesting HHA services. 

c. There was no evidence in the medical record that HHA services were ordered or conducted for Patient #13.

6. Upon interview on 11/9/21 at 11:30 AM, Staff #2 confirmed that the facility uses a staffing agency for home health aides. He/she stated, "We use [name of staffing agency] for HHA services. We have been trying to recruit, but we cannot find anyone. We don't have any of our own HHAs."

7. Upon interview on 11/10/21 at 11:00 AM, Staff #1 indicated that a PCA was a companion service provided through Medicaid for qualifying families. Staff #1 stated that if a family requests HHA services, and the facility is unsuccessful obtaining an HHA through the staffing agency, they will refer the patient for PCA services through the Medicaid office. He/she stated that staff will complete coordination notes indicating their attempts to get an HHA through the staffing agency and subsequent referral for PCA services, if needed.

8. Upon interview on 11/10/21 at 11:00 AM, Staff #1 confirmed that there was no evidence that an attempt was made to provide Patient #13 with HHA services through the staffing agency.  

N.J.A.C. 8:42-7.3(b)2

source_record.Facility Name: PROMISE CARE OF HUDSON COUNTY LLC
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:

A. Based on observation, staff interview, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that all staff adhere to acceptable standards of practice to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "Infection Prevention and Control - Sharps" states, "... Procedure: ... Equipment: Agency-supplied sharp safety devices appropriate for the services provided, for example: ... Sharps disposal container meeting OSHA standards for both staff and patient use. ... After Care: ... 2. The sharps container is to be replaced routinely when three-quarters full and should not be allowed to overfill or be opened, ..."

Credence #2: OSHA 29 CFR part 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(1) states, "Contaminated sharps shall be discarded immediately or as soon as feasible in containers that are: 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(1)(ii) Puncture resistant; 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(1)(iv) Labeled or color coded ..." 

Reference #3: Facility handout to patients/family from 'SafeNeedleDisposal.org': "What to Do with Used Sharps in New Jersey" notes - "Put used sharps in a strong, plastic container. ..." 

1. During a home visit for Patient #2 the following was revealed:

a. Review of the "Home Health Certification and Plan of Care" document, Patient #2's start of care (SoC) date was 11/2/18. The "Orders of Discipline and Treatments" included: Blood Glucose testing and supplies - Glucometer. 

b. On 11/26/18, Staff #5, a registered nurse (RN) and the patient's private home health aide, observed and assisted the patient in performing a glucose fingerstick to check his/her blood glucose levels. 

(i) A small empty water bottle and an empty deli-like food container were being used as sharps containers. The container was more than three-quarters full.

(ii) The patient's private aide took the top of the deli-like food container off and attempted to empty the used lancets into his/her hand. Staff #5 stopped the aide and provided teaching regarding safe handling of used/contaminated sharps.

c. The pamphlet provided to patients/families by staff, "What to Do with Used Sharps in New Jersey" has an illustrated picture of small water bottles and a large soda bottle with a circle and line through it, indicating not to be used. 

d. From the start of care on 11/28/18, the facility failed to monitor and ensure that the patient and/or caregiver was provided the appropriate education regarding infection prevention; and that proper supplies for sharps were provided or approved for safe storage, handling and disposal. 

(i) There was no documented evidence that sharps containers were routinely replaced, when three-quarters full, by any visiting staff.

2. During a home visit for Patient #3, the following was revealed:

a. As per the "Home Health Certification and Plan of Care" document, Patient #2's start of care (SoC) date was 11/2/18. The "Orders of Discipline and Treatments" included: Blood Glucose testing and supplies - Glucometer. 

b. On 11/27/18, Staff #6, an RN, supplied the patient with a sharps container provided by the agency, however, there was no evidence or documentation in the patient's medical record that a sharps container was provided at a prior time and/or that another designated sharps container was being used and/or identified since the start of care. 

3. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #1, Staff #2, Staff #8 and Staff #12. 

Reference #4: Facility policy titled "Bag Protocol" states: "... Standards: ... 2. Bag and contents should be given thorough cleansing with sanitizer as necessary... 9. Clean equipment according to protocol before returning it to bag. ..."

1. On 11/27/18, during observation of the cleaning and disinfecting of reusable equipment used during the home visit of Patient #3, the following was revealed:

a. Staff #6 placed his/her stethoscope on a napkin in the area he/she designated as work space, then proceeded to spray the stethoscope with "Sanizide." 

(i) Staff #6 then placed an unsanitized blood pressure cuff on top of the sanitized stethoscope, sprayed both sides of the blood pressure cuff and then placed it back on top of the stethoscope therefore contaminating it. 

(ii) Staff #6 did not re-disinfect the stethoscope. 

2. On 11/28/18, Staff #12 explained the cleaning of equipment from the staff members bags protocol, and indicated that it is provided by the facility through demonstration and observation of the staff members technique in accordance with facility approved disinfectants. The training is provided during initial orientation, annual training and on an "as needed basis." Staff #12 was unable to provide a written protocol. 

3. Staff #12 confirmed the above described practice was not in accordance with the protocol. 

Reference #5: Facility policy titled "Hand Washing Policy" states, "... INDICATIONS FOR HANDWASHING AND HAND ANTISEPSIS: ... C. If gloves are changed during a procedure and hands are not visibly soiled, waterless antiseptic hand cleaner may be used to decontaminate hands between glove changes..." 

1. During a home visit for Patient #1 on 11/26/2018, the following was observed:

a. At approximately 12:35 PM, during a wound vac dressing change, Staff #3 donned non-sterile gloves, removed the soiled wound vac dressing from patient's sacral area. 

(i) Staff #3 then handled the clean black foam, touched the wound and changed gloves. 

(ii) Staff #3 proceeded to pack the wound and cover the sacral area with clear dressing and changed gloves.

b. Staff #3 failed to perform hand hygiene in between glove changes during wound care activity. 

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1.

HH aide supervision elements
CFR(s): 484.80(h)(4)(i-vi)
Home health aide supervision must ensure that aides furnish care in a safe and effective manner, including, but not limited to, the following elements:

(i) Following the patient's plan of care for completion of tasks assigned to a home health aide by the registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional;

(ii) Maintaining an open communication process with the patient, representative (if any), caregivers, and family;

source_record.Deficiency Description: Development Of Ep Policies And Procedures
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Development of EP Policies and Procedures
CFR(s): 484.102(b)
§403.748(b), §416.54(b), §418.113(b), §441.184(b), §460.84(b), §482.15(b), §483.73(b), §483.475(b), §484.102(b), §485.68(b), §485.625(b), §485.727(b), §485.920(b), §486.360(b), §491.12(b), §494.62(b).



(b) Policies and procedures. [Facilities] must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 



*[For LTC facilities at §483.73(b):] Policies and procedures. The LTC facility must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least annually.



*Additional Requirements for PACE and ESRD Facilities:



*[For PACE at §460.84(b):] Policies and procedures.  The PACE organization must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must address management of medical and nonmedical emergencies, including, but not limited to: Fire; equipment, power, or water failure; care-related emergencies; and natural disasters likely to threaten the health or safety of the participants, staff, or the public.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 



*[For ESRD Facilities at §494.62(b):] Policies and procedures.  The dialysis facility must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. These emergencies include, but are not limited to, fire, equipment or power failures, care-related emergencies, water supply interruption, and natural disasters likely to occur in the facility's geographic area.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of three (3) of four (4) medical records (#1, #2, #4) reviewed for the patient's emergency preparedness plan, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure a patient-specific Emergency Preparedness plan is developed, reviewed with the client or caretaker, kept in the home, and entered in the medical record.

2. Review of Medical Record #2 on 1/27/22 lacked evidence that a patient-specific emergency preparedness plan was developed and reviewed with the patient or his/her caretaker.

3. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 1/25/2022 at 2:00 PM, the following was indicated:

a. Review of the patient's folder revealed that the emergency preparedness form was present, however, noted to be blank. 

b. At 2:35 PM, Patient #2's caregiver stated that facility staff did not discuss an emergency preparedness plan with him/her.

4. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #7 and Staff #13 on 1/27/22.

5. Review of Medical Record #4 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

a. In the Emergency Preparedness section of the electronic medical record (EMR), the tab marked "Evacuation Location" states, "Neighbors."

i. The evacuation location does not indicate a specific evacuation address the patient will be evacuated to in the event of an emergency.

b. There was no evidence in the medical record that a patient-specific emergency preparedness plan was developed and reviewed with the patient or his/her caretaker. 

6. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1, Staff #2, and Staff #6 on 1/27/22.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy titled, "0-9197 Emergency Management Program and Plan-Home Health, Medicare Certified Home Care and Hospice Offices" states, "...4.1.3 Client-Specific Emergency Plans. ... 4.1.3.1 As part of the comprehensive assessment, the admitting clinician will develop a Client-Specific Emergency Plan by entering the information into the electronic record... At each reassessment, the Client-Specific Emergency Plan will be reviewed with the client/responsible party and updated if necessary. The Client-Specific Emergency Plan will include specific instructions for the client. 4.1.3.3 A copy of the Client-Specific Emergency Plan will be kept in the client's home and a copy will be returned to the paper office electronic office chart. ... ."

1. Review of Medical Record #1 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

i. The evacuation location does not indicate the name or address of the rehab the patient will be evacuated to in the event of an emergency.

Conformance with physician orders
CFR(s): 484.60(b)
Standard: Conformance with physician or allowed practitioner orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of six (6) of seventeen (17) medical records (#2, #3, #4, #10, #15, #18), staff interviews, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure documentation of missed visits and physician notification of missed visits, are documented in the patient's medical record.

Findings include:

 

Reference: Facility policy titled, "0-6277 Missed Visits/Hours" states, "...1.1 Physician Ordered Services. The physician must be notified when the plan of care is altered due to fewer visits or hours of service being provided as ordered. Notification of the missed visits/hours is timely, and as directed on a schedule determined in collaboration with the physician. 1.1.1 Documentation-Home Health (visits) & Hospice. 1.1.1.1 Missed Visit Notification note to capture the reason that the visit was missed as well as evidence that the physician was informed verbally or by fax...of this variation from the plan of care must be entered in the electronic record."

 

1. Review of Medical Record #2 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

 

a. The Home Health Plan of Care effective 12/19/21 states, "HHA (Home Health Aid) 2wk1 (two times per week for one week), 3wk1 (three times per week for one week), 2wk2 (two times per week for two weeks)."  

 

i. During the week of 12/19/21, there was one (1) missed HHA visit. There was no evidence of a Missed Visit Notification note indicating why the visit was missed. There was no evidence that the physician was notified of the missed visit.

 

ii. During the week of 12/26/21, there were two (2) missed HHA visits. There was no evidence of Missed Visit Notification notes indicating why the visits were missed. There was no evidence that the physician was notified of the missed visits. 

 

iii. During the week of 1/9/22, there was one (1) missed HHA visit. There was no evidence of a Missed Visit Notification note indicating why the visit was missed. There was no evidence that the physician was notified of the missed visit.

 

2. Review of Medical Record #3 on 1/26/22 revealed the following:

 

a. The Home Health Plan of Care effective 11/16/21 states, "HHA 2wk2 (twice a week for two weeks) effective 12/5/21; HHA 2wk1 (twice a week for one week) effective 12/19/21." A Missed Visit Notification note documented on 12/20/21 indicated a HHA missed visit occurred on 12/13/21. There was no evidence the physician was notified of the missed visit.

 

b. A HHA note dated 12/27/21 indicated the HHA missed a visit on 12/27/21. There was no evidence the physician was notified of the missed visit.

 

c. Staff #2 confirmed that there was no evidence the physician was notified of the missed visits on 1/26/22 at 12:54 PM.

 

3. Review of Medical Record #4 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

 

a. The Home Health Plan of Care effective 1/3/22 states, “HHA 1wk1 (one time a week for one week), 2wk5 (two times a week for five weeks)."

 

i. During the week of 1/3/22, there was one (1) missed HHA visit. There was no evidence that the physician was notified of the missed visit.

 

ii. During the week of 1/9/22, there were two (2) missed HHA visits. There was no evidence that the physician was notified of the missed visits.

 

b. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #1, Staff #2, and Staff #6 on 1/27/22. 

 

4. Review of Medical Record #10 on 1/26/22 revealed the following:

 

a. The Home Health Plan of Care effective 11/28/21 states, "HHA 1wk1 (once per week for one week), 2wk4 (twice per week for four weeks)." 

 

b. For week 12/5/21 to 12/11/21, there were no HHA visits made. A HHA note dated 12/8/21 indicated the HHA missed a visit on 12/8/21. There was no evidence the physician was notified of the missed visit.

 

c. There was no evidence of a Missed Visit Notification note or physician notification for the second HHA visit missed during the week of 12/5/21 to 12/11/21.

 

d. On 1/26/22 at 3:10 PM, Staff #2 confirmed that there was no evidence of a Missed Visit Notification note or evidence of physician notification of the missed visits.

 

5. Review of Medical Record #15 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

 

a. The Home Health Plan of Care effective 8/11/21 states, "SN (Skilled Nurse) 2wk4 (twice per week for four weeks), 1wk5 (once per week for five weeks)."

 

b. A Missed Visit Notification note indicated that the SN missed a visit on 9/7/21. There was no evidence the physician was notified of the missed visit.

 

c. On 1/27/22 at 11:30 AM, Staff #2 confirmed that there was no evidence the physician was notified of the missed visit. 

 

6. Review of Medical Record #18 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

 

a.  The Home Health Plan of Care states, "PT (Physical Therapy), 3wk2 (three times per week for two weeks)."

 

i. During the week of 8/8/21, there was one (1) missed PT visit. There was no evidence of a Missed Visit Notification note indicating why the visit was missed. There was no evidence that the physician was notified of the missed visit.

 

7. The above findings were confirmed on 1/26/22 and 1/27/22 by Staff #12 and Staff #13.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interviews, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure N95 face masks are worn when caring for patients with symptoms of COVID-19.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility document, "COVID-19 Safety Strategies" states, "... Universal Masking: We encourage willing family members to wear a mask, although we do not require clients or household members to wear a mask. ... We are still able to safely provide care as long as our clinicians are following our PPE standards based on client/household scenario per our PPE Standards-at-a-Glance."

Reference #2: Facility document, "[Name of facility] PPE Standard At-A-Glance As of 11/1/21" states, "... Clients with symptoms or COVID-19-positive or awaiting rest results with symptoms... N95 mask; Eye protection (goggles/face shield); Contact protection (gown/gloves)."

1. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 1/26/22, in the presence of Staff #8, the following was observed:

a. Upon entry into the patient's home, Staff #8 was wearing a surgical mask, face shield, and goggles. Patient #3 was not wearing a face mask.

b. During a patient interview at 10:00 AM, Patient #3 indicated he/she was taking a new medication for "a runny nose, sore throat, sneezing, and coughing." Staff #8 continued the home visit wearing a surgical mask, face shield, and goggles.

c. Staff #8 failed to don an N95 mask or gown after the patient indicated he/she had symptoms consistent with COVID-19.

2. Staff #1 and Staff #2 confirmed the above findings on 1/27/22 at 2:00 PM.

Verbal orders
CFR(s): 484.60(b)(3)(4)
(3) Verbal orders must be accepted only by personnel authorized to do so by applicable state laws and regulations and by the HHA's internal policies.



(4) When services are provided on the basis of a physician or allowed practitioner's verbal orders, a nurse acting in accordance with state licensure requirements, or other qualified practitioner responsible for furnishing or supervising the ordered services, in accordance with state law and the HHA's policies, must document the orders in the patient's clinical record, and sign, date, and time the orders. Verbal orders must be authenticated and dated by the physician or allowed pracitioner in accordance with applicable state laws and regulations, as well as the HHA's internal policies.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interview, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure physician's sign all verbal orders, in accordance with facility policy.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy titled, "Physician's Orders" states, "... 6.0 When changes in orders are received verbally from the physician...the verbal order received is sent to the physician for signature. ... ."

1. Review of Medical Record #6 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

a. A physician's order dated 1/5/22 at 3:57 PM states, "...Verbal order: Y [yes]...Order Description: Change physical therapy visit to telephone call."

i. Upon interview on 1/27/22 at 11:35 AM, Staff #2 confirmed the order dated, 1/5/22 at 3:57 PM, was a verbal order. 

b. There was no evidence that the physician signed the verbal order. On the physician order form next to the section labeled "Physician Signature" it states, "Do not send." There was no physician signature on the form.

N.J.A.C. 8:42-6.2

Integrate all services
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(3)
Integrate services, whether services are provided directly or under arrangement, to assure the identification of patient needs and factors that could affect patient safety and treatment effectiveness and the coordination of care provided by all disciplines.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interviews, review of two (2) of two (2) medical records (#1, #4) of patients requiring case coordination, and review of facility policies and procedures, it was determined the facility failed to ensure integrative services are provided to all patients.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "Fall Prevention Program" states, “… Assessment Principles… Does the client need any assistive devices to improve safety?”

Reference #2: Facility policy titled, "Client Care Coordination" states, “… Case coordination involves identification of additional services needed, contacting community resources for these services… Integrating services, whether services are provided directly or under arrangement, to assure the identification of client needs and factors that could affect client safety and treatment effectiveness and coordination of care provided by all disciplines.”

1. Review of Medical Record #1 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

a. The Initial Assessment Physical Therapy note on 1/11/22 states, “… Safety Measures… Fall Precautions… Client is a 77-year-old female admitted to [name of hospital] on 12/24/21 following a fall at home. Client reports… lost her balance and unable to get up. She crawled on her knees to get her phone to call her son. … client lives alone… cannot afford to get a life alert… .”  

b. There was no evidence in the medical record that the physical therapist notified the nurse or medical social worker about the patient's financial need for assistance in obtaining a life alert device for safety.

c. The above finding was confirmed with Staff #6 on 1/27/22 at 11:00 AM. 

2. Review of Medical Record #4 on 1/27/22 revealed the following:

a. The Initial Assessment Physical Therapy note on 1/3/22 states, “… Presents with reported 10–20-pound weight loss but denies need for referral to RD (Registered Dietician). Using Ensure… Patient is at a high nutritional risk.”  

b. The Medical Social Worker visit note on 1/10/22 states, “… Nutritional… Client underweight due to emotional or physical issue… MSW (Medical Social Worker)… encouraged client to speak with the nurse, he is currently paying under the table, in order to provide him with more regular help throughout the week. MSW provided client with 3 private duty home care agencies.”

c. The Occupational Therapy visit note on 1/14/22 states, “… Client reports he is not eating enough because it is difficult to feed himself.”

d. There was no evidence that the facility provided skilled nursing or a registered dietician to evaluate the patient and determine his/her needs. 

e. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2 on 1/27/22 at 11:00 AM.

This facility is in compliance with 42 CFR Condition of Participation for Home Health Agencies 484.75: Skilled Professional Services. Standard level deficiencies were identified.

Interdisciplinary assessment of the patient
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(1)
Ongoing interdisciplinary assessment of the patient;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on staff interview, review of facility documentation, and review of five (5) medical records, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the re-evaluation of the patient's needs were communicated between the nursing staff and the physician in one (1) of five (5) medical records.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Policy titled, "Chart Data Requirements and Format - Home Health Practice" states, " ...4.10 NURSE'S NOTE - HOME HEALTH ... Nursing documentation should include the following information: a. Physical and psychological symptoms ... b. The care and services provided ... c. Any new service or treatment initiated d. Response to services ... e. Ongoing documentation of identified problems and any changes in the client's status ... g. Documentation of communication with the physician on a COORDINATION OF SERVICES (COS) NOTE ...".

Reference #2: Policy titled, "Client Care Coordination- NJ Medicare Certified Offices" states, "... Our Procedure: ...2.0 [Facility] regularly communicates with the client's physician or authorized individuals to ensure that care and services are coordinated..... Achieving care or service goals requires ongoing communication with client/caregiver(s), physician and other employees providing care. Communication must be: a. Appropriate to the needs and abilities of the client b. Inclusive of all employees providing care, and c. Timely and relevant to the care and services being provided....."

1. On 2/4/2021, the medical record of Patient #1 was reviewed and the following was identified:

a. A Client Coordination Note Report written by Staff #4, a nurse, on 10/26/2020, stated a urine sample from Patient #1 was dropped off at a local laboratory and the results were to be given to Staff #7, a physician.

c. A Client Coordination Note Report written by Staff #8, a nurse, on 12/3/2020 revealed the patient's family member inquiring about the results of the urinalysis, and Staff #8 indicated that he/she would reach out to the physician.

d. A Client Coordination Note Report written by Staff #9, a nurse, on 12/3/2020 revealed that Patient #1 was admitted to a local hospital with a diagnosis of metabolic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, and a urinary tract infection.

2. The medical record of Patient #1 lacked evidence of the communication between the physician and the nursing staff regarding the patient's urinalysis results.

3. An interview with Staff #2, an administrator, on 2/4/2021 confirmed that there was a lack of coordination of care between the physician and the nursing staff regarding the results of the patient's urinalysis and ongoing urinary issues.

B. Based on staff interview, review of facility documentation, and the review of five (5) medical records, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure the nursing notes did not reflect the care that was provided to the patient in one (1) of five (5) medical records.

Findings include:

Reference: Policy titled, "Chart Data Requirements and Format - Home Health Practice" states, " ...4.10 NURSE'S NOTE - HOME HEALTH ... Nursing documentation should include the following information: a. Physical and psychological symptoms ... b. The care and services provided ... c. Any new service or treatment initiated d. Response to services ... e. Ongoing documentation of identified problems and any changes in the client's status ... g. Documentation of communication with the physician on a COORDINATION OF SERVICES (COS) NOTE ...".

1. On 2/4/2021, the medical record of Patient #3 was reviewed, and a Visit Note Report written by Staff #6 on 11/20/2020, indicated that Staff #6 made a PRN (as needed) RN (registered nurse) visit due to a Foley catheter check.

a. The Visit Note Report did not contain documentation of what interventions and care were provided by Staff #6 at the time of the visit. 

2. An interview with Staff #2, an administrator, confirmed that the note lacked documentation of the services provided by Staff #6 on the 11/20/2020 PRN visit.

Patient and caregiver education
CFR(s): 484.75(b)(5)
Patient and caregiver education;

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, review of facility documentation, and the review of five (5) medical records, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that the patient's family received communication regarding the patient's condition and evolving needs in one (1) out of five (5) medical records.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Policy titled, "Client Assessment and Reassessment" states, "...4.2 All other practices. Assessments and Reassessments will reflect, as appropriate: ...m. Availability of a willing an capable caretaker, n. Client/family expectations and perception of service...".

Reference #2: Policy titled, "Client Complaints" states, "...DOCUMENTATION. 4.1 All complaints, verbal and written, are documented in the applicable electronic system. This includes the nature of the complaint, the investigation findings, any follow-up action that is needed and the date of follow-up with the client....."

1. On 2/4/2021, the medical record of Patient #1 was reviewed, and the following was identified:

b. A Client Coordination Note Report written by Staff #4 on 11/9/2020 revealed the urinalysis results were not received by Staff #7, and that Staff #4 faxed the results to Staff #7's office.

c. A Client Coordination Note Report written by Staff #8, a nurse, on 12/3/2020 revealed the patient's family member inquiring about the results of the urinalysis, and Staff #8 indicated that he/she would reach out to the physician.

2. An interview with Staff #2, an administrator, on 2/4/2021 at 12:13 PM confirmed that the medical record lacked evidence of the results of the urinalysis being communicated with the patient's family.

3. A second interview with Staff #2 at 1:00 PM on 2/4/2021 confirmed that the family member had called the agency several times with concerns and complaints. Staff #2 stated that he/she had tried to call the family member twice to resolve the issue. Staff #2 confirmed that there was no documentation to support that the complaint was addressed by the agency.

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
This was a Federal Recertification survey that resulted in Standard level deficiencies.

Number of Home Visits made: 5

Medical Records reviewed: 8

Number of Staff interviewed: 16

Track adverse patient events
CFR(s): 484.65(c)(2)
Performance improvement activities must track adverse patient events, analyze their causes, and implement preventive actions.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and document review, it was determined that the facility failed to implement preventive actions for the tracked adverse patient event of falls.

Findings include:

1. On 2/5/19, the Atlantic County branch of the HHA provided evidence of tracking patient falls quarterly for the year 2018. 

a. Staff #7 confirmed on 2/5/19 at 1:27 PM that although falls are tracked and the causes are identified, the HHA branch was not actively completing quality assurance and performance improvement (QAPI) by discussing and implementing preventive actions.

2. On 2/6/19, the Camden County branch of the HHA provided evidence of tracking patient falls for the year 2018.

a. Staff #2 and Staff #3 confirmed on 2/6/19 that although falls are tracked and the causes are identified, the HHA branch was not actively completing QAPI by discussing and implementing preventive actions.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility policy and procedure, and staff interviews, it was determined that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to ensure that their infection prevention and control policies are implemented. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy titled, "Hand Hygiene," states, "... Indications for Hand Decontamination ...Before applying and after removing gloves ... Washing with antimicrobial soap ... Rub hands together in a rotary motion to create friction for at least 15 seconds. ..."

Reference #2: Facility policy titled, "Bag Technique," states, "... A supply bag is required for all field employees who take client care supplies from client home to client home. ... When care is complete, disinfect items ... place items on a clean barrier until dry ..."

Reference #3: Facility document titled, "The Visiting Nurse Associations of America 2014, Infusion Therapy - Central Line Type: PICC (Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter)," states, "D. Dressing Change ... Place sterile barrier on clean surface; open sterile items that are not in kit, and drop onto barrier. ... Slowly loosen transparent dressing ... Remove contaminated gloves, perform hand hygiene, and don new sterile gloves. ..."

Reference #4: Facility policy titled, "Field Employee Policies and Benefits," states, "... Clothing ... Overall appearance, and hygiene are expected to be crisp, clean and tidy. ... Ripped, frayed or disheveled clothing are not appropriate. ... Hair must be clean and controlled. Long hair must be pulled back when providing direct care. ..."

1. During a home visit for Patient #5 on 2/4/19, in the presence of Staff #4, the following was observed:

a. Staff #5 entered the patient's home wearing a stethoscope around his/her neck.

 b. Staff #5 did not carry the stethoscope in a supply bag, as required, for all field employees who take client care supplies from client home to client home. 

2. The above finding was confirmed with Staff #4.

3. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 2/4/19, in the presence of Staff #4, the following was observed:

a. Staff #6 performed a dressing change.

(i) Staff #6 washed his/her hands with antimicrobial soap. Staff #6 did not rub his/her hands together in a rotary motion to create friction for at least 15 seconds.

(ii) Staff #6 removed his/her gloves, picked up a box of gloves, placed the gloves on a table, and then performed hand hygiene.

(iii) Staff #6 did not have his/her hair pulled back when he/she was providing direct care.

(iv) Staff #6 completed care, disinfected the stethoscope and blood pressure cuff, and placed the items on an unclean barrier.

4. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #4.

5. During a home visit for Patient #5 on 2/5/19, in the presence of Staff #11, the following was observed:

a. Staff #12 washed his/her hands with antimicrobial soap. Staff #12 did not rub his/her hands together in a rotary motion to create friction for at least 15 seconds.

6. The above finding was confirmed with Staff #11.

7. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 2/5/19, in the presence of Staff #11, the following was observed:

a. Staff #13 performed a dressing change on the patient's PICC line. 

(i) Staff #13 opened the central line dressing kit and placed the sterile barrier on a clean counter. 

(ii) Staff #13 removed two items from the central line dressing kit and placed the items directly on the counter, then, Staff #13 picked the two items up from the counter and placed the items on the sterile barrier. 

(iii) Staff #13 removed the old dressing and applied the new dressing wearing the same pair of gloves.

(iv) Staff #13 did not remove the contaminated gloves, perform hand hygiene, and don new sterile gloves before applying the new dressing. 

8. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #11.

9. During a home visit for Patient #7 on 2/5/19 in the presence of Staff #10, the following was observed:

a. At 9:38 AM, Staff #8 entered the home of Patient #7.

(i) Staff #8's uniform pants were noted to have white residue on the lower legs, and the pants were also noted to have been ripped and frayed at the bottom of the pants. The ripped pants were dragging on the ground, and were observed to fall underneath Staff #8's shoes.

b. Staff #9 was observed at 9:41 AM removing 2 barriers from the home heath bag and placing them one on top of each other on a table in Patient #7's home. 

(i) Staff #9 removed the blood pressure cuff, thermometer, and stethoscope from the bag and placed the equipment on the top barrier.

(ii) Staff #9 measured the patient's blood pressure using the blood pressure cuff, took the patient's temperature with the thermometer, and then listened to the patient's back and abdomen with the stethoscope. Staff #9 returned the equipment to the top barrier after patient use.

c. At 9:56 AM, Staff #9 cleaned the blood pressure cuff, the thermometer, and the stethoscope, and placed the equipment back on the unclean top barrier. 

10. The above observations were confirmed with Staff #10.

HHA Comprehensive Assessment in Disaster
CFR(s): 484.102(b)(1)
§484.102(b)(1) Condition for Participation:

[(b) Policies and procedures.  The HHA must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 

At a minimum, the policies and procedures must address the following:]



(1) The plans for the HHA's patients during a natural or man-made disaster. Individual plans for each patient must be included as part of the comprehensive patient assessment, which must be conducted according to the provisions at §484.55.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of two (2) of three (3) medical records, review of facility documents, and staff interviews, it was determined that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to ensure that all patient's receive an individualized emergency plan as part of their comprehensive assessment.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, Plan of Care states, "... 2. The individualized plan of care includes the following... Plans for the patient during a natural or man-made disaster. ... ."

Reference #2: Facility policy, Emergency Preparedness Plan states, "... 1. All patients admitted to service will be educated at the start of care on emergency preparedness, the need for an individualized emergency plan, and how and when to contact local emergency officials. ... ."

1. During a home visit for Patient #1 on 5/20/19 at 11:50 AM, the following was indicated:

a. Upon interview at 12:05 PM, Patient #1 was asked if he/she received education on Emergency Preparedness procedures. He/she stated, "no."

 

b. Patient #1 was asked if he/she had discussions with agency staff on what to do in the event of an emergency. He/she stated, "no."

c. Review of the patient's admission folder lacked evidence of an individualized emergency preparedness plan for the patient in the home.

d. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care for certification period 5/3/19 to 7/1/19 states, "Clinician to provide education related to emergency preparedness and steps to take if an emergency event occurs."

2. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 5/20/19 at 1:20 PM, the following was indicated:

a. Upon interview at 1:40 PM, Patient #2 was asked if he/she received education on Emergency Preparedness procedures. He/she stated, "No one spoke with me about emergency preparedness and I have a concern about that. They took away my life alert. I don't have a cell phone so if the phone lines go down, I don't know what to do."

b. Review of the patient's admission folder lacked evidence of an individualized emergency preparedness plan for the patient in the home. 

c. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care for certification period 5/1/19 to 6/29/19 states, "Clinician to provide education related to emergency preparedness and steps to take if an emergency event occurs."

3. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 5/20/19, review of the patient's admission folder lacked evidence of an individualized emergency preparedness plan for the patient.

4. Review of Medical Record #3 on 5/21/19 revealed the following:

a. The RN Oasis Admission dated 5/7/19 states, "Emergency Preparedness: The Evacuation Location - OCC."

b. Upon interview on 5/21/19 at 1:00 PM, Staff #1 was unable to identify what the initials "OCC" represented for the Evacuation Location plan. 

5. During a home visit for Patient #5 on 5/21/19 at 9:45 AM, the patient was unable to recall if he/she reviewed Emergency Preparedness with the nurse. Patient #5 stated, "I know how to evacuate the building - we are near the back door."

a. There was no evidence that Patient #5 had an individualized Emergency Preparedness plan in the home.

6. Review of Medical Record #5 on 5/21/19 revealed the following: 

a. The RN Oasis Admission dated 5/11/19 states, "Emergency Preparedness -The Evacuation Location - Home."

b. Upon interview on 5/21/19 at 1:30 PM, Staff #1 confirmed that "Home" was not an evacuation location. 

7. During a home visit for Patient #6 on 5/21/19, review of the patient's admission folder lacked evidence of an individualized emergency preparedness plan for the patient.

8. Review of Medical Record #6 on 5/21/19 revealed the following:

a. The RN Oasis Admission dated 3/24/19 states, "Emergency Preparedness -The Evacuation Location - Front/Back Door."

b. Upon interview on 5/21/19 at 1:30 PM, Staff #1 confirmed that "Front/Back Door" was not an evacuation location. 

9. Review of Medical Record #10 on 5/22/19 revealed the following:

a. On the RN Oasis Admission dated 3/17/19, the evaluation location under the section marked "Emergency Preparedness", was left blank. 

10. Review of Medical Record #16 on 5/22/19 revealed the following:

a. On the RN Oasis Admission dated 4/4/19, the evacuation location under the section marked "Emergency Preparedness", was left blank.

11. Review of Medical Record #17 on 5/22/19 revealed the following: 

a. On the RN Oasis Admission dated 4/30/19, the evacuation location under the section marked "Emergency Preparedness", was left blank. 

12. Staff #1, Staff #5, and Staff #11 confirmed the above findings.

Standard: Conformance with physician orders.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of two (2) of six (6) medical records, review of facility documents, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that services ordered by the physician are provided as indicated in the plan of care.

b. There was no evidence of a missed visit note indicating that the physician was notified about the missed visit.

2. Review of Medical Record #17 on 5/22/19 revealed the following:

a. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care for certification period 4/30/19 to 6/28/19 states, "Frequency/Duration of Visits: MSW (medical social worker), 1wk1 (once for one week)."

i. For week 1, 4/28/19 to 5/4/19, there was no MSW visit conducted. The plan of care indicated that one (1) MSW visit should be made that week.

b. There was no evidence of a missed visit note indicating that the physician was notified about the missed visit.

3. Staff #1 confirmed the above findings.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility documents, and staff interviews, it was determined that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to ensure that infection prevention and control policies are implemented. 

Reference: Facility policy, Bag Technique - Professional Field Staff states, "... 3. Use of Bag Inside the House... h. Provide patient care then disinfect equipment prior to returning to bag. ... 1. Stethoscope - at each visit routinely clean the bell and the diaphragm with an alcohol pad, using rotary motion. Must dry prior to placing in bag. ... 4. BP (blood pressure) - must be used on intact skin. Clean with alcohol before returning to bag. Place in case or in a plastic bag when returning to bag. ... 4. Point of care device... b) Lightly mist Zoono on both sides of tablet per manufacturer c) Tablet/PDA/stylus- may cover with plastic bag and wipe plastic with alcohol d) Patients may perform hand hygiene prior to signing on the tablet. ... ."

1. During a home visit of Patient #1 on 5/20/19 at 11:50 AM, the following was observed:

a. Staff #3 performed hand hygiene and removed a stethoscope, blood pressure cuff, and thermometer from his/her bag.

i. Staff #3 used the equipment to check the vital signs of Patient #1. When finished, he/she cleaned the thermometer with an alcohol wipe, and placed it back in his/her bag.

ii. Staff #3 placed the stethoscope and blood pressure cuff in his/her bag without first cleaning the equipment with alcohol.

b. Staff #3 used his/her tablet for documentation and to obtain the patient's signature. He/she did not spray the tablet with Zoono prior to placing it back in the bag.

2. During a home visit of Patient #3 on 5/20/19 at 10:54 AM, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #6 placed his/her bag on a chair with an upholstered cushion. There was no barrier placed underneath the bag. 

b. Patient #3 signed Staff #6's tablet with a stylus pen. The tablet and/or stylus pen was not covered with a plastic bag and the patient did not perform hand hygiene prior to signing the tablet. 

3. During a home visit of Patient #5 on 5/21/19 at 9:00 AM, the following was observed: 

a. Staff #16 placed his/her bag on a chair with an upholstered cushion. There was no barrier placed underneath the bag. 

b. Patient #5 signed Staff #16's tablet with his/her finger. The tablet was not covered with a plastic bag and the patient did not perform hand hygiene prior to signing the tablet. 

c. The patient was observed coughing into his/her hand, with and without a tissue, throughout the visit. 

d. After patient care, and prior to leaving the home visit, Staff #16 wiped the tablet screen with an alcohol wipe. 

e. Upon interview on 5/21/19 at 12:00 PM, Staff #10 confirmed that tablets are not to be wiped with alcohol. He/she stated that the product used to clean tablets is "Zoono". 

i. A request was made on 5/21/19 at 1:15 PM for the manufacturer's instructions for use (IFU) for Zoono. No IFU was provided.

4. Staff #1, Staff #5 and Staff #10 confirmed the above findings.
