source_record.Deficiency Description: Initial Comments - Not A Deficiency Citation
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This report is the result of unannounced standard-level Federal Recertification and State Re-licensure surveys, completed June 25, 2025, at Virtua Home Care at West Jersey. It was determined the facility is not in substantial compliance with Federal requirements of 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies and State requirements of N.J.A.C. Title 8 Chapter 42 Home Health Agency Licensing Standards.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observations in three out of three home visits (Patient (P)1, P2, and P5), staff interviews, and a review of facility policies, it was determined the facility failed to ensure: 1) staff follow infection control procedures when entering the clinical bag and the cleaning and disinfection equipment, to prevent the risk of cross-contamination; 2) maintain sterility during a PleurX drainage procedure. 

Findings include:

1) Facility policy titled, "Bag Technique and Contents," dated 5/2024, stated, "… II. Purpose: A. The purpose of this policy is to prevent the infection/ and avoid cross contamination of the clinical bag and its equipment … X. Procedure … **Remember** if you need to re-enter the clinical bag during the visit, hand hygiene MUST be performed after unzipping before re-entering the clinical bag … XI. Set Up of Fields: … 10. Used equipment will be cleaned and disinfected … 11. Clean equipment is placed on the clean field to air dry … 12. … perform hand hygiene and return the cleaned equipment to the clinical bag …" 

On 06/23/25 at 12:14 PM, in the presence of Staff (S)5 (Rehab Supervisor), S4, a Speech Language Pathologist (SLP) was observed providing care for P1.

At 12:15 PM, S6 accessed his/her bag without washing and/or sanitizing his/her hands and proceeded to set up the clean and dirty barriers for patient care. 

On 06/23/25 at 2:09 PM, in the presence of S7 (Team Manager Home Health), S6, a Registered Nurse (RN) was observed providing care for P2.

At 2:12 PM, while completing a medication reconciliation, S6 touched medication bottles and then proceeded to access his/her bag without washing and/or sanitizing his/her hands. 

At 2:20 PM, S6 completed vital signs on P2. During this process, P2 had a pulse oximeter on his/her left index finger and placed his/her left hand on the clean barrier field. At 2:25 PM, S6 cleaned the pulse oximeter, stethoscope, thermometer, and sphygmomanometer (blood pressure cuff) and placed them on the potentially contaminated clean barrier field. S6 then replaced the items into his/her bag without recleaning them.  

 On 06/24/25 at 8:46 PM, in the presence of S7, S8, a RN was observed providing care for P5.

At 9:04 AM, S8 accessed his/her bag without washing and/or sanitizing his/her hands and proceeded to put away the pulse oximeter, stethoscope, thermometer, and sphygmomanometer.

On 06/23/25 at 2:54 PM, S6 confirmed the above findings and stated that hand hygiene should be performed prior to entering his/her bag. 

2) Facility policy titled, "Pleural [thin linings that surround the lungs] and Peritoneal [refers to tissue that lines the abdominal cavity] Drainage System Care & Management," last revised on 3/2025, stated, "… II. Purpose: A. To provide the means for drainage of accumulating pleural fluid [liquid in the small space surrounding the lungs] … III. Policy: A. To minimize risk of infection … XI. Procedure: A. Adhere to Standard precautions and hand hygiene protocol … G. Open kit and establish sterile field … Section III, B. Intermittent Vacuum Drainage: PleurX [small flexible tube inserted into the chest or abdomen to drain excess fluid]: Prepare to Drain: 1. Set up a clean, clear workspace on a table or counter … 7. Open the Procedure Pack pouch … 8. Set bundle with sterile wrapping on the workspace … Carefully unfold the sterile wrapping … The items and the inside of the wrapping are sterile. Do not touch them with ungloved hands or other non-sterile items. 9. Remove the bottle with the drainage line from the bag. The items in the drainage kit bag are sterile … 11. … Be careful not to let the outside of the gloves touch anything non-sterile … Put on gloves …"

At 2:33 PM, S6 was observed performing the pleural fluid drainage procedure for P2. S6 washed his/her hands, opened the PleurX drainage bottle package, and placed the bottle on the table using his/her bare hands. S6 pushed his/her computer aside with his/her bare hand and then with the same hand repositioned the PleurX drainage bottle on the table. S6 did not perform hand hygiene after touching his/her computer and PleurX drainage bottle. S6 opened the PleurX Procedure Kit and without performing hand hygiene, put on the sterile gloves. While wearing the sterile gloves, S6 touched the potentially contaminated, non sterile PleurX drainage bottle, and repositioned it on the table. While wearing the same gloves, S6 removed the cap on the PleurX drainage bottle and connected the tubing to P2’s left indwelling catheter (thin flexible drainage tube). After the drainage procedure was completed, S6 disconnected the tubing and applied a sterile dressing to the P2’s left indwelling catheter.  

On 06/23/25 at 2:54 PM, an interview was conducted with S6. When the findings were reviewed with S6, S6 nodded in agreement and stated that the PleurX drainage procedure is a sterile procedure.

On 06/25/25 at 10:41 AM, an interview was conducted with S21, the Infection Prevention Manager, S21 stated that the PleurX drainage procedure is a sterile procedure performed in a clean environment. 

NJAC 8:42-12.2(b)

Written notice for non-covered care
CFR(s): 484.50(c)(8)
Receive proper written notice, in advance of a specific service being furnished, if the HHA believes that the service may be non-covered care; or in advance of the HHA reducing or terminating on-going care. The HHA must also comply with the requirements of 42 CFR 405.1200 through 405.1204.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interviews and facility policy review, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that all patients receive a “Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage” at discharge in one of five discharged patient medical records reviewed (Patient (P) 17).

Findings include:

Facility policy titled, “Home Care Notification of Medicare Non-Coverage (NOMNC)” states, “…Procedure: A. Home Care uses the approved Notice of Non-Coverage form (CMS-10123) to notify Medicare beneficiaries that Medicare services are ending…C. The RN [nurse] or Social Worker or designee delivers and explains the NOMNC to patient/representative at least two days before the last day of covered care…”

On 6/24/25, a review of P17’s medical record took place in the presence of Staff (S)9 (Quality Nurse).

On 5/22/25, P17 was discharged from home care services because he/she met established goals. P17’s medical record lacked evidence of a signed “Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage” form.

On 6/24/25 at 2:52 PM, S9 confirmed P17 had Medicare, and his/her medical record did not contain a “Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage.”

Communication with all physicians
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(1)
Standard: Coordination of Care. The HHA must: 
(1) Assure communication with all physicians or allowed practitioners involved in the plan of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interview, and review of facility policies, it was determined the facility failed to ensure communication with the physician was documented when a missed visit occurred, in two of the five medical records reviewed (Patient (P)10 and P11).

Findings include:

Facility policy titled, "Cancellation of Visits/Not Home Not Found," last revised on 11/2023, stated, "… II. Purpose: A. To assure patient … receives visits as outlined in the Plan of Care … IX. Definitions: … Not Home Not Found (NHNF) … C. If the clinician is called by the patient or office and notified prior to the visit that the patient is not available … 3) A new visit date and time should be scheduled for the patient. 4) If the visit is not rescheduled within the same Medicare week, the physician must be notified. The clinician will document notification of the physician in the EMR [Electronic Medical Record] under "clinical notes" … E. If the visit is a NHNF the clinician would: … 3) Write a clinical note stating: a. why the visit was missed/changed … d. The rescheduled date and time agreed upon by the patient/CG [Care Giver] … 4) If the visit is not scheduled within the same Medicare week, the physician must be notified. The clinician will document notification of the physician in the EMR under "clinical notes" … F. Any visit that is determined to be NHNF will be considered a missed visit …"  

On 06/24/25 at 1:10 PM, a review of P10's medical record was conducted with Staff (S)10 (Quality Registered Nurse) and revealed the following:

A review of P10’s Plan of Care Orders for the certification period beginning 5/8/25 showed visit orders for the Physical Therapist (PT) as "… 2 visits every week for 4 weeks …" from 5/18/25 to 6/14/25.

During the week of 5/18/25 to 5/24/25, the medical record lacked evidence that P10 received PT twice during this week. 

The medical record lacked evidence that the provider was notified that the patient did not receive any PT visits during the week of 5/18/25 to 5/24/25. The findings were confirmed by S3 (Director of Quality Management and Infection Control) and S10.

On 06/24/25 at 1:35 PM, a review of P11's medical record was conducted with S10 and revealed the following:

A review of P11’s "Plan of Care Orders" for the certification period beginning 5/24/25 showed orders for the Home Health Aide (HHA) as "… 2 visits every week for 4 weeks …" from 6/8/25 to 7/5/25 and orders for a Registered Nurse (RN) as "… 1 visit every week for 10 weeks …" from 5/24/25 to 7/22/25.

During the week of 6/8/25 to 6/14/25, P11 received only one visit by the HHA on 6/12/25.

On 06/10/2025 at 10:56 AM, a documented telephone conversation between S20 (Medical Assistant) and the family member of P11 stated, "spoke with patient’s [child] who agreed to HHA visits 2x/wk [week] on Tues/Thurs. … starting on 6/12/25 …" The medical record lacked evidence of notification to the provider regarding the missed visits. The findings were confirmed by S3 and S10.

During the week of 6/15/25 to 6/21/25, the medical record lacked evidence that P11 received an RN visit during this week. 

On 6/12/2025, an RN note documented that P11 requested for the next visit on 6/18/25 to be cancelled due to a doctor’s appointment. The medical record lacked evidence of notification to the provider for the missed visit. The findings were confirmed by S3 and S10.

On 06/24/25 at 1:40 PM, when questioned about missed visits, S10 stated, "The doctor should be made aware of missed visits."

 

NJAC 8:42-6.1(a)6

source_record.Deficiency Description: Aides Are Members Of Interdisciplinary Team
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Aides are members of interdisciplinary team
CFR(s): 484.80(g)(4)
Home health aides must be members of the interdisciplinary team, must report changes in the patient's condition to a registered nurse or other appropriate skilled professional, and must complete appropriate records in compliance with the HHA's policies and procedures.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interview, medical record review, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to complete accurate and appropriate records in accordance with the facility’s Home Health Aide (HHA) education and job description.

Facility document titled, “Overview” date of last change 02/20/2025 states, “… Job profile Name: Home Health Aide… Position Responsibilities: Knowledgeable of and supports the plan of care under the direction of the RN… Submits all documentation (care plan, time sheets, API, etc) accurately and timely…”

Facility policy titled, “Home Health Aide Education” last revised 06/2024 states, “Procedure: A. The Home Health Aide (HHA) will be asked to demonstrate a series of personal care skills to establish competency in these areas… 2) Observation, reporting, and documentation of patient status, care, and services furnished.”

On 06/23/2025 at 2:02 PM, a home care visit was conducted with Patient (P)3, in the presence of Staff (S)12 (Clinical Manager) and S13 (Home Health Aide [HHA]). S13 was observed assisting P3 with foot care with the use of a collapsible foot bath basin. S13 was observed washing P3’s feet, dried them with a small towel, and applied lotion. At 2:15 PM, S13 bathed P3’s back, dried with small towel, and applied lotion to P3’s back. At 2:18 PM, S13 assisted P3 with the application of compressions socks per P3’s request. P3 ambulated himself/herself back into bed. No further care observed or offered.

On 06/24/2025 at 12:59 PM, medical record review for P3 revealed “Aide Home Visit… Care Plan Visit Documentation… [check mark] Intervention: Aide encourage patient fluid intake...  [check mark] Intervention: Aide incontinence care and change adult diaper…  [check mark] Intervention: Aide assist with oral care…” Surveyor did not observe the care documented as completed to have been provided to P3 during this home visit.

Further medical record review for P3 revealed “Aide Home Visit… Care Plan Visit Documentation… Intervention: Aide meal preparation [Exclamation] Variance: Patient refused… Intervention: Aide catheter care [Exclamation] Variance: Patient refused Visit Notes: Patient refused… Intervention: Aide assist with shaving [Exclamation] Variance: Patient refused Visit Notes: Patient refused… Intervention: Aide perform hair care [Exclamation] Variance: Patient refused Description: Aide to assist patient in hair grooming including to Shampoo Hair and Brush Hair. Visit Notes: Patient refused…” Surveyor did not observe the P3 to have been asked for the care documented as refused to have been offered to P3 during this home visit.

On 06/24/2025 at 1:50 PM, an interview was conducted with S3 (Director of Quality Management and Infection Control) and S10 (Quality Registered Nurse). Upon interview, S10 confirmed that the HHA should provide each task on the patients’ care plan. S10 confirmed that a “check mark” on a patients’ care plan indicates completed care that was provided during their home visit. The above findings were reviewed with S3 and S10.  

N.J.A.C. 8:42-7.5(3)

source_record.Deficiency Description: Initial Comments - Not A Deficiency Citation
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): A Federal Recertification survey was conducted on December 16, 17, and 18, 2019, that resulted in Standard Level deficiencies.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interviews, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined that the Home Health Agency (HHA) failed to ensure that their infection prevention and control policies are implemented. 

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy "Hand Hygiene" states, "... Hand hygiene must be performed: ... Before and after coming in contact with a source that is likely to be contaminated ... before donning [put on] and upon removing gloves ..."

1. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 12/17/19, the following was observed:

a. Staff #7 assisted Patient #3 with colostomy care in the patient's bathroom.

(i) Patient #3 did not wash his/her hands prior to changing his/her colostomy appliance. Staff #7 did not instruct Patient #3 to perform hand hygiene prior to performing colostomy care.

(ii) Staff #7 donned gloves without performing hand hygiene. 

(iii) Staff #7 picked up sealed supplies that had fallen on the bathroom floor, with his/her gloved hands. Staff #7 did not perform hand hygiene or change gloves after touching the floor. 

(iv) When the colostomy care was completed, Staff #7 instructed Patient #3 to wash his/her hands. Staff #7 then told the patient that he/she should wash his/her hands before and after performing colostomy care.

 

2. The above finding was confirmed by Staff #2 and Staff #7.

Patients receive education and training
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(5)
Ensure that each patient, and his or her caregiver(s) where applicable, receive ongoing education and training provided by the HHA, as appropriate, regarding the care and services identified in the plan of care.  The HHA must provide training, as necessary, to ensure a timely discharge.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, medical record review, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure that the patient is provided education on pain management from physical and occupational therapists in two (2) of three (3) medical records reviewed. 

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy "Pain Assessment and Management of the Adult" states, "...Patient Education ... All health care providers are responsible to educate and document pain management. ..."

1. Upon review of Medical Record #6 on 12/18/19, the following was noted:

a. On 11/18/19, an Occupational Therapist performed an OT (Occupational Therapy) Initial Evaluation.

(i) A pain assessment was completed. The patient reported that he/she had pain.

(ii) There was no documented evidence that the patient received education on pain management. 

b. On 11/21/19, an Occupational Therapist performed an OT home visit.

(i) A pain assessment was completed. The patient reported that he/she had pain.

(ii) There was no documented evidence that the patient received education on pain management. 

2. Upon review of Medical Record #7, the following was noted:

a. On 10/31/19, a Physical Therapist performed a PT (Physical Therapy) Initial Evaluation.

(i) A pain assessment was completed. The patient reported that he/she had pain.

(ii) There was no documented evidence that the patient received education on pain management. 

3. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #2 and Staff #6.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Initial Comments - Not A Deficiency Citation
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This report is the result of an unannounced Federal Complaint survey, C#2992037, completed on May, 20, 2026 at Patient Care. It was determined the facility is not in substantial compliance with the requirements of 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies.

Plan of care
CFR(s): 484.60(a)(1)
Each patient must receive the home health services that are written in an individualized plan of care that identifies patient-specific measurable outcomes and goals, and which is established, periodically reviewed, and signed by a doctor of medicine, osteopathy, or podiatry acting within the scope of his or her state license, certification, or registration. If a physician or allowed practitioner refers a patient under a plan of care that cannot be completed until after an evaluation visit, the physician or allowed practitioner is consulted to approve additions or modifications to the original plan.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on a review of facility policy, medical record review and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to provide services to Patient (P)1 in accordance with his/her plan of care. 

Findings include:

 

Facility policy titled "Plan of Care (POC)," last revised 3/1/26, stated, "Purpose: To assure an appropriate plan of care is developed and revised in a timely  manner for each patient. To ensure that physician/authorized practitioner's orders are followed....Procedure...2. This POC includes:...b. Types, frequency, and duration of services required which may include virtual services...8. Medications, treatments, and interventions are provided by qualified agency staff as ordered by the physician or authorized provider..."

 

On 05/20/26, at 9:26 AM, an entrance conference was conducted with Staff (S)1. 

 

At 12:59 PM, Medical Record (MR) review was conducted for Patient (P)1 and the following was revealed:

 

On 12/31/2025, P1 was accepted to service by the facility with a diagnosis of Pneumonia. 

 

P1 was to receive Occupational Therapy (OT) services "Effective 01/04/2026 1WK6 [once a week for six weeks]."

 

On 01/07/26, the first OT assessment was conducted on P1. 

 

P1 was due for an OT visit between 01/18/26-01/24/26.

 

P1's schedule indicated he/she was to receive OT service on 01/21/26.

 

The facility was unable to provide documentation that P1 received OT service on 01/21/26 or on any other date between 01/18/26 through 01/24/26.

 

On 05/20/26 at 1:29 PM, S1 confirmed P1 did not receive OT services from 1/18/26 through 1/24/26.

source_record.Deficiency Description: 5 Calendar Days After Start Of Care
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
5 calendar days after start of care
CFR(s): 484.55(b)(1)
The comprehensive assessment must be completed in a timely manner, consistent with the patient's immediate needs, but no later than 5 calendar days after the start of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on a review of facility policy, medical record review and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure Patient (P)1 received a comprehensive Occupational Therapy (OT) assessment within five days after the start of care.  

Findings include:

 

Facility policy titled "Patient Assessment, Initial and Reassessment," revised 12/01/25, stated, "POLICY:...The comprehensive assessment is the responsibility of one clinician. However, the assessing clinician may obtain input from the patient, caregiver, or other healthcare personnel (i.e., physician, pharmacist, agency staff) if within the comprehensive 5-day window timeframe. For assessment items, the collaborating healthcare providers must have had direct in-person contact with the patient...PROCEDURE:...3...d. Physical Therapist, Speech Therapist, Occupational Therapist, medical Social Worker, and Dietitian may make initial evaluation of the patient status to determine the need for specific therapist. This initial discipline specific evaluation(s) will occur within 5 days from the Start of Care (SOC) date or order date or sooner if medically necessary..."

 

On 5/20/26, at 9:26 AM, an entrance conference was conducted with Staff (S)1. 

 

At 12:59 PM, Medical Record (MR) review was conducted for Patient (P)1 and P2 and the following was revealed:

 

On 12/31/2025, P1 was accepted for service by the facility with a diagnosis of Pneumonia. 

 

On 01/01/26, an initial assessment was conducted on P1 by his/her Registered Nurse (RN)

 

On 01/07/26, an Occupational Therapy (OT) assessment was conducted on P1, six days after P1's initial assessment.     

 

On 12/26/25, P2 was accepted for service by the facility for "aftercare following a joint replacement surgery". 

 

On 12/27/25, an initial assessment was conducted on P2 by his/her RN.

 

On 01/02/26, an OT assessment was conducted on P2, six days after P2's initial assessment.

 

On 05/20/26, at 1:56 PM, S1 confirmed the above finding and stated that additional disciplines, such as physical therapy and occupational therapy, have five days to evaluate a patient after the initial assessment is completed.

Communication with all physicians
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(1)
Standard: Coordination of Care. The HHA must: 
(1) Assure communication with all physicians or allowed practitioners involved in the plan of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on a review of facility policy, medical record review and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure changes in Patient (P)1's plan of care are communicated with his/her provider.  

Findings include:

 

Facility policy titled "Coordination of Care, From Admit Through Discharge," revised 12/1/25, stated, "...PROCEDURE:...4. Coordination of care with physician/authorized practitioner: At admission, throughout care, and at discharge, coordination of services is promoted through routine communication with the patient's physician:...c. When a missed visit occurs altering the Plan of Care...5. Coordination of care among disciplines and between in-person and virtual clinicians: Patient care is coordinated among various disciplines and services through care planning processes to ensure continuity of care form admission to discharge. This includes:... c...i...Missed visits and changes to scheduled visits. a. Reason for missed visit b. Changes to patient schedule...

On 05/20/26, at 9:26 AM, an entrance conference was conducted with Staff (S)1. 

 

At 12:59 PM, Medical Record (MR) review was conducted for Patient (P)1 and the following was revealed:

 

On 12/31/2025, P1 was accepted to service by the facility with a diagnosis of Pneumonia. 

 

P1 was to receive Occupational Therapy (OT) services "Effective 01/04/2026 1WK6 [once a week for six weeks]."

 

On 01/07/26, the first OT assessment was conducted on P1. 

 

P1 was due for an OT visit between 01/18/26-01/24/26.

 

P1's schedule indicated he/she was to receive OT service on 01/21/26.

 

The facility was unable to provide documentation that P1 received OT services on 01/21/26, or any other day between 01/18/26 through 01/24/26. 

 

The facility was unable to provide documentation that P1's provider was notified of the missed visit. 

 

On 05/20/26, documentation between S1 and P1's Occupational Therapist, via email, was reviewed and indicated P1's OT therapist requested a personal leave of absence from 01/21/26-03/08/26. 

 

On 05/20/26 1:29 PM, S1 confirmed P1 did not receive OT services the week of 01/18/26 through 01/24/26, and that there was no documentation of notification to P1's provider of the missed visit.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Initial Comments - Not A Deficiency Citation
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This report is the result of an unannounced standard-level Federal Recertification and State Re-licensure Survey completed August 1, 2024 at Patient Care. It was determined the facility is in substantial compliance with Federal requirements of 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies and State requirements of N.J.A.C. Title 8 Chapter 42 Home Health Agency Licensing Standards.

HHA Comprehensive Assessment in Disaster
CFR(s): 484.102(b)(1)
§484.102(b)(1) Condition for Participation:

[(b) Policies and procedures.  The HHA must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 

At a minimum, the policies and procedures must address the following:]



(1) The plans for the HHA's patients during a natural or man-made disaster. Individual plans for each patient must be included as part of the comprehensive patient assessment, which must be conducted according to the provisions at §484.55.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observations, staff interview, and review of facility policies and documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure an individualized emergency preparedness plan was available in one of five patient homes visited (Patient (P) 5).

Findings include:

On 7/31/24 at 11:08 AM, S13, a Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) was observed providing care for P5. 

A review of P5’s Plan of Care revealed the following: 1) Start of Care date: 11/13/23. 2) Functional limitations: “ambulation”. 3) Safety measures: “1 person transfer” and “ambulation precautions”. 

At 12:20 PM, the admission packet was asked of P5 and P5's caregiver for review by this surveyor. P5 and P5’s caregiver, were unable to locate the admission packet. P5’s caregiver stated, “it must be in my house." S13 stated that P5 was living in the caregiver’s house prior to moving to his/her current residence. P5 and P5’s caregiver stated that P5 moved to the current residence “a couple months ago.” When questioned about an emergency disaster plan, P5 stated, “I would call 911. I would get out the window.” P5 and P5’s caregiver were unable to state a clear evacuation plan for P5 in the event of an emergency or disaster.

On 7/31/24 at 1:45 PM, a review of P5’s medical revealed there was no emergency disaster plan in P5’s medical record.

On 7/31/24 at 3:05 PM, S1, Executive Director, confirmed the facility did not have an emergency disaster plan in the medical record for P5.

Facility policy titled “Patient Assessment, Initial, and Reassessment” last revised 1/1/24 states “Purpose: to describe the process of patient assessments … Procedure: 1. Upon admission and reassessments, the qualified clinician performs the following assessment activities and collects the following data: … p. Emergency disaster plan.”

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, patient and staff interview, and a review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure staff followed the policy to prevent transmission of infections and communicable diseases in two of four patients (Patient (P) 5 and P15).

On 7/30/24 at 12:26 PM, Staff (S) 10, a Physical Therapist (PT), was observed providing care for P15.

At 12:28 PM, S10 donned gloves and placed a barrier pad on a table in the patient's living room. S10 placed his/her equipment bag in the center of the pad. S10 then placed a second barrier on P15’s dining room table and removed vital signs equipment (thermometer, sphygmomanometer and blood pressure cuff, pulse oximeter, stethoscope, and tablet) from the equipment bag and placed them on the barrier pad on the dining room table. S10 then began taking P15’s vital signs. S10 completed vital signs and entered vital signs onto tablet without doffing gloves.

At 12:58 PM, after the completion of the PT exercises, S10 began cleaning the vital signs equipment. After cleaning the vital signs equipment, S10 placed the cleaned equipment on the barrier pad that also shared space with the equipment bag. The equipment bag was occupying most of the space on the barrier pad and there was only a narrow space around the bag for the clean equipment to be placed. The cleaned stethoscope and sphygmomanometer were observed touching the outside of the equipment bag and touching the living room table thus creating an opportunity for cross-contamination from the outside of the bag and the patient’s table to the newly cleaned equipment. S10, without re-cleaning the equipment, placed the equipment back into the clean interior of the equipment bag. 

At 1:00 PM, S10 asked P15 for a signature on the tablet. P15 used his/her finger to sign the tablet. S10 failed to clean the tablet before placing it back in the equipment bag.

On 7/31/24 at 11:08 AM, S13, a Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN), was observed providing care for P5 in the patient’s bedroom.

At 11:10 AM, S13 performed hand hygiene, donned gloves, and began placing barrier pads on P5’s bed. S13’s badge fell off his/her uniform and landed on the floor of the bedroom. P5’s mother picked up the badge and handed it to S13. S13 placed it back on his/her uniform without cleaning it. At 12:02 PM, after finishing P2’s wound care, S13 was observed leaning over the bed and the dirty badge on S13’s uniform touched the clean wound care supplies that were on a clean barrier pad that had been placed on the bed thus providing a potential for cross-contamination. S13 did not replace the wound care supplies that were touched by the badge and continued with providing care to the patient.

At 12:09 PM, S13 began cleaning the vital signs equipment (pulse oximeter, stethoscope, thermometer, sphygmomanometer and blood pressure cuff) and placed them on a clean barrier pad. The cleaned stethoscope and thermometer were observed hanging off the edge of the designated clean barrier pad and touching P5’s bed before being placed back in the equipment bag. S13 placed used, dirty supplies in P5’s trash can near bed and returned to cleaning the remaining pieces of vital signs equipment (pulse oximeter, blood pressure cuff and sphygmomanometer) without changing gloves and performing hand hygiene.

On 8/1/24 at 1:13 PM, the above findings were shared with S1, Executive Director during exit conference. S1 confirmed that there was an opportunity for cross-contamination if the above techniques were used.

Facility policy titled “Standard Precautions” last reviewed 12/01/21 states “Purpose:  to prevent the spread of disease and infection between and among patients and staff … Procedure: … 4. Standard Precautions include:  a. Hand Hygiene … ii. Perform hand hygiene immediately after gloves are removed, between patient contacts, and when otherwise indicated to avoid transfer of microorganisms to other patients or environments…”

Facility policy titled “Standard Precautions” last revised 12/01/21 states “Purpose:  to prevent the spread of disease and infection between and among patients and staff … Procedure: … 4. Standard Precautions include:  d. Patient-Care Equipment: … ii. Ensure that reusable equipment is not used for the care of another patient until it has been cleaned appropriately.”

Facility policy titled “Cleaning of Re-Useable Equipment” last revised on 6/01/22 states “Purpose:  to assure equipment required for patient care is clean and sanitized to prevent the spread of infections … Procedure: … 6. … a. The hand-held computer device (i.e. tablet or Smartphone) should be wiped down with a low-level disinfectant at the beginning and end of each visit…”

COMPLIANCE W/ ACCEPTED PROFESSIONAL STD
CFR(s): 484.12(c)
The HHA and its staff must comply with accepted professional standards and principles that apply to professionals furnishing services in an HHA.     




This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility documents, and staff interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that staff comply with accepted professional standards that apply to professionals furnishing services in a home health agency. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, Bag Technique, states, "... Procedure 1. Observe principles of standard precautions at all times. The inside of the bag shall be regarded and maintained as a clean area. ... 4. The bag should be placed on a hard flat clean surface with appropriate barrier. If there are dogs in the home do not place the bag on the floor but on a high surface or hang on the back of a chair or door knob where the dog will not have access. ... 5. Prepare a work area by spreading a barrier if indicated on the work surface. Place a receptacle to collect soiled equipment for disposal at the end of the visit. ... 7. Remove the items needed for the visit and place on the prepared work area. ... 8. ... All reusable equipment (e.g. stethoscope, thermometer, blood pressure cuff) should be wiped down with alcohol unless otherwise indicated before being returned to the nursing bag. ..." 

Reference #2: Facility protocol, Wound Care: Dressing Application, states, " ... 5. Remove tape by pushing skin from tape. Remove soiled dressing. 6. Discard dressing and gloves in appropriate containers. 7. Perform hand hygiene and don clean gloves. ..." 

1. During a home visit for Patient #3 on 1/11/18, the following was observed:

a. Staff #10 placed a barrier on the couch which is not a hard surface.

b. Staff #10 removed items from the nursing bag and did not place the items on a prepared work area. 

c. Staff #10 removed a dressing, assessed the wound, and applied a new dressing.

i. Staff #10 did not discard his/her gloves after removing the dressing.

ii. Staff #10 did not perform hand hygiene and don clean gloves before applying the new dressing.

d. The patient's dog touched an item on the barrier.

i. Staff #10 had his/her back toward the barrier and was unaware that this occured. 

2. During a home visit for Patient #5 on 1/11/18, the following was observed:

a. Staff #12 removed a bag containing a blood pressure cuff, from the nursing bag, and did not place the item on the prepared work area. 

b. Staff #12 removed a bag containing a thermometer and sheaths, from the nursing bag, and did not place the items on a prepared work area. 

c. Staff #12 removed a bag containing blue gloves, from the nursing bag, and did not place the items on the prepared work area. 

d. The bags were not cleaned before being returned to the nursing bag. 

3. During a home visit for Patient #4 on 1/11/18, the following was observed:

a. Staff #11 placed a barrier on the couch which is not a hard surface.

b. Staff #11 left the room to get wound care supplies.

i. The patient's dog touched an item on the barrier.

ii. Staff #11 was unaware that this occured. 

4. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2.

ii. The patient did not receive an OT visit the week of 12/17/17, 12/31/17, and 1/07/18.

iii. OT services were not provided in accordance with the plan of care.

484.75 Skilled Professional Services

Standard level deficiencies were also cited.

Skilled professional services
CFR(s): 484.75
Condition of participation: Skilled professional services.

Skilled professional services include skilled nursing services, physical therapy, speech-language pathology services, and occupational therapy, as specified in §409.44 of this chapter, and physician or allowed practitioner and medical social work services as specified in §409.45 of this chapter. Skilled professionals who provide services to HHA patients directly or under arrangement must participate in the coordination of care.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:

Findings include: 

1. The HHA failed to ensure that skilled professional services of a medical social worker are available to all patients. (G702)

2. The HHA failed to ensure that all needed skilled professional staff is involved in the patient's plan of care. (G706)

3. The HHA failed to ensure that skilled professional services of a medical social worker are delivered according to physicians orders. (G710)

HHA Comprehensive Assessment in Disaster
CFR(s): 484.102(b)(1)
§484.102(b)(1) Condition for Participation:

[(b) Policies and procedures.  The HHA must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 

At a minimum, the policies and procedures must address the following:]



(1) The plans for the HHA's patients during a natural or man-made disaster. Individual plans for each patient must be included as part of the comprehensive patient assessment, which must be conducted according to the provisions at §484.55.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview and review of three (3) of five (5) medical records (#1, #2, and #5), it was determined the facility failed to ensure all patients receive an individualized emergency plan as part of their comprehensive assessment.

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

Patients receive education and training

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1): This report is the result of an unannounced standard-level Federal Recertification and State Re-licensure surveys, completed June 6, 2025, at Hackensack Meridian at Home - Ocean County. It was determined the facility is not in substantial compliance with Federal requirements of 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies and State requirements of N.J.A.C. Title 8 Chapter 42 Home Health Agency Licensing Standards.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observations in one of seven home visits (Patient (P) P3), review of facility documents, staff interview, and review of nationally recognized guidelines, it was determined the facility failed to provide a sanitary environment by ensuring: 1) proper hand hygiene practices are implemented according to facility policy and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidelines; and 2) environmental cleaners and disinfectants are used in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions for use (IFUs).

Findings include:
1)    Reference: Guideline for Hand Hygiene in Health Care Settings: Recommendation of the Healthcare Infection Control Practices Advisory Committee [HICPAC] and the HICPAC/SHEA/APIC/IDSA Hand Hygiene Task Force, published in the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report at MMWR 2002; 51 (No. RR-16) page 32 states, “Recommendations 1. Indications for handwashing and hand antisepsis A. When hands are visibly dirty or contaminated with proteinaceous material or are visibly soiled with blood or other body fluids, wash hands with either a nonantimicrobial soap and water or an antimicrobial soap and water (IA) (66). B. If hands are not visibly soiled, use an alcohol-based hand rub for routinely decontaminating hands in all other clinical situations described in items 1C-J…Alternatively, wash hands with an antimicrobial soap and water in all clinical situations described in items 1C–J…F. Decontaminate hands after contact with a patient’s intact skin (e.g., when taking a pulse or blood pressure, and lifting a patient)… I. Decontaminate hands after contact with inanimate objects (including medical equipment) in the immediate vicinity of the patient… J. Decontaminate hands after gloves…”
Facility policy titled: “Hand Hygiene,” reviewed on 08/19/2024 states, “Introduction: Hand hygiene is a general term used by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the World Health Organization (WHO) to refer to handwashing, antiseptic handwashing, antiseptic hand rubbing, and surgical hand asepsis. It’s the single most important procedure in preventing infection. To protect a patient from health-care associated infection, hand hygiene must be performed routinely and thoroughly…YOUR FIVE MOMENTS FOR HAND HYGIENE:… (1) BEFORE TOUCHING A PATIENT (2) BEFORE CLEAN/ASEPTIC PROCEDURE (3) AFTER BODY FLUID EXPOSURE RISK (4) AFTER TOUCHING A PATIENT (5) AFTER TOUCHING PATIENT SURROUNDINGS…

On 6/4/25 at 1:02 PM, during a home care visit with Patient (P) 3, a Registered Nurse (RN) Staff (S) 10, was observed to remove and insert a foley catheter (flexible tube used to drain urine from the bladder) for P3 as per physician’s orders. 

At 1:02 PM, S10 repositioned P3’s legs and placed a pillow under P3’s calves, removed his/her gloves, failed to perform hand hygiene, then opened the sterile foley catheter kit and removed the sterile gloves.

At 1:11 PM, S10 was observed to attempt to insert P3’s foley catheter. After a failed attempt in inserting the foley catheter, S10 doffed his/her gloves, failed to perform hand hygiene, and then touched his/her face. 

At 1:19 PM, S10 was observed to perform a skin assessment on P3’s bilateral heels, doffed gloves, failed to perform hand hygiene, and then touched his/her face. 

At 1:27 PM, S10 was observed to dispose of a “dirty” disposable pad that was used for “dirty” medical equipment, failed to perform hand hygiene, and then went into P3’s bag that contained his/her medications.  

N.J.A.C. 8:42-12.3 (a)4

2)    The “Super Sani-Cloth General Germicidal Disposable Wipes” Instructions For Use (IFU) was reviewed and stated, “Super Sani-Cloth Germicidal Disposable Wipe: Effective against, Bacteria… Multi-Drug Resistant Bacteria… Viruses… Bloodborne Pathogens…  Precautionary Statements Hazards to Humans and Domestic… Avoid contact with skin. …”

On 6/4/25 at 1:19 PM, during an observation of S10 providing care to P3, S10 was observed to use a stethoscope, pulse oximeter, thermometer, and blood pressure cuff to obtain vital signs for P3. The “dirty” medical equipment was placed on a disposable barrier. S10 failed to don gloves and wiped each piece of medical equipment using a “Super Sani-Cloth Germicidal Disposable Wipe”. 

On 6/4/25 at 1:32 PM, an interview was conducted with S10. When asked whether it was necessary to wear disposable gloves when handling the disposable wipes, S10 stated, “you should.” 

On 6/5/25 at 11:12 AM, S3 (Director of Quality Improvement and Staff Development) indicated when cleaning the medical equipment, it is not required to wear gloves. S3 reviewed the IFU, and confirmed gloves should be used when handling the disposable wipes.

Communication with all physicians
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(1)
Standard: Coordination of Care. The HHA must: 
(1) Assure communication with all physicians or allowed practitioners involved in the plan of care.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interview, and review of facility policies, it was determined the facility failed to ensure communication with the physician is documented, when services are not provided according to the patients' care plan, in two of 17 medical records reviewed (Patient (P)14 and P15).

On 6/5/25, in the presence of Staff (S)19 (Staff Development) and S20 (Clinical Director), medical record review was conducted and revealed the following:

A review of P14's "Home Health Plan of Care" document, for the certification period beginning 3/20/25, showed visit orders for the Physical Therapy (PT) as “...3 visits every week for 1 week 3/23/25 to 3/29/25…2 visits every week for 2 weeks 3/30/25 to 4/12/25."

On 3/26/25, P14 had a missed PT [Physical Therapy] visit. The “PT Missed Visit Note” stated, “…Communication Details: Missed visit pending insurance authorization/approval…”. P14’s medical record lacked documentation of notification to the physician for the missed visit.

On 4/3/25, P14 had a missed PT visit. The “PT Missed Visit Note” stated, “…Communication Details: Missed PT visit due to pending insurance auth [authorization]…”. P14’s medical record lacked documentation of notification to the physician for the missed visit.

On 6/5/25 at 1:42 PM, the findings were confirmed by S19 and S20.

NJAC 8:42-6.2(a)3

Findings include:

Facility policy titled, "Monitoring Patient's Response/Reporting to Physician" last reviewed on 3/2022 states, "...Procedure:...3. The patient's physician (or other licensed practitioner) will be contacted on the same day when any of the following occur:...G. When a visit is missed for any reason.."

On 6/6/25, P15’s medical record was reviewed in the presence of Staff (S)1 (Clinical Director) and S21 (Staff Development Educator). The medical record revealed the following:

On 3/4/25 at 11:07 AM, P15 signed the “Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage” indicating Home Care services will end on 3/6/25.

On 6/5/25 at 1:51 PM, S1 explained that after the Notice of Medicare of Non-Coverage is signed, the clinician would need to obtain an order from the physician for additional visits. S1 and S21 confirmed that P15’s medical record lacked evidence of communication with the physician regarding the missed visit and there was no communication requesting additional visits after the Notice of Medicare of Non-Coverage date.

source_record.Deficiency Description: Development Of Ep Policies And Procedures
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Development of EP Policies and Procedures
CFR(s): 484.102(b)
§403.748(b), §416.54(b), §418.113(b), §441.184(b), §460.84(b), §482.15(b), §483.73(b), §483.475(b), §484.102(b), §485.68(b), §485.625(b), §485.727(b), §485.920(b), §486.360(b), §491.12(b), §494.62(b).



(b) Policies and procedures. [Facilities] must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 



*[For LTC facilities at §483.73(b):] Policies and procedures. The LTC facility must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least annually.



*Additional Requirements for PACE and ESRD Facilities:



*[For PACE at §460.84(b):] Policies and procedures.  The PACE organization must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must address management of medical and nonmedical emergencies, including, but not limited to: Fire; equipment, power, or water failure; care-related emergencies; and natural disasters likely to threaten the health or safety of the participants, staff, or the public.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. 



*[For ESRD Facilities at §494.62(b):] Policies and procedures.  The dialysis facility must develop and implement emergency preparedness policies and procedures, based on the emergency plan set forth in paragraph (a) of this section, risk assessment at paragraph (a)(1) of this section, and the communication plan at paragraph (c) of this section.  The policies and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every 2 years. These emergencies include, but are not limited to, fire, equipment or power failures, care-related emergencies, water supply interruption, and natural disasters likely to occur in the facility's geographic area.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of facility documents, patient interviews, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that its policy and procedure regarding emergency preparedness, is implemented.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility policy, "Emergency Management Plan" states, "... 9. Individualized plans for patients during a natural or man-made disaster will be included as part of the comprehensive patient assessment. The comprehensive assessment will be updated as frequently as the patient's condition warrants... 10. The organization educates patients and their families on emergency preparedness at the time of admission... ."

1. Review of Medical Record #2 on 9/30/19 revealed the following:

a. The patient was admitted to the agency on 9/21/19. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Treatment for certification period 9/21/19 to 11/19/19 states, " ... 21. Orders for Discipline and Treatments... SN (skilled nurse) Schedule begins 09/21/19... Instruct safety measures. Develop/instruct emergency plan... ."

2. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 9/30/19 at 1:10 PM, a request was made to Staff #7 for evidence of the patient's emergency preparedness plan. 

a. The emergency preparedness plan provided addressed medical emergencies only. The plan did not address the patient's course of action in the event of a natural or man-made disaster.

b. Upon interview at 1:48 PM, Patient #2, and his/her spouse, confirmed that they did not receive education by the nurse on emergency preparedness procedures.

3. Review of Medical Record #8 on 10/1/19 revealed the following:

a. The patient was admitted to the agency on 9/29/19. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Treatment for certification period 9/29/19 to 11/27/19 states, " ...21. Orders for Discipline and Treatments... SN Schedule begins 09/29/19... Assess/Instruct home safety and emergency management plan... ."

4. During a home visit for Patient #8 on 10/1/19, a request was made to Staff #14 for evidence of the patient's emergency preparedness plan.

a. The emergency plan in the patient's folder was blank. 

b. Upon interview at 1:37 PM, Patient #8 confirmed that he/she did not receive education by the nurse on emergency preparedness procedures.

5. Staff #2 and Staff #4 confirmed the above findings.

Written instructions to patient include:
CFR(s): 484.60(e)
Standard: Written information to the patient. The HHA must provide the patient and caregiver with a copy of written instructions outlining:

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on review of facility documents, staff interview, and patient interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that a written plan of care (POC) was provided to the patient upon admission. 

Findings include: 

Reference: Facility policy, "Home Health Aide Plan of Care," states, " ...A current copy of the home health aide plan of care will be maintained in the patient's home. ..."

1. During a visit to Patient #9's home on 10/1/19, the following was revealed:

a. The start of care was on 9/13/19. 

b. When asked, Patient #9 was not able to locate the POC in the home. 

c. The home health aide was observed reviewing a POC that was printed on 10/1/19. 

2. There was no evidence that the Plan of Care was present in the home prior to the visit on 10/1/19.

3. Upon review, Staff #5 confirmed that the POC for Patient #9, was not in the admission folder and there was no evidence of a POC prior to 10/1/19.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility documents, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that acceptable standards of practice regarding sterile technique, are implemented.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility document, "Infection Prevention and Control - Clean and Sterile Technique" states, "... 2. Sterile Technique... c. In the home, a sterile field should be established to prevent transmission of microorganisms from the environment or from the person to person. ... 6. Always place sterile items only on a sterile surface.. 8. Dispose of soiled supplies in appropriate containers. ... ."

1. During a home visit for Patient #2 on 9/30/19, the following was observed:

a. Staff #7 was at the patient's bedside to perform a PICC line (peripherally inserted central catheter) dressing change using sterile technique.

b. At 1:33 PM, Staff #7 began to remove the patient's dressing. He/she then paused, doffed his/her gloves, then placed the gloves onto his/her sterile field. Staff #7 then proceeded to retrieve additional supplies before donning new gloves and continuing with the dressing change.

c. Staff #7 contaminated his/her sterile field, increasing the risk of infection for the patient.

2. Staff #2 and Staff #4 confirmed the above finding.

Services provided by HH aide
CFR(s): 484.80(g)(2)
A home health aide provides services that are:

(i) Ordered by the physician;

(ii) Included in the plan of care;

(iii) Permitted to be performed under state law; and

(iv) Consistent with the home health aide training.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility documents, and staff interviews, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure that services provided by home health aides is in accordance with the patient's home health aide plan of care.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility policy, "Home Health Aide Plan of Care" states, "... 2. A homemaker-home health aide employed by a health care service shall only perform task that have either been delegated to him or her by the health care practitioner supervisor or which the health care practitioner supervisor has directed the homemaker-home health aide to perform. ... ."

Reference #2: Facility policy, "Care Planning Process" states, "... 5. The plan of care will be based upon the physician's (or other authorized licensed independent practitioner's) orders and will encompass the equipment, supplies, and services required to meet the patient's needs. ... 10. Clinicians will inform the patient's physician of any changes that suggest a need to alter the plan of care. ... ."

1. During a home visit for Patient #8 on 10/1/19, the following was observed:

a. At 1:10 PM, Staff #14 assisted the patient with ambulation to the bathroom for a shower. The patient was visibly weak, with shortness of breath (SOB) observed during activity.

b. At 1:12 PM, Staff #14 re-entered the patient's dining room and removed a wooden dining room chair to take into the bathroom. He/she stated, "I need this for the patient to sit on. It's not safe for the patient without this chair."

c. Upon interview at 1:33 PM, Staff #14 confirmed that the patient does not have a shower chair. When asked if the nurse was aware that the patient did not have a shower chair, he/she stated, "I don't know. This is my first time with this patient."

2. Review of Medical Record #8 on 10/1/19 revealed the following:

a. The patient was admitted to the agency on 9/29/19. The Home Health Certification and Plan of Treatment for certification period 9/29/19 to 11/27/19 states, "Homebound due to: post cardiac surgery with SOB (shortness of breath) that resolves with rest. Unsteady gait that requires client to have assistance for all transfers and ambulation."

b. The Home Health Careplan states, "Interventions... CT-Shower Each Visit... Start 9/29/19... CT-Shower Chair Each Visit... Start 9/29/19."

c. A Home Health Aide visit was conducted on 9/30/19. There was no evidence in the medical record that the home health aide notified the nurse that the patient did not have a shower chair, as ordered in the Home Health Aide Careplan.

d. There was no evidence in the medical record that the patient's plan of care had been changed to address the lack of a shower chair that was ordered to meet the patient's needs.

3. Staff #2 and Staff #4 confirmed the above findings.

The HHA must maintain a coordinated agency-wide program for the surveillance, identification, prevention, control, and investigation of infectious and communicable diseases that is an integral part of the HHA's quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program. source_record.Deficiency Description: Care Planning, Coordination, Quality Of Care
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Care planning, coordination, quality of care
CFR(s): 484.60
Condition of participation: Care planning, coordination of services, and quality of care.

Patients are accepted for treatment on the reasonable expectation that an HHA can meet the patient's medical, nursing, rehabilitative, and social needs in his or her place of residence.  Each patient must receive an individualized written plan of care, including any revisions or additions. The individualized plan of care must specify the care and services necessary to meet the patient-specific needs as identified in the comprehensive assessment, including identification of the responsible discipline(s), and the measurable outcomes that the HHA anticipates will occur as a result of implementing and coordinating the plan of care.  The individualized plan of care must also specify the patient and caregiver education and training. Services must be furnished in accordance with accepted standards of practice.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interviews, and  review of facility documents, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure 1) all patients receive skilled services according to physician orders (G0572); and 2) that patients receive the prescribed visits for all disciplines involved, to meet the patient's needs (G0608). 

 

 

Cross Reference:

§484.60(a) Standard: Plan of care

§484.60(d)(4) Coordination of Care

Plan of care
CFR(s): 484.60(a)(1)
Each patient must receive the home health services that are written in an individualized plan of care that identifies patient-specific measurable outcomes and goals, and which is established, periodically reviewed, and signed by a doctor of medicine, osteopathy, or podiatry acting within the scope of his or her state license, certification, or registration. If a physician or allowed practitioner refers a patient under a plan of care that cannot be completed until after an evaluation visit, the physician or allowed practitioner is consulted to approve additions or modifications to the original plan.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interviews, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure all patients receive skilled services according to the established plan of care and physician orders. 

Findings include:

Facility policy titled, “Rights/Responsibilities” dated 06/2025, stated, “… Procedure: 1. The patient will be informed verbally and in writing during the initial evaluation visit, in advance of furnishing care to the patient, of the following: … L. … The organization shall ensure that the patient receives all services outlined in the plan of care. M. The establishment and revision of the plan of care, including the disciplines that will furnish the care and the frequency of visits as well as any changes in the care to be furnished.”

Facility policy titled, “Staffing and Scheduling” dated 03/2022, stated, “… Procedure: 1. The Clinical Care Coordinator (CCC) in conjunction with the Manager of Clinical Practice (MCP) will review the patient census and staffing levels on a daily basis and will make patient assignments … 4. Clinicians will communicate with the office to report any planned visits for the day that were not made, to report availability for visits the next day, and to receive admission assignment or changes for the next day’s schedule.” 

Facility policy titled, “Verification of Physician Orders” dated 03/2022, stated, “…NOTICES TO THE PHYSICIAN: 1. The office will notify the physician if the patient refuses service or treatment ordered and will document that refusal in the clinical record. 2. If fewer visits are provided during the week than ordered, the physician will be notified with documentation in the clinical record that the physician is aware of the missed visit unless the physician has authorized missed visits under specific circumstances (for example the plan of care indicates that the office may skip nursing visits on the day of physician visits or that home health aide visits may be skipped when the patient’s daughter is in the home to provide personal care) …”  

On 07/22/26 at 11:15 AM, a review of P1’s medical record, conducted in the presence of Staff (S)1 and S5, revealed the following: 

A physician’s "Referral" note dated 06/29/26 stated, “… Home Care Disciplines/Needs: Skilled Nursing evaluation for SOC [start of care] assessment for disease and medication management, comprehensive assessment, and education. Monitor and educate on signs and symptoms of infection, reporting abnormal finding to MD [medical doctor]. Assess and educate on fall precautions and home safety. Educate on emergency medical management and activation of EMS [Emergency Medical Services]. SN [Skilled Nurse] assess for other disciplines. Home care Diagnosis/Focus of Care: Ascites/pancreatic mass …” 

P1 was admitted on 06/30/26.  

P1's "Skilled Nursing Care Plan" revealed that P1 was ordered to receive SN visits once a week for 2 weeks from 06/30/26 to 07/11/26.         

P1’s “Patient Calendar” indicated that P1 received an initial SN visit completed by S14 on 06/30/26 at 12:15 PM, where S14 recommended a Physical therapy (PT) evaluation for the patient and obtained an order. 

An “Inconvenience Visit” note completed by S7 on 07/06/26 at 2:23 PM stated, “… Patient was leaving for Doctor appointment as nurse was arriving. Discipline discharge rescheduled for Wednesday. Patient still waiting for therapy eval visit …” Upon interview, S1 stated that an "inconvenience visit" note is documented when a clinician arrives for a scheduled visit, but the patient is not available for appointment.  

A review of P1's "Skilled Nursing Care Plan" revealed that P1 was ordered to receive SN visit, one visit per week for one week, from 07/06/26 to 07/11/26. S1 stated the additional SN visit order string was entered so the SN could reschedule the visit that was missed when P1 had a doctor's appointment. P1's medical record lacked evidence of a rescheduled SN visit or SN discipline discharge.  

P1's "Ancillary Services Care Plan" revealed that P1 was ordered to receive one PT visit every six days for six days from 06/30/26 to 07/05/26. P1's medical record lacked evidence of a PT evaluation during the week of 06/30/26 to 07/05/26.  

P1's "Ancillary Services Care Plan" revealed that P1 was ordered to receive one PT visit every six days, for six days, from 07/06/26 to 07/11/26. P1's medical record lacked evidence of a PT evaluation during the week of 07/06/26 to 07/11/26.  

On 07/22/26 at 11:58 AM, during an interview, S1 and S5 confirmed that P1 only received the initial SN visit on 06/30/26 and did not receive follow-up SN visits or an initial PT visit. S1 confirmed the medical record lacked evidence of communication with the physician regarding the delay in the PT evaluation. S1 and S5 confirmed that P1 was still an active patient, but the ordered SN and PT order strings had expired.  

At 2:21 PM, during a telephone interview, S7 stated that another SN performed the initial intake and assessment for P1. S7 stated, he/she was assigned as the case manager for P1. S7 stated, he/she went to P1’s home once for a visit, but P1 was leaving the home for an appointment, and was unable to conduct the SN visit as scheduled. When asked why P1 did not currently have any orders for nursing or therapy, S7 stated that he/she forgot about P1. S7 stated, he/she was supposed to transfer service from SN to PT for P1. S7 stated, he/she must have forgotten to reschedule a visit to go out to see P1. S7 stated that he/she would definitely call to schedule a visit to see P1 now that surveyors brought this to their attention.  

On 07/23/26 at 10:13 AM, during an interview, S10 stated, he/she was responsible for managing the PT, OT (Occupational Therapy), and SLP (Speech Language Pathologist) disciplines at the facility. When asked about the process for a PT evaluation, S10 stated, the SN puts in for an evaluation, and a case communication note is sent to the scheduler. S10 stated, he/she triages the evaluation requests and assigns them to a therapist based on acuity and need. S10 stated, he/she keeps a running tally of patients who are still pending an evaluation for therapy. S10 stated, even if a PT evaluation order expires, the patient still remains on the running tally list and is a part of their daily conversations. S10 stated, if the visit frequency order expired, then they would need to obtain a new order from the physician. S10 stated, if there was a delay in care, he/she would call the physician and document a note in the electronic medical record (EMR).  

At 10:49 AM, during a telephone interview, P1 stated that the SN came out once since their discharge from the hospital. P1 stated, he/she only received an admission visit from the SN and has had no other visits. P1 stated, the facility contacted him/her at night on 07/22/26 and scheduled visits with the RN and PT for 07/24/26. P1 stated that he/she talked about a PT eval with the SN during the admission visit but hadn’t heard anything more about it until he/she was contacted by the facility on 07/22/26 and was not sure what the facility was doing to help him/her. P1 stated, he/she was weak from dialysis and was preparing for chemotherapy, however, had not experienced any falls or adverse events since his/her admission visit. P1 stated, he/she did not attempt to contact the facility when they did not receive visits. P1 stated, he/she was so busy with dialysis and chemotherapy that they forgot about the visits from the facility.

At 1:37 PM, an interview was conducted with S3. S3 explained that the case manager assumes patient care after the admission is completed. S3 stated, the case manager should be managing all of the visits and overseeing all the other disciplines involved in the patient’s care. S3 stated P1’s case manager should have gone out to reassess P1 and/or communicated with PT regarding the missed PT evaluations. S3 further explained that if there was an issue, he/she should escalate to a nursing or PT leader.

Coordinate care delivery
CFR(s): 484.60(d)(4)
Coordinate care delivery to meet the patient's needs, and involve the patient, representative (if any), and caregiver(s), as appropriate, in the coordination of care activities.

This Element is not met as evidenced by:
Based on medical record review, staff interview, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to coordinate delivery of care to ensure that patients receive the prescribed visits for all disciplines involved, to meet the patient's needs. 

Findings include: 

Facility policy titled, “Staffing and Scheduling” dated 03/2022, stated, “… Procedure: 1. The Clinical Care Coordinator (CCC) in conjunction with the Manager of Clinical Practice (MCP) will review the patient census and staffing levels on a daily basis and will make patient assignments … 4. Clinicians will communicate with the office to report any planned visits for the day that were not made, to report availability for visits the next day, and to receive admission assignment or changes for the next day’s schedule.” 

A review of P1’s medical record conducted in the presence of Staff (S)1 and S5, revealed the following:  

A physician’s "Referral" note dated 06/29/26 stated, “… Home Care Disciplines/Needs: Skilled Nursing evaluation for SOC [start of care] assessment for disease and medication management, comprehensive assessment, and education. Monitor and educate on signs and symptoms of infection, reporting abnormal findings to MD [medical doctor]. Assess and educate on fall precautions and home safety. Educate on emergency medical management and activation of EMS [Emergency Medical Services]. SN [Skilled Nurse] assess for other disciplines ..."

P1's "Ancillary Services Care Plan" revealed that P1 was ordered to receive one PT visit every six days for six days from 06/30/26 to 07/05/26 for "evaluation and treat for HEP [home exercise program], transfer, and mobility training." P1's medical record lacked evidence of a PT evaluation during the week of 06/30/26 to 07/05/26. 

P1's "Ancillary Services Care Plan" revealed that another order was received for, one PT visit every six days, for six days, from 07/06/26 to 07/11/26, for “evaluation and treat for HEP, transfer, and mobility training." P1's medical record lacked evidence of a PT evaluation during the week of 07/06/26 - 07/11/26. 

On 07/22/26 at 11:58 PM, S1 and S5 confirmed that P1 did not receive an initial PT visit. S1 confirmed the medical record lacked evidence of communication with the physician regarding the delay in the PT evaluation. S1 and S5 confirmed that P1 is still an active patient, but his/her PT order strings have expired. 

On 07/23/26 at 9:47 AM, during an interview, S9 stated that patients are triaged by the manager and assigned to a clinician based on diagnosis, location of patient’s home, and availability of clinicians. S9 stated that they handle a high volume of patients and work to schedule them as best as possible. S9 stated that he/she meets with the therapy and nursing manager several times per day to discuss visit frequencies. According to S9, if a visit frequency order was approaching an expiration date, then he/she would alert the manager to obtain a new order. S9 stated that he/she would not be alerted to a missed visit after an order expired, thus would not have known about the patient. S9 stated that the manager would contact the patient’s physician to obtain a new order.  

At 10:13 AM, during an interview, S10 stated that they were responsible for managing the PT, OT (Occupational Therapy), and SLP (Speech Language Pathologist) disciplines at the facility. When asked about the process for a PT evaluation, S10 stated, the SN enters an evaluation in the electronic medical record (EMR), and a case communication note is sent to the scheduler. S10 stated, he/she keeps a running tally of patients who are still pending an evaluation for therapy. S10 stated, even if a PT evaluation order expires, the patient still remains on the running tally list and is a part of our daily conversations. S10 stated, if the visit frequency order expired, then he/she would need to obtain a new order from the physician. S10 stated, if there was a delay in care, he/she would call the physician and document a note in the EMR. Upon request, S10 was unable to provide documentation of the "running tally list" from June 30 until July 22, 2026 (first day of survey). 

At 1:37 PM, an interview was conducted with S3. S3 stated that the case manager assumes patient care after the admission is completed. S3 stated, the case manager should be managing all of the visits and overseeing all of the other disciplines involved in the patient’s care. S3 stated P1’s case manager should have gone out to reassess P1 and/or communicated with PT regarding the missed PT evaluations. S3 stated that if there was an issue, he/she should escalate it to a nursing or PT leader. When asked about the lack of documentation regarding the PT evaluation delay, S3 stated the CCC normally documents the communication in the chart. During the medical review, there was no documented evidence by the CCC concerning the delayed or missed visit.
