source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
This was a Federal Recertification survey conducted at Seabrook Home Health Agency on December 6, 7 & 8, 2023, to determine compliance with 42 CFR Part 484 - Conditions of Participation for Home Health Agencies.

Standard-level deficiencies were cited.

Services by skilled professionals
CFR(s): 484.75(a)
Standard: Provision of services by skilled professionals.  

Skilled professional services are authorized, delivered, and supervised only by health care professionals who meet the appropriate qualifications specified under §484.115 and who practice according to the HHA's policies and procedures.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, it was determined that the Home Health Agency failed to ensure the skilled professional services of a medical social worker, are provided directly or through written agreement, to patients who need the service.

Findings include:

On 12/6/23 at 10:37 AM, during the entrance conference, Staff 1 (S1), the Administrator, confirmed that the facility provides social work services to patients. On 12/7/23, during an interview with S2, the Director of Nursing, he/she explained that if patients needed social work services, they were referred to the social worker who works in the medical practice office, which is not a part of the home health agency. S2 stated that the patients would have to set up an appointment with the social worker and go to the medical office to see the social worker. S2 confirmed that the social worker is not an employee of the Home Health agency nor does the Home Health Agency have a contract with the social worker.

N.J.A.C. 8:42-9.1

source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
This was a Federal Recertification Survey and Federal COVID-19 Focused Infection Control Survey conducted May 19, 20, and 21, 2021. Seabrook Home Health Agency is not in compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart B requirements, for Home Health Agencies.

As a result of this survey, Condition and Standard level deficiencies were cited. 

The following Conditions of Participation (CoP) are out of compliance:

484.70 Infection Prevention and Control

484.75 Skilled Professional Services 

484.75 Compliance with Federal, State, Local Law

Infection prevention and control
CFR(s): 484.70
Condition of Participation: Infection prevention and control.

The HHA must maintain and document an infection control program which has as its goal the prevention and control of infections and communicable diseases.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, review of facility policies and procedures and nationally recognized guidelines, and staff interview, it was determined the facility failed to ensure its infection control program adheres to acceptable standards of practice.

Findings include:

1. The facility failed to ensure its infection control program adheres to acceptable standards of practice in limiting contamination to surfaces directly need for patient care. (Cross refer to Tag G-682)

2. The facility failed to ensure its infection control program includes methods for surveillance, identification, prevention, and investigation of communicable diseases. (Cross refer to Tag G-684)

3. The facility failed to ensure its infection control program educates staff on maintaining the recommended contact time for approved disinfectants. (Cross refer to Tag G-686)

Skilled professional services
CFR(s): 484.75
Condition of participation: Skilled professional services.

Skilled professional services include skilled nursing services, physical therapy, speech-language pathology services, and occupational therapy, as specified in §409.44 of this chapter, and physician or allowed practitioner and medical social work services as specified in §409.45 of this chapter. Skilled professionals who provide services to HHA patients directly or under arrangement must participate in the coordination of care.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, it was determined the Home Health Agency failed to ensure the skilled professional services of a medical social worker, are provided directly or through written agreement, to patients who need such services.

Findings include: 

1. The facility failed to ensure skilled professional services of a medical social worker are available to all patients. (Cross refer to Tag G-702)

2. The facility failed to ensure a designated Registered Nurse performs annual evaluations for the facility's Registered Nurses. (Cross refer to Tag G-704)

source_record.Deficiency Description: Compliance With Federal, State, Local Law
source_record.Statement of Deficiency Text (Part 1):
Compliance with Federal, State, Local Law
CFR(s): 484.100
Condition of participation: Compliance with Federal, State, and local laws and regulations related to the health and safety of patients.



The HHA and its staff must operate and furnish services in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations related to the health and safety of patients. If state or local law provides licensing of HHAs, the HHA must be licensed.

This Condition is not met as evidenced by:
Based on staff interview, review of facility documents, and review of Chapter 42 - Licensing Standards for Home Health Agencies, it was determined the facility failed to ensure a full-time Director of Nursing is appointed by the Governing Body.

Findings include:

Reference #1: Chapter 42 - Licensing Standards for Home Health Agencies 8:42-7.3(a) states, "The governing authority shall appoint a full-time Director of Nursing, who shall be available at all times. An alternate or alternates shall be designated in writing to act in the absence of the director."

1. On 5/19/21 at 10:05 AM, Staff #1 stated he/she was the Director of Nursing. 

2. On 5/19/21 at 1:20 PM, Staff #1 stated he/she was a Physical Therapist.

3. On 5/19/21 at 1:23 PM, Staff #1 and Staff #2 stated, "We do not have a Director of Nursing."

 

4. Review of the facility Governing Body minutes lacked evidence of a Director of Nursing or an Alternate Director of Nursing.

5. On 5/21/21 at 10:50 AM, a review of Staff #1's personnel file confirmed Staff #1 is a Physical Therapist.

6. The above finding was confirmed with Staff #2 on 5/21/21.

Infection Prevention
CFR(s): 484.70(a)
Standard: Infection Prevention.  

The HHA must follow accepted standards of practice, including the use of standard precautions, to prevent the transmission of infections and communicable diseases.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on observation in one (1) of four (4) home visits, staff interview, and review of CDC guidelines, it was determined the facility failed to ensure separation between clean and soiled equipment is maintained.

Findings include:

Reference: CDC 2007 Guideline for Isolation Precautions: Preventing Transmission of Infectious Agents in Healthcare Setting(http://www.cdc.gov/hicpac/pdf/isolation/Isolation2007.pdf) page 50 states, "During patient care, transmission of infectious organisms can be reduced by adhering to the principles of working from 'clean' to 'dirty', and confining or limiting contamination to surfaces that are directly needed for patient care."

1. On 5/21/21 at 11:00 AM, during a home visit for Patient #8, the following was observed:

a. After assessing the patient's oxygen level, Staff #9 placed the pulse oximeter directly next to clean equipment, without disinfecting it. 

b. After assessing the patient's blood pressure, Staff #9 placed the blood pressure cuff, without it being disinfected, directly next to clean patient care equipment.

2. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2.

B. Based on observation and staff interview, it was determined the home health agency failed to ensure COVID-19 screening questions are completed prior to visitors entering the facility.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility document titled, Screening Questions, States, "In the past 2 weeks have you been: Diagnosed with or exposed to an individual with COVID-19? ... In the past 2 days have you or anyone in your household experienced: Fever, chills, or body aches? ... Sore throat or coughing ... Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea? ... Sinus congestion, loss of sense of taste or smell? ..."

1. Upon arrival at the home health agency, through the Gatehouse, the following was noted:

a. On 5/19/21 at approximately 9:15 AM, the Security Guard did not ask the following screening questions prior to allowing entry to the facility:

i. In the past 2 weeks have you been: Diagnosed with or exposed to an individual with COVID-19?

ii. In the past 2 days have you or anyone in your household experienced: Fever, chills, or body aches? ... Sore throat or coughing ... Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea? ... Sinus congestion, loss of sense of taste or smell?

b. On 5/20/21 at approximately 9:15 AM, the Security Guard did not ask the following screening questions prior to allowing entry to the facility:

i. In the past 2 days have you or anyone in your household experienced: Fever, chills, or body aches? ... Sore throat or coughing ... Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea? ... Sinus congestion, loss of sense of taste or smell?

c. On 5/21/21 at approximately 9:15 AM, the Security Guard did not ask the following screening questions prior to allowing entry to the facility:

i. In the past 2 days have you or anyone in your household experienced: Fever, chills, or body aches? ... Sore throat or coughing ... Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea? ... Sinus congestion, loss of sense of taste or smell?

2. The above findings were confirmed by Staff #2.

C. Based on observation in three (3) of four (4) home visits, staff interview, and review of facility documents, it was determined the home health agency failed to ensure COVID-19 screening questions are completed prior to staff entering patient residences.

Findings include:

Reference: Facility document titled, Screening Questions, States, "In the past 2 weeks have you been: Diagnosed with or exposed to an individual with COVID-19? ... In the past 2 days have you or anyone in your household experienced: Fever, chills, or body aches? ... Sore throat or coughing ... Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea? ... Sinus congestion, loss of sense of taste or smell? ... Have you traveled outside of North America or been on a cruise ship in the past 14 days and not yet been cleared? ..."

1. On 5/19/21, prior to a home visit for Patient #5, the following was noted:

a. Staff #5 did not ask the patient the following screening questions:

i. In the past 2 weeks have you been: Diagnosed with or exposed to an individual with COVID-19? 

ii. In the past 2 days have you or anyone in your household experienced: Fever, chills, or body aches? ... Sore throat or coughing ... Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea? ... Sinus congestion, loss of sense of taste or smell?

iii. Have you traveled outside of North America or been on a cruise ship in the past 14 days and not yet been cleared? 

2. On 5/20/21, prior to a home visit for Patient #2, the following was noted:

a. Staff #10 did not ask the patient the following screening questions:

i. In the past 2 days have you or anyone in your household experienced: Fever, chills, or body aches? ... Sore throat or coughing ... Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea? ... Sinus congestion, loss of sense of taste or smell?

3. On 5/20/21, during a home visit for Patient #5, the following was noted:

a. Staff #8 did not ask the patient the following screening questions:

i. In the past 2 weeks have you been: Diagnosed with or exposed to an individual with COVID-19? 

ii. In the past 2 days have you or anyone in your household experienced: Fever, chills, or body aches? ... Sore throat or coughing ... Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea? ... Sinus congestion, loss of sense of taste or smell?

iii. Have you traveled outside of North America or been on a cruise ship in the past 14 days and not yet been cleared? 

4. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2.

Infection control
CFR(s): 484.70(b)(1)(2)
Standard: Control.  

The HHA must maintain a coordinated agency-wide program for the surveillance, identification, prevention, control, and investigation of infectious and communicable diseases that is an integral part of the HHA's quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) program. The infection control program must include:



(1) A method for identifying infectious and communicable disease problems; and



(2) A plan for the appropriate actions that are expected to result in improvement and disease prevention.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
Based on observation, staff interview, and review of facility documents, it was determined the facility failed to ensure the implementation of CDC guidelines to address prevention and control strategies for mitigating the spread of COVID-19. 

Findings include:

Infection control education
CFR(s): 484.70(c)
Standard: Education.  

The HHA must provide infection control education to staff, patients, and caregiver(s).

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on (2) of two (2) home visit observations for wound care management, staff interview, review of policy and procedure, and review of manufacturer's instructions (IFUs) for use of disinfectants, it was determined the facility failed to ensure staff are educated on maintaining recommended contact time for approved disinfectants.

Findings include:

 

Reference #1: Facility Policy Infection Prevention and Control Safe & Sanitary Environment states, "To maintain a safe and sanitary environment through cleaning and disinfection and / or sterilization of equipment ... .3. Non-critical items - (i.e., furniture, stethoscopes, ...) a. Clean items with a hospital grade disinfectant ... b. Must follow manufacture's instructions for use. ..."

Reference #2: Oxivir Tb manufacturer's instruction for use state, " ... Wipes 1. Apply undiluted .... 2. All surfaces must remain visibly wet for 1 minute for viruses and bacteria, 5 minutes for Hepatitis C and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. To kill E-Coli, P. vulgariiss, P. aeruginosa, S. aureus and Fungi use a 10 minute contact time. 

1. During a home visit, Staff #5, was observed using Oxivir Tb to disinfect equipment.

a. Upon interview, Staff #5 was unsure of the required contact time to kill viruses and bacteria. 

2. On 5/20/21 at 10:35 AM, Staff #4, an Infection Preventionist, stated the approved disinfectant for the Home Health Agency is Oxivir Tb wipes.

a. Staff #4 further stated the contact time was two (2) minutes.

3. During a home visit, Staff #9, was observed using Super Sani-Cloths to disinfect equipment.

4 Staff #4 confirmed the above findings.

B. Based on staff interview conducted between 5/19/21-5/21/21, it was determined the facility failed to ensure staff are aware of whom to direct any infection control questions.

Findings include:

1. On 5/19/21, Staff #1 and Staff #2 stated the Infection Preventionist is Staff #4.

2. Upon review of personnel files, it was confirmed that Staff #4 is the Infection Preventionist.

 

3. Upon interviews conducted between 5/19/21-5/21/21, Staff #5, Staff #8, Staff #9, and Staff #10, stated they direct all infection control questions to Staff #1, a Physical Therapist.

 4. Staff #2 confirmed Staff #1 is a Physical Therapist and staff direct all infection control questions to him/her.

Services by skilled professionals
CFR(s): 484.75(a)
Standard: Provision of services by skilled professionals.  

Skilled professional services are authorized, delivered, and supervised only by health care professionals who meet the appropriate qualifications specified under §484.115 and who practice according to the HHA's policies and procedures.

This Standard is not met as evidenced by:
A. Based on one of (1) of two (2) home visits for wound care observations, and review of facility policy and procedure, it was determined the facility failed to ensure their policy for handwashing is implemented. 

Findings include:

Reference #1: Facility Policy Hand Hygiene states, " ...5. Procedure technique for hand washing with soap and water: The CDC Guidelines for Hand Hygiene: when cleaning your hands with soap and water *wet hands wit clean running water *apply the amount of product recommended by the manufacturer to your hands, and rub your hands together vigorously for at least 20 seconds, covering all surfaces of the hands and fingers. *Rinse hands with clean water ... ."

1. A home care visit was conducted on 5/19/21 at 12:30 PM. Upon observation of the visit for Patient #5, Staff #5 missed six (6) of six (6) opportunities to wash his/her hands according to facility policy and CDC Guidelines.

a. Staff #5 turned on the faucet, applied soap to his/her hands, wet his/her hands and rubbed his/her hands together under running water for less than 20 seconds. 

2. Staff #5 confirmed he/she applied soap, wet his/her hands, and rubbed his/her hands together under running water for less than 20 seconds.

B. Based on staff interview, it was determined the facility failed to ensure skilled professional services of a medical social worker are provided directly or through written agreement to patients who need such services.

Findings include:

1. Upon interview, Staff #2 stated, "We do not have a social worker on our staff."

2. Staff #2 was unable to provide documented evidence of a written agreement to provide medical social work services.

3. The above findings were confirmed with Staff #2.
